waves.goal: Unblock and make safe: production browser grants, close ZDR/tenant leaks and ungated script, stop resource leaks and relaunches, ship the inline ScrapeOptions contract and file routing, plus S-sized reliability fixes. Includes phase 1 of F-t2-013 (takeover enforced in Quarry).

Reach table-stakes parity on both halves: the shared user+AI browser (free browsing, chat beside the page, co-browsing, planner on, trusted input, run trace) and the acquisition API (scoped robots-compliant crawl, job lifecycle, executable schedules, structured extraction, actions and screenshots), with budgets, profile encryption, redaction, org policy and capacity limits.

Governed depth: credential handoff, per-origin consent and approval UX, presence overlay, observation quality, durable sessions, downloads, monitors, document parsing, webhooks, decision audit, batch and discovery, metering, caching and screening.

Platform and leverage: procedures, result sets, packs, crawl planning, provider-API routing, engine planner v2, geo/egress tiers, remote and isolated backends, routines, research jobs, code mode, external MCP contract and extraction profiles.
Nice-to-have polish and long-tail bets, scheduled opportunistically or after an ADR.

adrNeeded.topic: Web policy of record and tighten-only claims (org-core in Control Plane vs capability-core in Model Plane)
adrNeeded.why: Several items need one owner for disabled/allowed/forced capability policy that reaches Quarry only as signed claims (no cross-plane DB access). The consolidators left the owner open; Space access must never widen it.

adrNeeded.topic: Secret custody across planes for browser credential use
adrNeeded.why: integration-corev2 holds secrets, Quarry would resolve and fill them, and the Model must only ever see opaque references. This touches plane ownership, audit and ZDR (no secret material in receipts or telemetry).

adrNeeded.topic: Shared human+agent sessions: grant binding, control lease and human-session navigation policy
adrNeeded.why: Free human browsing needs a broker-defined navigation policy that is not a single-host allowlist, and co-browsing binds a Model run to a user lease. Both change what a grant means and must keep "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects".

adrNeeded.topic: ZDR semantics for caches, monitors, schedules, durable crawl and telemetry
adrNeeded.why: Monitors, URL caches, schedules and durable crawls all store content or fingerprints; the team must decide per feature whether ZDR means hash-only, inline-only or refused, and publish it as the ZDR capability matrix.

adrNeeded.topic: Anti-bot posture: honest identity vs stealth, robots override, proxy escalation
adrNeeded.why: Consolidated items conflict (delete stealth code vs wire it under policy). Verevon contracts forbid challenge bypass; the ADR should confirm the honest posture and what policy-gated escalation is allowed.

adrNeeded.topic: Script execution model: evaluate, scrape actions and code-mode vs one governed action per call
adrNeeded.why: Code-mode REPL and generated extractors are model-written programs; they fit only if every binding call is still validated and executed by Quarry with grants, caps and no raw mutating script by default.

adrNeeded.topic: External agent exposure (MCP server) and its auth model
adrNeeded.why: docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG defers MCP exposure; an MCP front needs audience-bound OAuth, delegation to Quarry and integration-corev2, and a ZDR-aware tool-call log. Owner decision required.

adrNeeded.topic: Run trace envelope and sharing: Model Plane run trace vs Application Plane projections and Space grants
adrNeeded.why: A canonical cross-plane trace envelope and live projections must not let a Space member see more than the owning plane ACL allows.

adrNeeded.topic: Automation owner for follow-ups and routines (Application Plane vs Model Plane routines)
adrNeeded.why: Completion-triggered follow-ups and scheduled/heartbeat agent runs need one owner and per-fire browser grants for unattended runs.

adrNeeded.topic: Browser execution substrate: shared Chromium pool vs per-session containers/VMs, remote providers and user-browser extension
adrNeeded.why: Isolation level, processor approval for remote providers and the egress-containment proof decide which backends may run agent sessions; the user-browser extension gives up containment and ZDR evidence.

items.title: Production BrowserBroker grants and delegated bearer forwarding (unblocks every browser path)
items.summary: Give the Model Plane BrowserBroker a durable (Postgres) grant store and a production issue/acquire/revoke path. The gateway obtains a user-session grant when it creates a browser session, sends grant_id on POST /v1/agent/runs, forwards x-browser-authorization and x-inference-authorization, and derives child grants for AI runs instead of the interim session:{id} string. Add one end-to-end contract test (gateway -> model-gateway -> execution-core -> quarry-edge) in prod mode that fails on 401/403.
items.whyItMatters: Prod-mode Quarry requires a broker grant on every agent run and refuses to boot without a validator (SRC), yet nothing outside tests issues grants and the broker store is in memory (SRC). Until this lands, the in-app browser, the AI step/loop, co-browsing, the credential bridge, budgets carried in the grant and per-origin consent cannot work in production (INF, high confidence, not runtime-tested). This is the single highest-leverage item in the audit.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (hardened page hosting, iab-028/029)
others: Aside (Chromium fork, so the same pattern is inferred, INF)
Aside (AA005/AB050 signed-challenge short-lived CDP tokens; AA007 routed, cancellable command bridge)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources record it (Codex); treated as common because Aside is a Chromium fork (INF). For Verevon the matching mechanism is a trusted issuer deciding host authority, which is a prerequisite rather than a reference feature. || 2 of 3 sources (Aside, Codex); table-stakes || hosted browser sessions as an API: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl), differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex's main process intercepts every guest attach (will-attach-webview): it forces partition, session and preload, deletes allowpopups, disablewebsecurity and nodeintegration, and pre-registers a route token so only known tabs can attach; the renderer cannot widen any of it. The Verevon analogue already exists on the Quarry side: host authority is broker-owned (Quarry overwrites a client's allowed_domains with the grant's canonical list at acquisition and revalidates every step). What is missing is the issuer. || Merged items add: The browser control endpoint refuses unauthenticated clients. A client fetches a challenge, signs it with an installation key and receives a short-lived bearer token. Browser-level commands go over a bridge routed per (account, profile, mode) with register/runCommand/cancelCommand and stale-connection rejection. Verevon analogue: a broker-issued grant checked by quarry-edge on every /step. || Session {ttl 30-3600 s, activityTtl 10-3600 s, profile, location, zdr}; a reaper closes a session on either timer and settles billing; live-view and replay URLs; /scrape/:id/interact lazily creates a session by replaying the scrape's URL, waits and actions. Verevon should copy the two timers and the bridge but not the free-form code execution.

items.approach: Model Plane BrowserBroker (Go grant.go): durable store plus issue/acquire/revoke with two grant kinds, user-session and run (org and owner scoped, canonical host list up to 32, TTL, ZDR flag; ZDR grants stay ephemeral). Gateway browser.rs: obtain the grant at session create, forward both bearers and derive child grants for AI runs. Quarry stays validator and executor and changes only in tests. The lease TTL reaper moves to F-t2-006 and the scrape-to-session bridge to F-t2-035. || Source detail: [R-t2-08-01] Model Plane BrowserBroker (Go, grant.go): add a durable store (Postgres) and an issue endpoint for a user-session grant kind (org and owner scoped, ZDR flag, TTL, bounded canonical domain list). Gateway browser.rs create_session calls the issuer with the delegated browser-audience bearer, passes grant_id on /v1/agent/runs and forwards x-browser-authorization to Quarry and model-gateway. start_ai_run (browser.rs:1235) mints a child grant from the session grant instead of the 'session:{id}' string; sensitive actions keep single-use child grants. Add an integration test that runs the gateway against Quarry in prod mode. Quarry is unchanged except for tests; the Model proposes, Quarry validates and executes. || [R-t2-09-01] Model Plane: BrowserBroker gets a durable store (Postgres) and AcquireGrant/Revoke called by model-gateway at run start, grant scoped per run and per domain set with TTL; ZDR runs keep grants ephemeral. Frontend gateway (verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs): replace the interim string with the broker grant and forward x-browser-authorization plus x-inference-authorization. Add a contract test across gateway, model-gateway, execution-core and quarry-edge that fails on 401/403. || [R-t2-01-05] Model Plane: durable BrowserGrant record plus an issuance API (canonical host allowlist up to 32, org/owner scoped, short TTL, persisted instead of in-memory) that the gateway calls on session create; model-gateway already validates a VerifiedBrowserBearer. Frontend gateway browser.rs: obtain the grant, send x-browser-authorization and pass the real grant id in start_ai_run. Ingestion Plane quarry-edge: enforce ttl_s with a reaper and add an activity TTL, excluding sessions awaiting approval; add POST /v1/scrape/:id/session (needs the scrape_id from R-t2-01-01) that creates an agent run seeded with the scrape URL and render hints. Do not add arbitrary code execution: keep one governed action per call with receipts so 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' holds.

items.risks: Grant scope creep: keep the canonical bounded host list (max 32) and single-use sensitive child grants. Restart semantics for in-flight sessions. Issuing grants for user sessions must not become a way around the model-initiated cross-domain HITL gate. || A grant scope that is too broad would widen ACLs: keep grants per run and per domain set, never per user globally. The gateway never obtains a grant: create_session posts to Quarry /v1/agent/runs with no grant_id (browser.rs:483-506), which prod Quarry rejects with 403 (agent_routes.rs:1377-1381, main.rs:182-200), and start_ai_run sends the string session:{id} (browser.rs:1235) with data-plane, inference, execution and session bearers but no x-browser-authorization, which model-gateway's VerifiedBrowserBearer extractor requires (browser_run.rs:304, auth.rs:427-437). Missing: a durable store, an issuance path reachable by the gateway, browser-bearer plumbing, run-grant derivation and a prod-mode cross-service test.

verevon.constraints: Model Plane owns grant issuance; Quarry only validates (per step) and executes, and domains must come from the broker, never from the client (exact-equality check at agent_routes.rs:314-339). The gateway must not mint authority itself: issuance must go through the broker with the user's delegated browser-audience bearer so org and owner derive from verified claims (server.go AcquireGrant uses the verified principal). The broker is gRPC-only on :9095, so the gateway needs a gRPC client or an HTTP issue endpoint on model-gateway. ZDR: model-gateway already refuses durable browser runs under ZDR, ZDR user sessions that go straight to Quarry still need a grant, and ZDR grants must not be persisted. Grants stay org and owner scoped and a Space must never widen them. A 15-minute broker TTL caps session length until a renewal path exists (see F-t2-011).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Placement is right (Model Plane broker plus gateway plumbing, Quarry unchanged). Corrections: (1) the gateway already forwards x-inference-authorization and the data-plane, execution and session bearers on start_ai_run; only x-browser-authorization is missing, so add a browser-bearer parameter to proxy_model_json_with_delegations and mint it through the already-declared BrowserBroker audience. (2) Prefer a model-gateway HTTP endpoint that wraps AcquireGrant, since it already holds the broker client and verified bearer, over teaching the gateway gRPC. (3) create_session, which goes directly to Quarry, needs the grant as well as start_ai_run. (4) Sensitive child grants exist, but deriving a narrower run grant from a session grant is a new broker API. (5) Slice it: issuance, gateway wiring and a prod-mode contract test on the existing in-memory store first, then the Postgres store.
verevon.effortNote: Touches the Go broker (store, migration, issue path), model-gateway, gateway proxy plumbing and a prod-mode contract test across four services in three planes; M only holds for the first slice on the in-memory store.
verevon.verdictReason: Verified in code: prod Quarry requires a grant on every run and step, nothing in production issues one, the broker store is in memory and the gateway lacks the browser bearer, so every browser path is blocked in prod mode; the plane placement is correct and only details need adjusting.

reference.corrections: 1) Prevalence/class: the cluster C-t2-08-001 mechanism (will-attach-webview rewrite) is Electron-specific; Aside being a Chromium fork does not imply it has the same attach hardening, so the 'treated as common because Aside is a Chromium fork (INF)' line must go. items.title: Gate Evaluate and raw script actions behind a grant capability and one-shot approval
items.summary: Make AgentAction::Evaluate (and raw CSS selector paths) read-only by default: run in an isolated world with a non-mutating document proxy, JSON-only arguments and credential-field masking. Mutating script requires an explicit grant capability plus a one-shot approval, and the planner does not see Evaluate unless the grant allows it.
items.whyItMatters: Quarry otherwise fails closed, but Evaluate has no approval branch, so any risky action (submit, delete, read a sensitive field) can be expressed as script and bypass the risk-classified approval model. The executor must be sound regardless of which caller reaches /step.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (CA018, CI114: three gates plus a domain allowlist for raw CDP; read-only isolated-world evaluate wrapper that cannot mutate the DOM)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources (Codex); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Evaluate runs in Page.createIsolatedWorld against a frozen read-only proxy of document (no setters, no event dispatch), JSON-serializable args only, credential inputs masked. Raw CDP only when the grant has rawCdp=true and the method is on an allowlist; request/cookie params that carry URLs are authorised.

verevonToday.gap: The Verevon UI facade refuses raw script, but Quarry accepts Evaluate{script} on normal runs: sensitive_approval_for_action handles dialog, upload and download only, and Evaluate appears in agent_routes.rs just as a label mapping (SRC, this audit). The execution-core LLM planner schema does not emit evaluate today (llm_planner.rs:53-65), so current exposure is via direct /step callers, compiled procedures and any future code-mode.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser, quarry-runtime, quarry-edge): isolated-world read-only evaluate by default; add 'evaluate_mutating' as a sensitive action needing a grant capability and one-shot approval (the same mechanism as upload/download). Model Plane: hide the action from the planner unless the grant allows it. Audit existing callers of Evaluate first.
items.risks: Some extraction flows may rely on mutating evaluate; audit callers before tightening.

verevon.exactGap: Quarry's /step path has no gate for AgentAction::Evaluate: sensitive_approval_for_action covers only respond_dialog, upload_ref and download_ref and falls through to Ok(None) at agent_routes.rs:280, the broker's sensitive-action allowlist has no evaluate (grant.go:30-36), and ChromiumoxideDriver::evaluate runs page.evaluate in the main world (chromiumoxide.rs:3003-3017). The Model Plane half is already done: execution-core's browser.act schema (agent.rs:3479-3512) and the planner ACTION_SCHEMA (llm_planner.rs:53-65) never offer evaluate and the gateway sanitize_action denies it (browser.rs:3751), so exposure is direct service callers of /step plus Quarry's own unwired ModelPlanePlanner prompt, which advertises evaluate and pdf (mp_client.rs:383). The /step path also discards the script's return value (observation.rs:542-543), so a read-only isolated-world evaluate has no consumer there; ActionRuntime::Evaluate (action_runtime.rs:380-392) has no production caller.
reuse: sensitive_approval_for_action + validate_sensitive_approval + the used_sensitive_approval_grants one-shot set (agent_routes.rs:144-310, 2276-2290)
GrantValidation::authorizes_exact_sensitive_action single-action approval rule (grant_validator.rs:98-109)
BrowserBroker allowedSensitiveActions and scoped approval grants (grant.go:30-36)
gateway sanitize_action's typed browser_action_denied response as the denial shape (browser.rs:3751)
require_ephemeral_evidence_action, which already excludes Evaluate in the ephemeral tier (agent_routes.rs:1153-1176)
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects: the gate must live in quarry-edge/quarry-runtime, not only in the planner schema, and denials must be typed Quarry errors. Grant authority belongs to the Model Plane BrowserBroker (Go), so a new sensitive action class needs a broker allowlist and proto alignment change as well as the Quarry change; approvals are strict single-action one-shot grants and sensitive actions require a parent run grant (agent_routes.rs fails with Forbidden without one). UI-driven runs use an interim 'session:{id}' grant_id today (browser.rs:1235), so the gate must fail closed when no real parent grant exists. Practical severity is defense-in-depth (internal service callers only), not an open user-facing hole.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reduce to a default-deny gate on /step: add 'evaluate' to the broker's allowedSensitiveActions and to sensitive_approval_for_action (bind the script hash into the approval), or simply reject AgentAction::Evaluate on agent runs until a real consumer exists. Drop the 'hide it from the planner unless the grant allows it' sub-task (already true on the Model Plane side) and remove evaluate/pdf from the unwired mp_client planner prompt. Build the isolated-world read-only evaluator (Page.createIsolatedWorld, JSON-only args, size/time/result caps) only together with F-t2-023, because scrape-time actions are where a return value is consumed.
verevon.effortNote: S holds for the deny-by-default plus sensitive-approval gate; the isolated-world read-only evaluator is a separate M and should move under F-t2-023.
verevon.verdictReason: The Quarry-side gap is real and cheap to close, but half the approach is already shipped on the Model Plane and the read-only-evaluate design is mis-scoped to a path that discards results.

reference.corrections: Codex does not put playwright.evaluate behind a capability or an approval. It makes evaluate structurally safe instead: an isolated world, read-only wrappers, masked credential fields, a block on import(), and capped results. The consent and approval gates apply only to raw CDP: the full_cdp_access_enabled preference (default false), the enterprise requirement, and a per-origin consent that a preference can auto-answer. 'Domain allowlist' means CDP protocol domains (22 usable), together with a per-method denylist and parameter checks, not website domains. 'grant rawCdp=true' and 'one-shot approval' are Verevon proposals, not Codex mechanisms. 'Unique' holds only for the read-only evaluate. Gating raw script actions is also in Firecrawl, where Safe Mode strips executeJavascript and rejects interactive sessions, and Aside isolates the REPL guest from the raw CDP client, although Aside's page.evaluate can mutate the page subject only to permission rules.
caveats: Codex raw CDP is default-off and gated by preference and enterprise requirement; the source record says the docs mark it development-only (doc not re-opened)
Codex evidence comes from a beautified copy of the shipped browser plugin bundle (SRC of a shipped artifact)

items.title: Close the gateway search-cache ZDR and tenant hole, then publish a per-feature ZDR capability matrix
items.summary: Phase 1 (S): the gateway /search cache key (search.rs:218-226) holds query, limit, include_answer and filters but no org or user scope, and store() runs without any ZDR check (SRC, re-read in this T2 pass); results are kept 4 h and served stale when Quarry fails. Add the authorized org id to the key, skip lookup and store for ZDR requests and ZDR orgs, and route every cache through one shared should_cache() admission rule (never cache ZDR, credentialed, action or profile requests). Phase 2 (M): declare a per-feature ZDR capability matrix with explicit refusal codes, and keep a content-free ZDR run tombstone with a default retention janitor.
items.whyItMatters: Two architecture rules are broken at once: ZDR must propagate, and no tenant may see another tenant's data. If smart-router results include org-scoped corpus or Data Plane vector hits (INF from the router design, not traced end to end), this is a cross-tenant disclosure, not only a ZDR gap. Phase 1 is a one-file fix.

others: Firecrawl (requests row that redacts URL and options under ZDR while keeping outcome, timing and cost plus a scheduled deletion and a TTL access row; explicit per-feature ZDR honour/refuse/degrade list with team modes disabled|allowed|forced)

It returns false for opt-out, ZDR, any credential-bearing input (custom headers, actions, profile or session), custom screenshot sizes and partial or low-fidelity engine output (for example truncated or unparsed PDFs). || Merged items add: Static table feature to {honours, degrades with warning, refuses with status} checked during validation; a team-level mode overrides request flags and responses warn about skipped features. Run rows requests(id, org, kind, origin, outcome, started_at, ended_at, cost, zdr, target or redaction marker) with result blobs keyed by id and a job_access(id, org, expires_at) row checked on retrieval; a janitor deletes rows and blobs past plan retention.

items.approach: Frontend Plane gateway first (search.rs, cache.rs): scope the key by the authorized org id and bypass the cache for ZDR (crate::zdr::request_zdr / org_zdr_enabled already exist). Then a shared should_cache() used by gateway and Quarry caches, a ZDR matrix published from quarry-core, and a tombstone row in quarry-control. || Source detail: [R-t2-04-02] Frontend Plane gateway first (S): move CacheAdmission into a shared module (for example next to zdr.rs), call it from search_web before lookup and store, and include the authorized org id in the key. Extend the scrape-preview key with the request variant (formats, headers, actions) or refuse to cache when any are present. Ingestion Plane second: add one should_cache() in quarry-core, used by quarry-edge, the search router and the future URL cache, excluding ZDR, credentialed inputs, actions/profiles and PII-redacted raw bodies. Add a test that a ZDR org's search leaves no gateway cache entry. || [R-t2-07-05] Ingestion Plane owns the matrix (JSON in quarry-runtime/contracts, generated from or tested against route attributes) and the tombstone row in quarry-control; the janitor default and retention days come from Control Plane plan settings. Frontend Plane gateway: skip the search-web cache for ZDR and key it by org when not ZDR (ship this first, it is a small fix), and read the matrix for UI gating. Fix the ZDR scrape to return inline content.
dependencies: Authorized org id from AuthenticatedUser / upstream::authorized_org_id
Control Plane plan and retention settings
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane gateway (phase 1); Ingestion Plane (matrix, tombstone)
items.risks: Lower hit rate for repeated queries across orgs, which is acceptable. The search path should fail closed on a ZDR lookup failure, as zdr.rs already does. || The matrix can drift from code, so generate or test it. The tombstone must be reviewed against the ZDR contract (metadata only). Do not weaken Verevon's existing stricter ZDR refusals when aligning with the reference.

verevon.exactGap: Phase 1 is fully open: gateway search_web builds its cache key from query, limit, include_answer and filters only (search.rs:209-226), stores with no ZDR check (search.rs:285), keeps entries fresh 4 h and for 24 h with a stale fallback (cache.rs:20-25), and search.rs contains no zdr reference. This is a confirmed cross-tenant path, not only a ZDR gap: the Quarry /v1/search it fronts uses org-scoped private-corpus providers (TantivyLocalIndex, org_id taken from the JWT, search_routes.rs:503-517, local_index.rs module docs) and include_answer feeds an org-scoped answer pipeline, while the gateway key carries no org. Quarry itself is correct (org-keyed SearchCache with no cache read or write under ZDR, search_routes.rs:762-780), a ZDR-aware CacheAdmission already exists privately for the scrape preview (knowledge/quarry.rs:213-280, though its key at line 104 is still target-only), and per-endpoint ZDR refusals exist (routes.rs:563-588); there is no declared per-feature ZDR matrix and no ZDR run tombstone.

verevon.constraints: Two architecture rules are broken today (ZDR must propagate; no tenant may read another tenant's data), and the gateway is the one boundary the ownership matrix says must hold neither. Frontend Plane gateway owns the fix for phase 1; Quarry (Ingestion) owns the ZDR matrix and any tombstone, and a tombstone must be metadata-only and reviewed against the ZDR contract. Fail closed on ZDR lookup failure as zdr.rs already does. Do not weaken Verevon's stricter existing ZDR refusals when aligning with Firecrawl.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep phase 1 as written but make it one change: move the private CacheAdmission to a shared module, call it in search_web before lookup and before store, add the authorized org id to the key, and also key the scrape-preview cache by org and request variant (formats, headers, actions). Phase 2: generate or test the ZDR matrix from route attributes in quarry-core rather than hand-maintaining JSON, and do the tombstone only after the contract review.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: phase 1 is S (one gateway file plus a test), phase 2 is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Gap confirmed in code and upgraded from inference to source-verified cross-tenant exposure; the approach is already right and phase 1 is the highest-value quick fix in this batch.

reference.corrections: shouldCache is an inline boolean inside sendDocumentToIndex, not a separate pure function. It excludes any custom headers, actions or profile (hasCustomRequestContext), not only credential-bearing input, and there is no 'session' term. It also excludes results from low-fidelity engines (TLS client, fetch, except the sitemap team), Exchange, the index itself, and page-aware or marker PDF parsers. Firecrawl's deletion is a per-request ZDR cleanup queue plus access-row expiry (24 h default, crawlTtlHours for crawls), not a janitor that runs on plan retention. Plan-based retention comes from Apify and is DOC-only. 'Run history with retention 3 of 4' is overcounted: the Aside record cited (065) shows local session storage and no retention policy. Aside's only evidenced retention is a 15-minute purge of ephemeral sessions in a terminal state. Several ZDR refusals (agent/extract, scrape-status) trigger when the team flag forces ZDR, not on the per-request flag.

items.title: ZDR-safe telemetry: span sampler, late-ZDR registry, log filter and safe/sensitive log fields in Quarry and the gateway
items.summary: In quarry-edge telemetry.rs add an OpenTelemetry sampler and span processor that drop spans for zdr=true requests (plus a bounded registry for runs that turn ZDR after a span started) and a tracing Layer that keeps events emitted inside ZDR spans out of the JSON fmt layer. Add one small shared helper (Rust crate plus the quarryotel Go package) whose log API forces two maps, safe (ids, enum outcomes, durations, counts) and sensitive (url, query, error text, selectors), with export sinks stripping sensitive by default. Propagate ZDR posture on internal hops as a header and NATS header, and add an operator kill switch that disables all exporters.
items.whyItMatters: Architecture rule: Zero-Data-Retention must propagate. It currently stops at the observability boundary: telemetry.rs always installs a JSON fmt layer and an OTLP layer with no ZDR awareness, and change_routes.rs logs the source URL inside the very branch that says ZDR is active. A leak in logs or OTLP is invisible to users and would breach ZDR contracts, and it blocks safe SIEM export and support diagnostics.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (ZeroDataRetentionSampler returning NOT_RECORD, bounded late-ZDR trace registry, ZDR log-metadata filter, X-Zero-Data-Retention header honoured by helper services)
others: Codex in-app browser (every lifecycle log entry is {safe, sensitive} with stable prefixes; BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_AMBIENT_NETWORK kill switch)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources for ZDR-aware telemetry and 2 of 4 for privacy-classified logs; differentiator (Firecrawl-only for the sampler and registry)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rust: a custom opentelemetry Sampler returning Drop when parent context or attributes carry zdr=true; a bounded LRU of trace ids flagged ZDR after start, checked in a SpanProcessor on_end so descendants and in-flight spans are dropped; a tracing Layer that suppresses events inside zdr=true spans; a log helper with signature log(safe: Map, sensitive: Map) where sinks drop or hash sensitive and ZDR requests always drop it. Posture travels as an internal header (for example x-verevon-zdr) and a NATS header so receivers skip request-correlated logs. A QUARRY_DISABLE_AMBIENT_TELEMETRY switch turns off every exporter.

verevonToday.gap: ZDR is carried on requests, events (emit_for_zdr) and artifact paths, but telemetry.rs installs the JSON fmt layer and the OTLP layer unconditionally with no ZDR sampler or filter (no "zdr" string in telemetry.rs or quarryotel). Logging relies on a documented convention of low-cardinality fields; about 295 tracing macro calls exist across the crates and several carry error text or URLs (change_routes.rs:635 logs url inside the ZDR-active branch at debug level; default filter is info, so it only surfaces with RUST_LOG=debug). No cross-plane ZDR telemetry header exists.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane first. quarry-edge/src/telemetry.rs: add ZdrSampler, a ZDR trace registry plus SpanProcessor, and a ZDR-aware tracing Layer; create a shared obs module (Rust) mirrored in pkg/quarryotel (Go) exposing safe/sensitive helpers; add the ZDR propagation header to the cross-plane contracts folder next to cross-plane-token-requests.json. Then Model Plane (execution-core, model-gateway) and the Frontend Plane gateway adopt the helper. Keep content-free counters (outcome, duration, driver) outside the ZDR filter so ZDR tenants still have operational metrics. Add a test that a ZDR scrape and a ZDR browser step export zero spans and no log line containing the URL, and a lint that url/query fields are only logged as sensitive.
dependencies: Shared ZDR header name in the cross-plane contracts
Item F-t2-029 (span vocabulary builds on this sampler)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (adopted by Model Plane and Frontend Plane gateway)
items.risks: Partial adoption gives false confidence, so enforce with a test or lint. Over-suppression hides incidents for ZDR tenants; keep counters outside the filter. The retrofit touches many call sites.

verevon.exactGap: quarry-edge/src/telemetry.rs:25-64 installs a JSON fmt layer and an optional OTLP layer under one global EnvFilter with no ZDR awareness, and pkg/quarryotel/quarryotel.go:39-93 uses ParentBased(AlwaysSample); neither has a sampler, span processor, late-ZDR registry or safe/sensitive field helper. Practically the live exposure is JSON log events (for example change_routes.rs:632-637 logs source_url inside the ZDR-active branch at debug), because the edge only creates tower-http TraceLayer spans (routes.rs:303, debug level by tower-http default, INF) and a grep of the Go services finds quarryotel.Init but no tracer.Start or otelhttp, so almost no spans are exported at the default info filter. ZDR posture already propagates through the token floor plus body flag (auth.rs:121-139), emit_for_zdr (events.rs:137) and the NATS envelope zdr key (natsx/publisher.go:57); the only off-switch is leaving OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset.
reuse: ZdrMode and Claims::effective_zdr_mode as the single posture source inside Quarry (auth.rs:121-139)
emit_for_zdr and the natsx Publisher body-key suppression as the existing event-side ZDR guard
page_renderer.rs ZDR-gated debug log without URL fields as the field-discipline pattern
mp-telemetry (Model Plane) and gateway zdr.rs request_zdr/org_zdr_enabled as the plane-local adoption points
verevon.constraints: ZDR must propagate, but each plane owns its own telemetry init (quarry-edge telemetry.rs, mp-telemetry, gateway); a shared helper is a documented contract, not shared code across planes. Quarry derives posture from the verified token floor OR the body flag, and deliberately ignores a service principal zdr claim (auth.rs:104-120), so a new ZDR header or NATS header would be a third carrier that Quarry does not read (the gateway sets x-zdr at upstream.rs:1788 but Quarry reads token plus body). Content-free counters must stay available to ZDR tenants, yet the metrics crates in quarry-edge are inert (telemetry.rs:6-18), so there is no recorder to keep outside the filter yet.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder. Phase 1 (S): remove the url field at change_routes.rs:635, sweep the 250-plus tracing call sites for url, query and error text fields (reqwest errors embed URLs), and add a test or lint; carry effective ZDR in a task-local or span field so a per-layer filter on the JSON fmt layer can drop sensitive fields. Phase 2: sampler, late-ZDR registry and the shared safe/sensitive helper only once spans exist (F-t2-029), since today almost no spans are produced. Do not add a ZDR header or NATS header; reuse token claim plus body flag plus envelope zdr key, and add an explicit exporter disable flag if an operator kill switch is wanted.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall but split: Phase 1 is S and can ship alone; the sampler/registry/helper crates are M and depend on span instrumentation landing first.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real and architecture-relevant, but the item centres on a span sampler and registry for spans that are barely created at the default filter; the live exposure is log fields (one known debug leak) and the posture carriers already exist, so the fix list and the proposed header need rewording.

reference.corrections: Prevalence conflates two different things: ZDR-aware telemetry is Firecrawl-only (Codex's BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_AMBIENT_NETWORK is a sandbox/eval kill switch for gates, Sentry and analytics, not a ZDR mechanism), and safe/sensitive classified log fields are Codex-only (Firecrawl filters whole log lines by a zeroDataRetention flag). Codex's safe/sensitive split is observed at call sites and in the logger shape, but how sinks treat 'sensitive' (drop/hash/upload) was not found, so 'sinks drop or hash sensitive' is a Verevon proposal (INF), not Codex behaviour. items.title: One strict ScrapeOptions contract: formats[], inline return (the ZDR path) and main-content controls
items.summary: Define ScrapeOptions once in quarry-core (deny_unknown_fields, validate() with field paths, schemars JSON Schema for OpenAPI and the Model Plane tool schema) with formats[] (markdown, html, rawHtml, links, metadata now; json, screenshot and pdf via F-t2-019 and F-t2-023), inline return up to a size cap with artifact-ref fallback, timeout, maxAge, onlyMainContent, include/exclude selectors, extractor choice (readability, clean_full, raw) with a full-HTML fallback, headers and location. Return effectiveOptions and a scrape_id, add GET /v1/scrape/:id (not for ZDR), and embed the struct in crawl, batch, search hydration and schedules.
items.whyItMatters: Every agent web_fetch pays two calls today (scrape, then GET artifact), and a ZDR scrape returns no content because outputs exist only as artifact refs that are never written under ZDR (SRC). Inline return is the natural ZDR path. One validated contract is what lets the Model propose options and Quarry reject bad ones with field-level 400s. docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:22 claims format parity is done; the code contradicts it (no formats field on ScrapeRequest).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-001 inline scrape under a per-team semaphore; fc-002 shared zod strictObject)
others: Apify web-fetch / Website Content Crawler (DOC; same format list, run as an Actor)
Firecrawl (api-surface-038/039 for the formats union and Document metadata; api-surface-047 for attributes/images formats)
Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-086 streaming Rust transform, api-surface-040 options)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: inline scrape: 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify), table-stakes; shared strict options contract: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl), differentiator; scrape-by-id: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl) || 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); common for scrape APIs (INF: a per-call output-format choice is the standard shape; Apify, Codex and Aside are not scrape-API shaped) || 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify); table-stakes for scrape APIs (the two browser sources have no scrape API)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Validate the request against a single options schema; take a per-org concurrency permit with a bounded wait (2/3 of the request timeout); run the pipeline in-process; build the Document with only the requested formats (markdown default, rawHtml only on request) and put scrapeId, status code, final URL and queue time in metadata; cross-field rules (waitFor <= timeout/2, action count and total wait caps, one screenshot format); write a per-job access row {scrapeId, orgId, expiresAt} so GET /scrape/:id can re-serve the result, and write none for ZDR. Caution from the reference: it silently defaults skipTlsVerification to true, so echo effective options and never flip a security default silently. || Merged items add: Request: formats: Array<string | {type, ...opts}>; strings are lifted to {type} and validated against a tagged union so each format has its own option schema (serde #[serde(tag="type")] in Rust). Pipeline: fetch once, then run only requested transformers in a fixed order (clean html -> markdown -> links/images/attributes -> LLM formats -> redaction -> diff). Response: one Document with optional fields per format plus metadata {statusCode, sourceURL, url, contentType, cacheState, cachedAt, proxyUsed, creditsUsed, warnings[]}. Exclusive formats (raw base64) are rejected when combined with others. || Parse with a DOM or streaming rewriter (lol_html, kuchikiki). Remove head/meta/style/script/noscript. If includeTags is given keep only matching subtrees; remove excludeTags. If onlyMainContent, remove a fixed list of about 42 chrome selectors unless the node contains a force-include region. Resolve lazy images (data-src, data-srcset, largest srcset) against the base href. Choice of extractor, falling back to full cleaned HTML when readability yields too little text. Firecrawl's optional LLM clean pass is unsupported under ZDR and not worth copying.

items.title: Reap abandoned agent runs (idle and absolute TTL), cap concurrent runs, and make the fleet console real
items.summary: Add a background sweeper in quarry-edge that closes agent runs past their lease ttl_s (derived from max_runtime_s) or an idle timeout, releases the browser lease, emits a run.expired event and denies further use of the run's grant. Add per-org and global caps on concurrent runs and a tab-count warning, move the in-process run registry to durable state for multi-instance operation (non-ZDR only), and proxy /v1/fleets through the gateway so the fleet console shows real runs.
items.whyItMatters: Abandoned user or AI sessions currently hold a Chromium context and a live browser grant indefinitely. That is a resource leak on a shared browser host and a security exposure (a usable grant with no user present), and it grows with every agent run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (global run semaphore, sub-agent cap, tab warning, idle sweeper)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; differentiator (only Aside has code evidence, and for a local single-user product)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A global semaphore (200 concurrent runs) gates run start; a per-run counter limits active sub-agents (8); the agent is warned at 5 open tabs; each tab carries a last-activity timestamp and a sweeper closes agent tabs and sessions past an idle TTL (15 minutes) and emits an event; ephemeral sessions are retained for a fixed 15-minute window.

verevonToday.gap: ttl_s is computed from max_runtime_s (default 120) and stored on the lease at agent_routes.rs:1446-1502 but nothing sweeps it; a grep of agent_routes.rs finds no idle or reaper logic. Only max_steps is enforced on the step path. Runs live in an in-process HashMap (new_runs) so they cannot be shared across edge instances. The lease pool holds 2 sessions on one shared Chromium. The fleet console is a stub with placeholder live views fetching /v1/fleets that the gateway does not proxy. Step budgets and fleet budget aggregation do exist.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-edge) with a small Frontend change. Add a tokio interval task that scans the run registry and closes runs past ttl_s or an idle threshold, where last_activity is refreshed on every step, on an attached frame/WS viewer, and on user takeover; on expiry release the lease, close the CDP BrowserContext, emit run.expired and mark the grant used-up (ask Model Plane BrowserBroker to revoke). Add org-scoped and global run caps at run start returning a typed 429/RESOURCE_BUSY with retry-after. Persist run records through the existing AgentRunCheckpoint path to Postgres for non-ZDR runs so the registry works across edge instances; ZDR runs stay in memory and simply expire. Frontend: proxy /v1/fleets in the gateway and replace placeholder tiles. Implementing the ttl check also enforces max_runtime_s for agent runs.
dependencies: F-t2-025 per-org caps share the admission code
items.risks: Reaping a run a user is still watching or co-browsing; refresh activity on viewer and takeover activity and never auto-close takeover tabs. Run-registry persistence must respect ZDR.

verevon.exactGap: No reaper exists: start_run computes ttl_s from max_runtime_s (agent_routes.rs:1446,1502) but nothing reads it, enforce_step_budget checks max_steps only (agent_routes.rs:446-451), and runs leave the in-process registry only through close_run (agent_routes.rs:3623-3626); the 15-minute BrowserBroker grant TTL (server.go:22) bounds use of an abandoned run but not the leaked Chromium pages. There is also no cap on agent runs at all: the agent ChromiumoxideDriver is one shared browser whose acquire never blocks (chromiumoxide.rs:1914-1942, main.rs:1284-1288), and the RuntimeLeasePool(2)/(4) at main.rs:323,337 only gates scrape-render fetches through BrowserDriverAdapter (browser_driver.rs:133-142). The fleet console is routed at /agents/fleets/:fleetId (App.tsx:216) but fetches /v1/fleets directly, the gateway has no /v1/fleets route, its Pause button PATCHes a route the edge does not register (fleet_routes.rs:216-222), and member tiles are placeholder text (FleetRunConsole.tsx:120-130,155-163).
reuse: the run registry and close_run release/receipt/checkpoint path (agent_routes.rs:3600-3650) as the single close routine the sweeper must call
AgentRunCheckpoint, checkpoint_for_entry and the resume_checkpoint flow for non-ZDR resume (agent_routes.rs:453-471, 1425-1445)
Quarry-v2 janitor and the sandbox-manager process Sweeper as sweeper patterns (sandbox-manager is Go in the Model Plane, so copy the pattern, do not import)
existing control_mode (agent_control / human_takeover) as the takeover signal for last_activity
FleetRegistry and fleet_router already in the edge (fleet_routes.rs:216-222) for the console backend
verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane owns the browser lifecycle; Model Plane owns grants, so revocation is a BrowserBroker call and not Quarry's to make (the 15-minute grant TTL already bounds exposure, making explicit revocation optional). A RunEntry owns a process-local Chromium session, so the live registry cannot be shared across edge instances: durable state only enables resume through the existing checkpoint path, and cross-instance steps need sticky routing by run id. ZDR runs are never checkpointed and must stay in memory and simply expire. Reaping must not close a run a user is watching or has taken over.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep the sweeper and add org-scoped and global run caps at start_run with a typed 429 plus retry-after; cap accounting must also cover UI-created browser sessions, since the SPA has no beforeunload or sendBeacon close so a closed tab or crash leaves the session open. Replace 'move the in-process run registry to durable state for multi-instance operation' with 'checkpoint for resume and use run-id affinity routing'. Treat grant revocation as optional. Fix the fleet console as its own S: gateway proxy for /v1/fleets plus a PATCH/cancel route in the edge, or hide the route until then.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for sweeper plus caps; the fleet console proxy plus cancel route is a separate S.
verevon.verdictReason: The leak and missing caps are real and confirmed; the multi-instance registry idea does not fit a process-local browser, the 2-slot pool evidence applies to scrape rendering, and the grant TTL already narrows the security half.

reference.corrections: Aside's sweeper (flushIdleTabs) closes agent-owned tabs only for sessions whose status is idle, interrupted or aborted and whose session updatedAt is older than closeAfterIdleMinutes. It skips sessions with live activity and uses the session timestamp, not a per-tab last-activity timestamp. It does not reap running runs or delete sessions, and no event emission was seen. Ephemeral sessions in a terminal state are purged after 15 minutes. Aside has no absolute run TTL. A separate in-memory idle TTL of 10 minutes (DEFAULT_IDLE_TTL_MS) unloads agent session objects. The 5-tab warning is a text line added to the tool output. Prevalence is understated: Firecrawl hosted browser sessions have both an absolute ttl (default 600 s, max 3600) and an activityTtl (default 300 s), enforced by the closed Hangar service. Firecrawl is the better reference for 'idle and absolute TTL' in a multi-tenant server. No reference evidence supports a 'fleet console'.

items.title: Stop viewport-triggered browser relaunches: per-page emulation, a small Chromium process pool and page hygiene
items.summary: Apply the viewport per page or context with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride instead of closing and relaunching the single shared Chromium whenever a lease's viewport differs (None vs Some counts as different). Then replace the one process with a pool of K Chromium processes with maxOpenPages, retire-after-N-pages and a page semaphore, add a /health probe that really opens a page, and size the lease pool from config instead of the hard-coded 2. In the same page-attach path add Page.setWebLifecycleState(active) and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true) and a fixed per-lease viewport so coordinates and screenshots are deterministic.
items.whyItMatters: ensure_browser closes the browser and clears every session's pages, egress receipts, dialogs and telemetry when the viewport changes, so two concurrent in-app browser or agent sessions with different viewport options can destroy each other's live sessions. The in-app browser and AI runs need predictable capacity and crash containment; pages that check focus or visibility (menus, chat widgets, video) also behave unpredictably without focus emulation.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify Crawlee BrowserPool (apify-platform-058, DOC); Aside for page hygiene (aside-agent-control-architecture-029, SRC)
others: Firecrawl Playwright service: health probe that really opens a page plus a page semaphore (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-008, SRC)
Codex: background-throttling exemption only while driven or captured (codexbrowser-automation-and-safety-129, SRC)
Aside: 1440x900 stable viewport floor (aside-browser-product-085, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Pool lifecycle: 2 of 4 sources (apify, firecrawl), table-stakes. Page hygiene: 2 of 4 (aside, codex), differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Pool of N browser processes; each tracks open pages and pages served. New contexts go to the least-loaded process below maxOpenPages; after retireAfter pages a process stops taking work and closes when idle; pre/post launch and page hooks run in a fixed order; /health opens about:blank in a fresh context with a deadline. Per page on attach: Page.enable, DOM.enable, Network.enable, Page.setWebLifecycleState('active'), Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true), Target.setAutoAttach(flatten). Rust shape: Vec<BrowserSlot{proc, open, served, retiring}> behind a Mutex plus a tokio Semaphore for pages.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane, quarry-browser: replace the single `browser` plus `active_viewport` fields with Vec<BrowserSlot>. Apply BrowserLease.viewport per page via Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (this also gives R-t2-03-05 its mobile/locale hooks). Assign each session to a slot with affinity so the per-session pinned egress proxy, devtools collectors, receipts and dialog maps move into per-slot or per-session state rather than driver-global maps; keep --disable-quic when the pinned proxy is on. Read pool size, maxOpenPages and retireAfter from config, add a health probe that opens a page with a deadline, and add the two hygiene CDP calls in the page-attach path. Gateway and SPA need no change. Acceptance test: two concurrent leases with different viewports, neither loses its page.
items.risks: More processes raise memory pressure; driver-global state maps (egress receipts, dialogs, telemetry) must be re-keyed per session or slot without breaking receipt ordering; keep per-session proxy binding intact when a session moves between processes.

items.title: Enforce cost and runtime budgets in the Quarry executor, meter browser time, and clamp crawls to the remaining entitlement
items.summary: The run contract carries max_cost_usd and max_runtime_s, but only max_steps is enforced on the /step path, defaults are unbounded and browser minutes are not metered (SRC). Quarry, as the executor, reserves on run start, charges per step and per browser-second, stops gracefully at the cap with a typed BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and clamps crawl/batch page limits and requests per minute to the remaining entitlement. Model Plane cost-core passes the remaining budget inside the grant and reconciles; org default caps arrive via the policy claims of F-t2-022.
items.whyItMatters: Agents with live browsers and paid providers can run up unbounded cost. docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:50-53 says max_cost_usd is enforced, but the HTTP step path does not enforce it (doc/code divergence, SRC). Apify (charge within cap, DOC) and Firecrawl (reserve then settle, SRC) both enforce in the executor.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (reserve then settle exactly once under a row lock with a reconciliation sweep for browser sessions; request-scoped CostTracking that throws CostLimitExceededError)
others: Apify (per-run cost display and caps, DOC)
Apify (executor-side charge limit), with Firecrawl's reserve-then-settle for time-billed browser sessions
Firecrawl (limit clamped to remaining credits at kickoff, depth cap, per-crawl concurrency/delay, sharded usage counters, crawl TTL)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources; common || 2 of 4 sources; differentiator || 2 of 4 sources (both crawl platforms); table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: On session create: check entitlement, reserve a concurrency slot and estimated cost. On stop: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE the session row, compute duration-based cost (separate rates for human, AI-driven and ZDR use) and mark it settled; a periodic sweep settles sessions whose stop was missed. Per step: add action and LLM cost to a run-scoped accumulator and fail the step with BUDGET_EXCEEDED when it passes max_cost_usd. || Merged items add: Caller sets a max total charge per run. Before each billable step the executor calls charge(event, count), which returns how many units are still chargeable within the cap; when the cap is reached it finishes the current step, persists partial results and ends with a budget-exhausted status. items.title: Route PDFs, Office files and images to the right parser in /v1/scrape (Content-Type plus magic bytes)
items.summary: After any driver returns bytes, sniff Content-Type and then the first bytes (%PDF-, a zip containing [Content_Types].xml, OLE compound file, PNG/JPEG/WebP). If the body is not HTML, hand the already-fetched bytes to the matching parser in quarry-transform (pdf.rs, docx.rs, images.rs) instead of running charset decoding and readability over binary data, and record the detected kind in output metadata. Express it as a typed Replan::IsFile when the planner work in R-t2-03-06 lands.
items.whyItMatters: PDFs and Office files linked from sites are a common knowledge-base input. Today a PDF URL goes through readability and produces garbage markdown that users notice immediately, even though a PDF text extractor already exists.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl specialtyScrapeCheck (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-017, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (firecrawl), unique; table-stakes for a Firecrawl-class scraper
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: kind = sniff(content_type) or sniff_magic(first 512 bytes): %PDF-, PK zip with [Content_Types].xml, OLE compound file, PNG/JPEG/WebP. If kind is not html, raise AddFeature(pdf|document|image) carrying the already-downloaded bytes as prefetch so the parser needs no refetch. Record kind in output metadata.

items.title: Turn on the LLM browser planner by default, with budgets, a browsing procedure prompt and connector-first routing
items.summary: Replace the QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM env gate with an org-policy flag so the planner in execution-core is the default AI browser loop, with per-run step, time and token budgets. Add a versioned browsing procedure to the planner prompt (observe, act, re-observe; escalation ladder AX ref -> semantic locator -> set-of-marks -> coordinates; stop rules) and a routing step that prefers Integration Plane provider actions or Quarry search/scrape before opening a browser, unless the user asked for the browser.
items.whyItMatters: This is the AI-browser feature users actually see; without an enabled planner the in-app browser has no real agent. A procedure prompt raises task success at near-zero cost, and connector-first routing is cheaper, more reliable and honours provider OAuth scopes.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (FE098 hosted interact loop: capped interactive snapshot, one tool, step caps and guardrails) for the loop; Aside for the procedure prompt; Codex for connector-first routing
others: Aside AA035 harness versioning

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Loop 2 of 3 (common); procedure prompt 2 of 3 (table-stakes); connector-first 1 of 3 (unique to Codex)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Loop: interactive snapshot (capped around 40k chars) plus URL goes to the LLM with one tool; execute; return a snapshot diff; stop on done, step cap or budget; guardrails reject commands outside the allowed set. Prompt: observe -> act -> re-observe to confirm, escalation ladder, no URL-guessing loops, trust one authoritative on-page signal, periodic progress updates. Routing: if a linked resource has a connector, call it; use search for public lookups; open the browser only on explicit intent or connector failure.

verevonToday.gap: A durable loop with pause/resume/stop exists, but LlmPlanner::from_env returns None unless QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM is 1/true/yes (SRC, read in this audit; compose does not set it per baseline), so the default is a deterministic planner. The planner schema offers only navigate/click/type/scroll/wait/extract/done and the system prompt is one short paragraph about ref targeting with no verify, escalation or stop rules (SRC). Connector-first routing between provider actions, Quarry search and the browser is unverified.

items.approach: Model Plane execution-core: flip the default behind an org-policy flag, enforce per-run step/time/token budgets, add the versioned procedure prompt and widen the planner schema to Quarry verbs it cannot reach today (press, select, back, get_content), keeping the existing risk gates and ZDR checks. Add a routing policy (connector -> Quarry search/scrape -> browser) recorded in run receipts that honours explicit user intent. Frontend: one 'Do this in the browser' entry point. Evaluate prompt changes against Quarry step receipts.
items.risks: Runaway cost: budgets are mandatory before default-on. Over-long prompts: keep rules short and test-driven. Eager routing can ignore an explicit request to use the browser.

verevon.exactGap: A durable LLM-planned loop exists (execution-core llm_planner.rs and browser_agent.rs with pause/resume/stop, max_steps, max_runtime_s, forwarded max_cost_usd and HITL risk gates), but LlmPlanner::from_env returns None unless QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM is 1/true/yes (llm_planner.rs:130-148) and nothing under apps/Model Plane sets it, so the deterministic planner runs by default; users already have a flag-free LLM-proposed loop through the SPA's suggest-action path (model-gateway http_routes.rs:2023-2100, browser-loop.ts:1-30). The durable planner's ActionType is goto/click/type/extract/observe/scroll/wait only (browser_agent.rs:91-99) with a one-paragraph prompt (llm_planner.rs:236-241) and a fixed 512-token cap per call, so press, select and back (present in Quarry's wire actions, quarry_agent.rs:125-175) are unreachable, there is no per-run token budget, and no connector-first routing exists.

items.title: Let users browse freely: a human-session policy plus an omnibox that routes free text to Verevon search
items.summary: Add a human-browsing session mode distinct from agent runs: an idle-timeout lease (reset by user input and frame activity) instead of max_steps 12 and 120 s, and a broker-defined navigation policy that is not a single-host list, so omnibox entries and link clicks under takeover work. Agent-initiated cross-domain navigation keeps the existing cross_domain_navigation HITL gate, and Quarry's egress/SSRF policy stays on. Add hard reload and make reload retry a failed URL. Rewire browser-omnibox.ts so URL-like input navigates and free text opens Verevon search (Quarry /v1/search results, or Ask into chat), with suggestions from the gateway's existing search autocomplete and local web history.
items.whyItMatters: A browser locked to its first host for 120 s is not a browser, and today free text in the address bar becomes a google.com URL that the domain lock then rejects. This is the largest day-one usability gap for people, and it is the part of 'a built-in browser users and AI both use' that users touch first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (navigation commands iab-037; omnibox suggestion service iab-036)
others: Aside (omnibox reuses the browser engine plus an AI mode with attached tabs, aside-browser-product-011)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Navigation controls: 1 of 3 recorded (Codex), table-stakes because Aside is Chromium (INF). Omnibox suggestions: 2 of 3, common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Commands navigateBack, navigateForward, reload and hardReload (ignore cache); the preload captures mouse buttons 3 and 4; reload from an error page retries the original URL. The suggestion service is token based: start(query) streams matches {contents, description, destinationURL, acceptToken, deleteToken}; accept(token) navigates and records; deleteMatch removes a history entry. For Verevon: a gateway suggest call that merges local history, search autocomplete and URL heuristics, and non-URL input goes to Verevon search rather than google.com.

verevonToday.gap: Back, forward and reload ship, but the user cannot leave the first host or browse past 120 s. Because Quarry's governed mode makes the broker the only source of host authority, the allowlist cannot be extended by the gateway or by Quarry alone; a broker-defined policy mode (or a versioned grant re-issue that Quarry validates) is needed. The omnibox has no suggestions and its search fallback cannot work.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (Quarry): add a human session kind on /v1/agent/runs (or a dedicated session route) with an idle reaper, per-navigation timeline rows tagged source=user, and unchanged egress policy. Model Plane BrowserBroker: add a human-browse grant kind (open public web minus a broker/org denylist, audited, bounded) that Quarry validates in place of the exact domain-list equality; Quarry keeps rejecting agent-initiated cross-domain navigation without HITL approval, and Quarry-owned control mode decides whether an action is human or agent. Frontend gateway/omnibox: hard reload, error-page retry, suggest endpoint combining web-history.ts, the search domain autocomplete and URL heuristics; free text opens Quarry /v1/search results in the tab or sends to chat. Share the idle/absolute TTL machinery with R-t2-03-08 instead of building it twice.
dependencies: Gateway search cache gets org/user key and ZDR gating before it feeds suggestions (baseline gap 9)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (Quarry) with Model Plane broker and Frontend Plane omnibox
items.risks: SSRF and egress abuse (keep private-IP blocks and per-navigation audit), unbounded host growth, cost of long-lived Chromium leases (idle reaping), unforgeable user-versus-agent origin of a navigation. Under ZDR no history or suggestions are stored.

verevon.exactGap: The chrome already ships back, forward, soft reload (navigate to the session URL), new tab and a human-takeover control mode (BrowserChrome.tsx:1143-1215, browser.rs:263-300 and 690-790), but every user session is created with allowed_domains = first host, max_steps 12 and max_runtime_s 120 (browser.rs:483-490), and Quarry applies the same step budget and domain list to human steps (agent_routes.rs:446-451, 2258-2300). In governed mode the broker list must be non-empty, canonical, at most 32 hosts and equal to the live run's list on every step (quarry-browser lib.rs:55-77, agent_routes.rs:314-339) and broker grants expire after 15 minutes (server.go:22), so open-web human browsing needs a broker policy kind, not a gateway change. The omnibox turns free text into a google.com URL (browser-omnibox.ts:14-15), has no suggestions, and web-history.ts is a search-home card store, not omnibox history.

items.title: Chat beside the browser: a dockable browser panel bound to the chat run
items.summary: Promote BrowserChrome from the dashboard Crawl composer to a dockable panel inside the chat view (right, bottom, maximised, hidden), bound to the chat run's Quarry session, reusing frame streaming, takeover, approvals and the timeline drawer. Add a floating composer over the page and a 'new chat per tab or keep the chat' rule. The chat live-run panel becomes a compact mode of the same component instead of a separate read-only viewer.
items.whyItMatters: Both reference browsers converge on chat and page side by side. It is where the user watches, takes over and talks to the agent about the visible page in one view; Verevon has the pieces (frames in chat runs, takeover, approvals) but not the surface.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 3 sources (Codex, Aside); table-stakes for a chat-plus-browser product.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex hosts the browser as right, bottom, detached or hidden, chosen by a command with a layout-stepping command, and a floating composer posts into the active chat. Aside calls sidePanel.setOptions per tabId with a sessionId, resolves the target session when a tab activates, offers a new-session|keep-session setting, and injects a 'you are a sidecar to this page' framing block on the first tab mention.

verevonToday.gap: The interactive browser lives only in the dashboard Crawl composer with no standalone route; the chat panel cannot steer the browser or ask about the visible page in the same view.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: extract BrowserChrome into a layout-agnostic panel component, add dock state (right, bottom, maximised, hidden) persisted per user, bind it to the chat run's Quarry session via the gateway browser domain, and add the new-chat-or-keep-chat rule. Page context reaches the Model Plane only through governed attachments (R-t2-08-05); no direct DOM access from the SPA.
items.risks: Layout complexity on small screens; frame bandwidth when docked next to streaming chat.

items.title: Co-browsing: the agent works in the user's visible session in agent-flagged tabs, with takeover enforced inside Quarry
items.summary: Phase 1 (S, land in W1): make quarry-edge /step reject agent steps while control_mode is human_takeover (typed USER_TOOK_OVER, monotonic control epoch) and record the initiator (user or agent) in step receipts. Phase 2: an attach mode so a Model Plane run binds to the user's Quarry session through a session-bound child grant and works in a new agent-flagged tab that appears without stealing focus, with Reveal, Take over and Give back. Phase 3: deliverable and handoff tab marks so finished pages stay open for the user.
items.whyItMatters: Co-browsing is table-stakes in both browser references (Codex and Aside) and is the core of a browser that users and AI share. Today the AI run drives a separate hidden lease that inherits only profile_id and start_url (SRC). T2 re-read the code: takeover is enforced only in the Frontend gateway (browser.rs:705-723 and 2071-2090), and the Quarry /step admission path in agent_routes.rs never consults control_mode (SRC). A Model Plane run that calls Quarry directly is therefore not stopped by a human takeover. This corrects the strength claim (C-t2-08-017) that takeover is authoritative in Quarry.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (claimTab with fail-closed mention resolution, typed user_took_over, interrupt hooks, requestManualHandoff, markTab handoff|deliverable)
others: Aside (AB062 'controlling this tab / Take over' strip; AA030/AA031 owned vs borrowed tab rows with orphan reconciliation)
Codex in-app browser (iab-068, hidden agent tabs)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 3 sources (Aside, Codex); table-stakes || 1 of 3 sources (Codex); unique as a co-browsing model.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Session control_mode {agent|human}; 'Take over' flips it and cancels in-flight steps; every agent step checks control_mode and returns USER_TOOK_OVER. Claim: a mention token {browserId, tabId, title, url} is validated against live state, a control lease is taken and released (not closed) at end of turn. session_tabs(ownership owned|borrowed, mark) lets turn end close owned unmarked tabs and keep deliverable/handoff ones; an idle sweeper reconciles orphans. || Merged items add: Each agent tab gets a hidden webview host (about:blank until the snapshot URL is known); open-browser-tab is sent with active:false; presentation state decides whether the hidden host stays mounted, and the tab strip shows it without focus change. For Verevon: the AI loop attaches to the user's visible Quarry run (same lease, own tab) and Quarry's control-mode arbitration decides who may act.

Model Plane execution-core browser_agent gains attach_session_id and maps USER_TOOK_OVER to a suspended run. Frontend BrowserChrome: agent badge, Ask AI on this tab, Reveal / Take over / Give back. The Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects. || Source detail: [R-t2-09-03] Ingestion Plane (quarry-edge, quarry-runtime): enforce control_mode and a control epoch in /step, add initiator to step receipts, add request_handoff with reason, then a lease-holder field on the session with a transfer API and tab marks. Model Plane: browser_run accepts an existing session/tab id with a session-scoped grant, and maps USER_TOOK_OVER to a suspended run. Frontend (BrowserChrome.tsx): 'Ask AI on this tab', take over / give back, show marked tabs after the run. || [R-t2-08-03] Model Plane: add an attach mode to execution-core browser_agent (attach_session_id instead of client.start_run at browser_agent.rs:669); BrowserBroker issues a run grant bound to that session id, not a free string. Quarry: tab ownership flag opened_by agent|user in the tab list and timeline, agent steps allowed only on agent-flagged tabs (or the active tab when control_mode is agent), existing 409-during-takeover rule kept. Frontend: agent badge on tabs, new agent tab opens without focus, Reveal and Take over buttons, shared timeline. Keep the plane rule that Quarry executes or rejects every proposed action.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (control lease, tabs) + Model Plane (attach mode) + Frontend Plane (tab UI)
items.risks: Races between an in-flight step and takeover (hence the epoch); the agent must inherit only the session's grant and never widen the user's ACL; ZDR sessions stay non-persistent; tab leaks without an idle sweeper. || Concurrency between human and agent inside one session; step and cost budgets versus the idle policy of item 02; grant binding to exactly one session; cross-domain navigation by the agent stays behind HITL.

A Model Plane run never attaches: execution-core start_run (browser_agent.rs:674) leases its own session with only profile_id, start_url and an interim grant string (browser.rs:1235), and the SPA shows the agent session through a read-only BrowserChrome embed (ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx:608), with no agent badge, reveal, give-back-with-state or deliverable/handoff marks.

browser-broker Grant.SessionKey, ParentGrantID and CreateScopedSensitiveApproval (grant.go:44-130) for a session-bound child grant

Gateway takeover pre-checks (browser.rs:704-723, 2065-2075) kept as UX-level early rejection
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: enforcement has to move into Quarry /step, with the gateway check kept as UX only. Ownership blocks attach today: caller_owns_browser_run (agent_routes.rs:474-482) requires claims.actor_id() to equal the run actor, execution-core calls Quarry with an org-scoped service token (browser:execute, quarry_agent.rs:34,556), and Claims has no on-behalf-of field (auth.rs:62-91), so a Model Plane run is answered 404 on a user-owned session; attach needs a delegation design (Auth Core claim or session-bound child grant) that never widens the user ACL or Space authority. Production browser grant issuance is unbuilt (gateway sends the interim session:{id} string, browser.rs:1222-1236; no non-test AcquireGrant caller found in Model Plane), a prerequisite shared with F-t2-001. ZDR sessions stay non-persistent (control timeline writes are skipped under ZDR, agent_routes.rs:493-495).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Derive the initiator inside Quarry from the verified principal (service principal means agent, user token means human) rather than trusting the gateway body field. Phase 1 (S, ship alone): /step rejects agent-principal steps while control_mode is HumanTakeover with a typed USER_TOOK_OVER, a monotonic control epoch is stamped on control events and receipts, and initiator is added to StepReceipt and tab operations. Phase 2 (attach, agent-flagged tabs) needs an explicit delegated-authority design first, because the ownership check rejects service principals; schedule it after grant issuance (F-t2-001) and treat it as L to XL.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in letter, but Phase 1 is S and Phase 2 carries an Auth Core / Control Plane delegation dependency, so Phase 2 may exceed L.
verevon.verdictReason: Gap confirmed in code (enforcement only in the gateway, no initiator, no attach), but Phase 2 as written ignores that Quarry rejects non-owner service principals, and Phase 1 should be split out as an immediate small fix with initiator derived from the principal.

items.title: Surface one canonical agent run trace in the UI: typed events, receipts, live view, correlation envelope
items.summary: Define a versioned TraceEvent envelope owned by the Model Plane ({schema_version, event_id, run_id, occurred_at, producer_seq, correlation{org_id, actor_id, turn_id, request_id, origin}, agent{id, role, parent_id}, type, payload}); have Quarry publish browser-session, step-receipt, egress-decision and artifact events in the same envelope on NATS (persisted unless ZDR), served as GET trace with a cursor plus an SSE tail by from_seq. Gateway proxies the Quarry receipts, egress-receipts, procedure and live-view routes it does not proxy today and the SPA renders one run timeline in place of the FleetRunConsole placeholder; fix the run-start grant/bearer wiring first. Quarry edge adopts x-request-id through a tower layer and an origin enum on runs, and the devtools route gains level/substring filters with a read-only browser.console model tool.
items.whyItMatters: This is what users watch while the agent browses. Without it, "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects" is invisible, approvals lack context and support cannot follow one run across gateway, Model Plane, Quarry and audit. It blocks the vision of a browser shared by humans and AI, and most server-side pieces already exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (versioned run-trace envelope with producerSequence, parent agent, typed events, artifact snapshot versions and structured errors; x-request-id reused as idempotency key)
others: Codex in-app browser and automation (toolSurface/tab metadata on every result, size-capped activity, async browser notifications appended to the next result, tab.dev.logs typed pull tool with levels/filter/limit)
Apify (meta.origin enum on runs, run log with size cap and secret redaction)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Run trace 2 of 4 sources (differentiator); correlation id and origin 3 of 4 (table-stakes); agent-readable console logs 2 of 4 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Model Plane and Quarry emit TraceEvent onto NATS; non-ZDR events are persisted; GET /runs/{id}/trace serves a cursor and an SSE tail by from_seq; artifacts are referenced by snapshot id; each step response carries surface_meta {surface, tab list, sanitized url} plus drained async notifications (popups, dialogs, downloads). Edge middleware reads x-request-id (or generates it), puts it in the span and response header and forwards it on every internal call. Console pull: a bounded per-tab ring buffer exposed as GET .../console?levels=warn,error&filter=substr&limit=N.

verevonToday.gap: Quarry already exposes receipts, egress-receipts, procedure compile and replay-check, live-view, tabs, devtools and a typed agent-event SSE (agent_routes.rs:3662-3716), but the gateway proxies only the browser-session timeline and devtools, and a grep of the SPA finds no use of egress-receipts or procedure routes, so none of that is visible. The AI-run start likely fails on grant/bearer wiring (INF from the baseline, high; unconfirmed here). No envelope with a producer sequence spans Model Plane and Quarry, FleetRunConsole is a stub, quarry-edge mints its own request_id per handler (RequestKind::new()) and has no x-request-id intake (quarry-control echoes it, and a grep finds no x-request-id handling in the gateway source), no run origin enum exists, and devtools events are paged only by after_sequence and limit with no filters and no model-facing pull tool.

items.approach: Model Plane owns the run-trace contract (it owns runs and sessions): add TraceEvent to the Model Plane protos and publish from execution-core. Ingestion Plane: publish browser-session, receipt and egress events in the same envelope (reuse the existing NATS bus, PostgresEventHistory and ?from_seq replay), add a tower layer for x-request-id and an origin field on runs, and add levels/filter params to the devtools route. Application Plane projects the stream for realtime. Frontend Plane gateway proxies the missing Quarry routes and the SPA renders a single run timeline (replace FleetRunConsole, which calls an unrouted /v1/fleets). Model Plane execution-core adds a read-only browser.console tool that goes through the grant-checked run. ZDR runs stay live-only: no trace persistence.
dependencies: Item F-t2-004 for ZDR-safe trace and log handling
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (trace contract); Ingestion Plane and Frontend Plane deliver their halves
items.risks: Event volume and cross-plane ordering. Console text and page content can carry prompt injection or secrets, so apply the same redaction and untrusted-content labelling as observations. Never use the request id as an authorization or tenancy key; cap its length and charset.
