items.title: Actionability checks and trusted input for every ref-targeted action, then rich input actions
items.summary: Change Quarry's ref-targeted click/type path from element.click() via Runtime.callFunctionOn to: scroll into view, wait for attached/visible/enabled/stable (poll content quads over two frames), hit-test the centre via DOM.getNodeForLocation including cross-process iframe hops, then dispatch trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent/KeyEvent. Return typed errors (covered by <tag>, not_visible, disabled) and keep element.click() only as an explicit fallback. Follow-up phase: press with modifiers, drag, select_text and paste with a per-session virtual clipboard.
items.whyItMatters: Every AI click passes through this executor. Untrusted synthetic clicks silently no-op on sites that ignore them or sit behind overlays; honest 'covered by cookie banner' errors let the model recover. Flaky agents are noticed immediately.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (CA056/CI115: hit-testing across nested and cross-process iframes returning hittable|covered(hitTag)|unpositioned; key synthesis bound to an input target)
others: Aside AA022 (waitForReady attached|visible|enabled|stable with 32 ms stability sampling)
Codex clipboard shim and action set for the rich-input follow-up (1 of 3, DOC-backed)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Actionability 2 of 3 sources (table-stakes); rich input 1 of 3 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded; poll getContentQuads until stable over two frames; compute the centre; DOM.getNodeForLocation per frame hop with coordinate transforms; check the hit node is the target or a descendant, else error 'covered by <tag>'; then Input.dispatchMouseEvent moved/pressed/released and dispatchKeyEvent with modifiers.

verevonToday.gap: execute_native_target_action resolves the backend node and checks isConnected, then runs element.click() inside Runtime.callFunctionOn: a synthetic, untrusted click with no visibility, stability, scroll or covered-element check (SRC, read in this audit). Only coordinate click_point uses trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent. Press carries only a key string, and a grep of contracts.rs finds no drag, paste, modifier or clipboard support.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser (chromiumoxide.rs): implement the actionability + hit-test pipeline with OOPIF coordinate transforms behind a driver capability first, add typed error codes to quarry-core contracts, then extend AgentAction (press{modifiers}, drag, select_text, paste{format}) with a per-session virtual clipboard in the page.
items.risks: Cross-origin iframe coordinate transforms are fiddly and regressions in existing flows are possible, so ship behind a capability flag. The rich-input phase is nice-to-have and can be deferred.

verevon.exactGap: Ref-targeted click, type and select run as in-page DOM operations through Runtime.callFunctionOn: execute_native_target_action checks only isConnected, then calls element.click() or sets the value and dispatches synthetic events (chromiumoxide.rs:1232-1330), and the non-native verified-target path does the same in a page script (chromiumoxide.rs:2026-2093). There is no scroll-into-view, visibility, enabled, stability or covered-element check and no hit-test on the ref path; only click_point (chromiumoxide.rs:2841) dispatches trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent, the legacy selector click and type use chromiumoxide's scrolling, trusted-event helpers (2828-2915), Press carries only a key string (contracts.rs:699), and the only typed target error is TargetRepairRequired (error.rs:30).
reuse: execute_native_target_action backend-node resolution and per-frame execution-context lookup (chromiumoxide.rs:1232-1290)
click_point's moved/pressed/released Input.dispatchMouseEvent sequence as the trusted dispatch primitive (chromiumoxide.rs:2841-2896)
BrowserDriverCapabilities flag pattern (lib.rs:269-286) to gate the new pipeline per driver
ActionOutcome::unknown(postcondition_required) in observation.rs, which keeps Quarry from claiming a business effect
verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser only; Quarry owns execution and must keep returning an unverified postcondition rather than claim success. The Model Plane browser.act wire schema is a closed list, so new inputs (modifiers, drag, paste) are not reachable by the model without a separate Model Plane contract change. Upload and download reuse the same native click helper and stay approval-gated, so changing the click semantics must not weaken or alter those gates.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Direction is right. Express the new failures as ErrorCode::TargetRepairRequired (409) with details.reason (covered_by, not_visible, disabled, unstable) instead of new ErrorCode variants, since ErrorCode is a wire contract shared with the Go, TypeScript and Model Plane clients. Put the pipeline behind a new BrowserDriverCapabilities flag so Browserbase, Browserless and Kernel adapters are unaffected, and leave the synthetic path for governed download clicks until trusted-click download behaviour is verified. Sequence same-frame actionability and trusted dispatch first; the cross-process iframe hit-test and the rich-input phase (modifiers, drag, select_text, paste, virtual clipboard) are separate follow-ups.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for same-frame actionability, hit-test, trusted dispatch and typed errors; the OOPIF coordinate transforms and the rich-input phase together are L and should be split out.
verevon.verdictReason: Accurately describes a real gap on every AI ref click and type; only the error-contract and capability-flag details need adjusting.

items.title: Scoped, robots-compliant crawl: wire CrawlFrontier scoping, robots enforcement and typed denials into the live crawl path
items.summary: The Go CrawlJobWF enqueues every discovered link with no scope or robots check (workflows.go:396-610, SRC), while the Rust CrawlFrontier with typed denials and the RobotsCache/parser exist unused; robots.txt is applied only in /v1/map. Add the scoping vocabulary (include/exclude paths with ReDoS and size caps, subdomain and external-link switches, depth, sitemap mode) on a ScrapeOptions-backed CrawlRequest; enforce robots by default on crawl, batch and Model-proposed autonomous fetches, with ignore-robots as an audited Control Plane entitlement; report blocked URLs as typed per-URL errors with fix-it messages; and decide the ZDR posture of the durable orchestrator path (crawls are refused under ZDR today).
items.whyItMatters: Scoping and robots compliance are table-stakes in both crawl benchmarks (Firecrawl SRC, Apify DOC). Repo docs claim robots handling is closed while the code does not enforce it (SRC). Unscoped crawls waste budget and expose every org to compliance risk.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (native Rust filter_links with typed denial map and remediation messages)
others: Apify enqueueLinks (strategy, globs, transformRequest hook)
Firecrawl (api-surface fc-008 full scoping vocabulary)
Firecrawl (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources (both crawl platforms; Codex and Aside have no crawler); table-stakes || scoped crawl: 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify), table-stakes || 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify); table-stakes for the scraping half
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: filter_links(candidates, opts) returns (allowed, denials{url: reason}). Checks in order: parse, protocol, fragment-only, depth > maxDiscoveryDepth, scope (directory prefix of seed unless crawlEntireDomain/allowBackwardLinks), domain/subdomain/external, include then exclude patterns on path or full URL, file extension, social-media, robots. Patterns are validated with ReDoS caps (<=1000 patterns, <=2000 chars each, 100k total). Each denial reason maps to a message that names the matched pattern or depth and the option to set (for example allowSubdomains). Apify adds a transformRequest hook so callers can drop or retag requests. || Merged items add: CrawlRequest {url, includePaths[], excludePaths[] (regex, optionally matched on the full URL), maxDiscoveryDepth, limit, crawlEntireDomain, allowSubdomains, allowExternalLinks, sitemap skip|include|only, ignoreQueryParameters, delay, maxConcurrency, scrapeOptions, webhook}; reject over 1000 patterns or 2000 chars each; the frontier filters candidates through scope rules, a robots cache, canonicalisation and dedupe; a robots override exists only behind a team flag; limit is clamped to remaining credits. || Before enqueue/fetch, get robots.txt for the origin from a cache (TTL about 1 day), fetching it through the normal engine chain with a short timeout. Evaluate it for the product user agent. If disallowed, skip the URL and record {url, reason: robots} in a per-job blocked set that the errors endpoint returns. Crawl enforces by default and scrape is opt-in. Override flags (ignore robots, custom UA) are team entitlements checked at request time and forbidden under a compliance profile. Fetch errors fail open.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: call the Rust scope and robots filter from the Go workflow (edge endpoint or activity helper), add CrawlRequest fields, and unify the user-agent token as a first step (the rest of identity work is F-t2-067). Control Plane: ignore-robots entitlement and audit event. items.title: Public async job lifecycle: status, paginated results, per-URL errors, cancel/pause/resume, origin and live tail
items.summary: Expose the missing job lifecycle for crawl and batch: GET /v1/crawl/:id (status, completed/total, warnings, expiry, cursor-paged data capped at 100 docs or 10 MiB), GET /v1/crawl/:id/errors (per-URL failures including robots-blocked), GET /v1/crawl/ongoing, DELETE /v1/crawl/:id (cancel) and POST pause/resume, with /v1/batch aliases. Turn /v1/jobs/:id/events into a real live tail that sends a catch-up snapshot first and supports Last-Event-ID. || Add authenticated, org-checked routes on the Quarry edge and the gateway for crawl status, cancel, pause and resume that map onto the Temporal signals the crawl workflow already handles. Add a live SSE tail for job events, a recorded run origin (user, agent, schedule, webhook, api) and a stage timeline on the job record, and surface the controls in the crawl UI and as Model Plane tools.
items.whyItMatters: Users notice immediately when a runaway crawl cannot be stopped or a failed page cannot be explained, and agents need a single poll call. This is also the dependency for webhooks, waiters, resumable timeouts and monitors. The Temporal cancel/pause/resume handlers already exist, so most of the work is route wiring rather than new engine logic. || A user or agent who starts a crawl today (up to 5000 pages) has no way to stop, pause or inspect it from the product. Agents need the same controls to honour budgets, and the audit model needs to know who or what started a run.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: GET /crawl/:id returns {status, completed, total, creditsUsed, expiresAt, data[page], next, warnings[]} where the page ends at 100 docs or 10 MiB and the cursor advances by what was actually returned; /errors returns [{url, code, error, requiresAction}] plus robotsBlocked[]; DELETE sends a cancel signal; results expire by TTL. The stream sends {type:'catchup', data: status}, then each finished document, then done, with defined close codes; support Last-Event-ID so reconnects do not lose events (the reference polls once a second server-side and its SDK falls back to polling, so build the tail off durable event history instead). || Merged items add: A state machine is persisted on the run record with a timestamp per transition and an origin. Abort emits an aborting event, waits a grace period (30 s on Apify) and then hard-stops. State is persisted periodically and on a migrating event so a run can resume. Resurrect restarts the timer with the same storage ids. Firecrawl records an array of steps so a UI can draw a timeline.

items.title: Make scrape, crawl and batch schedules actually execute (Temporal schedules)
items.summary: Map crawl, scrape and batch schedule target kinds to Temporal ScheduleSpec instead of skipping them, wire a Temporal client into quarry-control so trigger and backfill stop returning 501, add a timezone field and record skipped reasons as job events. Until this ships, stop the gateway UI offering actions the backend cannot perform.
items.whyItMatters: Scheduled re-crawls of tracked sources keep Verevon's knowledge fresh, and the UI already lets users create such schedules. Today only change_monitor schedules run, so users can create schedules that silently never fire, which erodes trust and leaves knowledge stale.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (scheduler with lease claim, deterministic jitter, skipped_overlap/skipped_no_credits, stale recovery, plain-English cron)
others: Apify (timezone-aware cron, per-run input overrides, failure notifications)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources (both crawl platforms); table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Scheduler tick selects due schedules FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and sets lease_until; fire_at = next_cron(tz) + sha256(id) mod min(interval/2, 5 min); if the previous run is still active record skipped_overlap and advance; if entitlement is insufficient record skipped_no_credits; otherwise reserve credits, start the workflow with the stored input override and advance next_run_at. Runs active past a threshold are marked failed and released. A phrase parser turns 'every 30 minutes' into cron with a 5-minute minimum. Failures notify the owner.

verevonToday.gap: workflowFor in schedule_wire.go maps only change_monitor to a workflow; scrape, crawl and batch return an empty workflow and the orchestrator skips them (the code comment says they are not run_id-safe for recurring dispatch yet). MountScheduleAliases receives a nil Temporal client, so trigger and backfill return a typed 501. Cron is a strict 5-field expression with no timezone, and there is no jitter or skipped-reason status. The gateway UI exposes overlap policy, pause, trigger and backfill that the backend cannot fully honour (INF from comparing gateway and control code).

items.approach: Ingestion Plane. Extend workflowFor to return CrawlJobWF, scrape and batch workflow names plus args, deriving a fresh replay-safe run_id from each scheduled workflow execution exactly as ChangeMonitorWF already does. Let Temporal schedules provide overlap policy (skip), jitter, timezone and backfill rather than building a custom Firecrawl-style scheduler. Inject the Temporal client into quarry-control (MountScheduleAliases) so trigger and backfill work. Add a timezone column and spec field, write skipped/failed reasons as job events, and send failure notifications via notification-core in the Application Plane. Scheduled fires must inherit the org's ZDR floor and re-check entitlement at fire time, not only at create time. Migrate with an explicit enable step so previously created schedules do not all start firing at once.
dependencies: F-t2-008 entitlement check for a skipped_no_credits state
items.risks: Existing schedules will start firing after the fix, which can surprise users and spend budget; require an explicit re-enable. Recurring crawls without R-t2-05-01 scoping would repeat the off-site walk, so sequence after scoping.

items.title: Structured extraction that works in production: json, summary, question and highlights formats over a real Model Plane structured-output grant
items.summary: Add json (schema plus prompt, strict-schema normalisation, JSON repair), summary, question and highlights as ScrapeOptions formats on scrape and crawl, executed by calling a Model Plane structured-output endpoint over an org-bound, metered model-invoke grant. Today the prompt field is dead code, JSON exists only on /v1/extract, and the cross-plane token manifest denies model-invoke, so extraction only works under dev bypass (SRC). The grant is a tracked deferral (DEF-QB-T17-PART2, owner and date unassigned).
items.whyItMatters: Schema-to-JSON extraction is the most-used LLM feature of scrape APIs and the basis for monitors, research jobs and extraction profiles. The Model Plane already centralises ZDR-aware model routing, so Quarry should call it rather than hold its own model keys.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: normalizeSchema (additionalProperties:false, every field required, $ref resolved) then validate for strict mode with clear errors; pick the model by schema complexity ($ref/$defs go to a larger model); trim markdown by character bound then tokenizer to 80 percent of the context; call with response_format json_schema strict; on parse failure run a repair pass; on provider error fall back to the next provider; return data + warnings + token usage. summary, question and highlights are each one LLM call over trimmed markdown (10,000-char inputs) with a fixed instruction, returned as document.summary|answer|highlights; billed per page. || Merged items add: formats:[{type:'json', schema, prompt}] on scrape: convert the page to markdown, call the LLM with schema-constrained output, validate against the schema, return data.json; multi-page work goes through batch or the agent; the old /extract stays with Deprecation headers pointing to the new shape.

items.title: Harden persistent browser profiles: complete snapshots, per-org envelope encryption at rest, ordered saves, ZDR enforced inside Quarry
items.summary: Capture cookie expiry, storage for every origin and IndexedDB in profile snapshots; envelope-encrypt snapshots (and secret job inputs) per org and owner with keys obtained through a Control Plane key API (env master key first, KMS later); add monotonic saved_at and deletion tombstones; wire the S3 store and the GDPR purge consumer; and enforce in Quarry, not only in the UI, that ZDR orgs get no persistent profile.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent profiles hold live session cookies for users' signed-in sites. Today snapshots are incomplete and not encrypted at rest (SRC), which is a data-governance risk that grows with every login handed to the agent. Encryption is specified in docs/CONTRACTS.md:185-199 but not implemented.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl profiles (firecrawl-api-surface-058 and firecrawl-engine-and-infra-106, SRC)
others: Apify SessionPool with session-to-proxy-IP pinning (apify-platform-059, DOC)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources (apify, firecrawl), table-stakes || 1 of 4 sources; unique (adopted here as a security baseline, not a feature)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Profile = {id, scope, owner, fingerprint, egress affinity, snapshot blob ref, saved_at, deleted_at}. Save is an UPSERT with saved_at = GREATEST(saved_at, new) and is ignored when a newer deletion tombstone exists, so a late save cannot resurrect a deleted profile. Snapshot = all cookies (expiry, SameSite, partition key) + local/session storage per origin + IndexedDB export, encrypted with a per-org key. Profiles are refused under ZDR, lockdown and Safe Mode. Caller cookies go in with Network.setCookies at the registrable domain. || Merged items add: On save generate a random AES-256-GCM key, encrypt the value, wrap that key with an RSA-2048 public key unique to (user, tool) and persist ENCRYPTED_VALUE:<wrapped>:<ciphertext>. At run start the runtime receives the private key through a mounted file or env and decrypts in process; logs and stored input keep only ciphertext.

Profile pinning for scrape is F-t2-058. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-02] Ingestion Plane: in quarry-browser capture_snapshot use Storage.getCookies/Network.getAllCookies for the BrowserContext with expiry and SameSite, iterate visited origins for DOMStorage, add IndexedDB via the CDP IndexedDB domain, and re-apply UA/locale/timezone with Emulation overrides on restore. In quarry-runtime profile stores add an envelope-encryption layer (data key per profile wrapped by an org key; the Control Plane owns keys and Quarry fetches wrapped keys over its API, never through its DB), a saved_at monotonic upsert plus tombstone column in postgres_profile_store.rs, and construct S3ProfileStore in main.rs for blobs above a size threshold. In profile_routes.rs and session create, reject persistent profiles when the request or token ZDR floor is set. Keep scopes and the restore probe; Space access must never widen a profile's owner ACL. || [R-t2-06-03] Ingestion Plane, quarry-runtime: add an encrypting layer at the row/object serialization boundary of postgres_profile_store.rs and s3_profile_store.rs (not above the cache) so the Redis cache holds the ciphertext envelope, or bypass the cache for snapshots. Envelope format {enc_v, key_id, nonce, aad = org|profile|snapshot, ciphertext}; data key per (org, owner) wrapped by a master key from QUARRY_PROFILE_KEY or a KMS id with key_id for rotation. Lazy re-encrypt plaintext rows on next save plus a one-off backfill migration. Wire the existing GDPR purge consumer to delete the wrapped key (crypto-shredding). Mark isSecret in the pack schema (R-t2-06-06) so receipts and gateway logs redact them.

verevon.verdictReason: Gaps are real (current-URL cookies, no expiry, no IndexedDB, plaintext at rest, no ordering) but ZDR is already enforced inside Quarry for runs, the S3 path is unnecessary for the first slice, one evidence line is a test fixture, and the purge consumer does not touch profiles; reword and split.

items.title: Secret redaction at capture time: AX/DOM snapshots, screenshots, OCR, receipts and logs, before storage or model exposure
items.summary: Wire the existing agent_memory::redact_sensitive (used today only by the scratchpad) into observation, evidence, OCR and log paths, and add Aside-style two-tier redaction inside Quarry's snapshot builder: snapshots always mask password, tel, one-time-code and card fields (input type, autocomplete token, label and secret-pattern rules, Luhn check), and durable captures redact by field meaning and value shape (JWTs, API-key prefixes, private keys, OTPs); mask the same fields in screenshots using their boxes. The opaque credential vault is F-t2-024.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon records more than any reference (receipts, timeline, proof bundles, live frames), so it also captures more secrets. Only URLs and egress receipts are redacted today and the AX projection copies node values verbatim (SRC; whether Chromium masks password values in the AX tree was not checked). Redaction is a precondition for credential handoff.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (secret redaction at capture, aside-browser-product-041)
others: Aside (opaque vault refs; fills run in an isolated world that re-checks origin and password-field type; two-tier redaction: snapshots always redact password inputs, durable capture redacts by input type, autocomplete semantics and value shape)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources (Aside); unique. || Redaction 2 of 4 (differentiator); credential vault 1 of 4 (Aside, unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: In the accessibility-snapshot capture: drop values for input types password and tel and for sensitive autocomplete tokens; regexes on field labels (cvv, otp, pin, ssn, secret); value patterns (jwt, aws-access-key, api-key, slack-token, private-key-block, labelled secret, numeric OTP) plus a Luhn check for digit runs; replace with [redacted]. Rules are layered and applied before storage. || Merged items add: The REPL or tool API returns summaries and opaque refs only. fill() runs Runtime.callFunctionOn in an isolated world that checks protocol and host against the bound origin and that the element is a connected, enabled input[type=password], then sets the value with Input.insertText and never returns it. Persisted evidence goes through a redactor with typed detectors; secrets injected into runs are registered so their literal values are scrubbed from logs.

The AX projection copies each node value verbatim (ax_value_text(node.get("value"))) with no role-based masking in Verevon code; whether Chromium already masks password values in its AX tree, and what screenshots or OCR expose, was not confirmed. There is no credential vault, autofill or secret-reference action; persistent-profile cookies are unencrypted per the baseline; integration-corev2 has an AES-GCM token vault, but only for OAuth tokens.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser snapshot and observation builder, artifact writers) first, then Model Plane observation and log paths. Verify the snapshot builder end to end before building. || Source detail: [R-t2-08-08] Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser snapshot and observation builder): a rule module with unit tests that run before persistence and before the response to the Model Plane; screenshot masking of password-like fields using their rects; keep rules auditable and versioned. Confirm separately whether typed text for sensitive fields appears in action receipts. Reuse rule definitions with R-t2-02-09 (PII stage for scraped content) but keep this pass deterministic and local to live observation. || [R-t2-07-07] Ingestion Plane: apply redact_sensitive at the observation builder and evidence/OCR persistence points, add password-field masking to native_projection_from_cdp and the DOM snapshot, and test against the quarry-runtime TestSite login page. Vault: secrets live in the Control Plane or integration-corev2 (reuse its AES-GCM vault crypto); the Model Plane proposes fill(item_ref, target_ref) (the Model proposes, Quarry executes); Quarry performs the origin-checked injection after a sensitive one-shot grant and a first-use approval, with an audit event per fill. Decide explicitly how vault use interacts with ZDR.
dependencies: Item F-t2-036 for the fill audit and durable grants
items.risks: False positives hide useful values (keep rules auditable); regex cost on large snapshots; screenshot masking depends on accurate rects. || High: credential exfiltration through prompt injection, mitigated by origin binding, per-item policy and approval on first use. Over-redaction can break extraction, so keep rules narrow and typed.

Rules must be deterministic and local with no model call. ZDR: live observations and frames are returned even when nothing is persisted, so masking applies on the ZDR path too. Quarry and Model Plane are separate workspaces, so share patterns by duplication with a conformance test (or an ADR for a shared crate) rather than a cross-plane dependency. Credential fill stays in F-t2-024 with origin binding.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: redact_sensitive is dead code and the better pattern source is execution-core scrub.rs. Field-semantic masking needs input type and autocomplete, which an AX node does not carry, so the snapshot builder must fetch them (for example a DOM describe or page evaluate per input target); whether Chromium already masks password values in the AX tree is not verified here. Redact AgentAction::Type text and the stored observation at receipt persistence, and scrub the planner prompt's extracted_text before inference. Treat screenshot masking by element rects as a follow-on slice.
verevon.effortNote: The item spans AX, DOM, receipts, screenshots, OCR and logs; text surfaces alone (AX, DOM, receipts, planner prompt) are M, screenshot and OCR masking adds a second M.
verevon.verdictReason: Quarry-side capture masking is genuinely absent, but the item misstates what exists: redact_sensitive is unwired, a pattern scrubber already guards Model Plane persistence, and receipts keep typed text; reword with scrub.rs as the source and split text from screenshot masking.

items.title: Org-pinned, tighten-only web policy: tri-state capability gates delivered as signed claims and enforced by Quarry
items.summary: Make the Control Plane the policy of record for web and browser capabilities (robots mode and override, maximum proxy tier, credential/cookie/header stripping, login or form-write actions for autonomous runs, raw evaluate, uploads and downloads, recording, persistent profiles, paid providers, domain allow/deny, ZDR) as disabled/allowed/forced, delivered on the signed-claim channel that already carries the ZDR floor and inside BrowserBroker grants as action classes. Quarry rejects at the edge and re-resolves per URL in PageRunner and the step path as a backstop. Requests, Spaces and the Model can only tighten.
items.whyItMatters: This is the direct implementation of three Verevon rules: Quarry executes or rejects, ZDR must propagate, and Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. Today two RunPolicy types exist and the edge hard-wires RunPolicy::default(), so no org or request policy is applied (SRC); control-plane presets are not consumed. Firecrawl Safe Mode (SRC) is the reference shape.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl Safe Mode (SRC)
others: Firecrawl (per-team tri-state flags and per-key restrictions), with Codex's default-off browser gates
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique, but it maps onto Verevon's own governance rules || 2 of 4 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: ResolvedPolicy = merge(orgPolicy, defaults) is computed in the API layer, which rejects requests that ask for forbidden options (403 SAFE_MODE_BLOCKED), and is recomputed in the worker for every URL including crawl children as a backstop that downgrades instead of trusting the request. It strips Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization, write/press/executeJavascript actions, profiles and URL userinfo, blocks browser endpoints, and bypasses allow-listed domains. All violations produce audit events. || Merged items add: Firecrawl TeamFlags hold disabled|allowed|forced per capability (ZDR for scrape and search can be forced, plus ignoreRobots, threatProtection, ipWhitelist); effective option = forced ? on : (allowed ? request : reject with typed error). Keys additionally carry allowedEndpoints and allowedFormats, checked per request and cached about 60 s. Codex keeps fine-grained gates (browserUse, full CDP access, webMcp, record-and-replay, auto-auth-for-sites, multi-window) that default to off with a dev-only env override.

verevonToday.gap: RunPolicy not org-pinned and not enforced; gates live in env or manifests; ZDR already works as a forced posture via the zdr JWT claim floor, which is the pattern to generalise (SRC).

items.approach: ADR first: policy of record in org-core (Control) vs capability-core (Model). Then Control Plane org-core policy storage and admin UI, auth-core claim minting, BrowserBroker action-class grants, and Quarry edge/PageRunner enforcement with typed denials (F-t2-032 builds per-origin consent on top). || Source detail: [R-t2-04-05] Control Plane: org policy record, entitlements (robots.ignore, proxy.enhanced, and so on) and audit events. Gateway shared::quarry_token adds a compact policy_floor claim beside the ZDR floor. Ingestion Plane: one resolved-policy type in quarry-core that merges the org floor over the request (replace the hard-wired defaults at routes.rs:461 and similar, and reconcile the two RunPolicy types). Enforce at the edge by rejecting with a typed sub-code, and again in PageRunner and agent step execution per URL (including crawl children and redirects), downgrading rather than trusting the request. Remove or entitlement-gate presets that contradict governance (fast = RobotsIgnore, stealth). Model Plane: pass the resolved policy in the run grant so the planner does not propose forbidden actions. Scope it to autonomous and agent actions and credential use; the human user's own manual browsing in the pane is not blocked, unlike Firecrawl's blanket 'no interactive sessions'. || [R-t2-06-02] Control Plane: org-core owns an admin-editable capability policy ({capability_key: disabled|allowed|forced}, keys such as browser.evaluate, browser.upload, browser.download, browser.persistent_profile, search.paid_provider, crawl.ignore_robots), exposed read-only to auth-core the way retention-posture is today. auth-core adds a capability-policy claim next to zdr and Quarry's Claims struct resolves request options against it (forced overrides, disabled rejects with a typed error). Model Plane: browser-broker adds allowed_action_classes and allowed_formats to ordinary grants (persisted in Postgres or Redis), computed from the org policy intersected with capability-core's Allow/Deny/Ask decision, with escalation through the existing approval flow. Quarry: the grant validator checks action class per step; ship default-deny plus sensitive approval for Evaluate immediately, independent of the rest.
dependencies: Control Plane policy record, entitlements and audit
BrowserBroker grant issuance in production (cross-category; not re-verified)
org-core policy storage and admin UI
Decide the policy of record: org-core (Control) versus capability-core (Model)
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (policy of record) + Model Plane (grants) + Ingestion Plane (enforcement)
items.risks: Policy resolved in two places can drift, so share one crate and test both paths. Overly strict defaults can break legitimate login-based research. A Space must never be able to widen the org policy (ownership-matrix rule). Ship a thin first slice (claims floor, robots, proxy-tier cap, credential stripping) together with R-t2-04-01. || Claim staleness when policy changes mid-run (mitigate with the short 15 min grant TTL and revalidation per action). Overly narrow grants can cause mid-run failures, so keep escalation through approvals. Two policy engines (org-core entitlements versus capability-core) must not diverge: pick one of record. Space access must never widen these gates.

verevon.exactGap: Only ZDR is org-pinned today: org-core's RetentionPosture feeds an auth-core claim that Quarry's Claims::zdr_floor raises over request flags, and that floor applies to user tokens only (service tokens are ignored by design). No org or request web policy exists: the edge hard-wires RunPolicy::default() (routes.rs:461, main.rs:1493), two unrelated RunPolicy types exist, control's presets (fast = RobotsIgnore) are never consumed by the edge, and quarry-control's /v1/blocklists entries have no org column and are not read by the edge. The Model Plane gate is one coarse capability (browser.observe/act and browser_agent all map to cap.browser.open) plus capability-core org-scope grants, with no action-class, robots, proxy-tier or header-stripping gates.
reuse: org-core RetentionPosture read endpoint plus auth-core claim stamping as the delivery pattern for a read-only policy posture (org-core types.go:255-315, quarry-edge auth.rs:56-140)
Claims::effective_zdr / zdr_floor as the 'can only raise, never lower' merge semantics to copy for every other gate
BrowserBroker grants: broker-owned allowed_domains (agent_routes.rs validate_run_grant) and the sensitive-action allowlist (grant.go:30-36) as the carrier for action classes
capability-core tenant-bound org-scope grants (engine.go denyOnGrant) and execution-core capability_policy Allow/Deny/Ask
quarry-runtime RunPolicy / DiscoveryPolicy (robots, proxy, block) as the base for one ResolvedPolicy type
BrowserEgressPolicy deny-all default and the existing ZDR refusals (zdr_persistent_profile_forbidden, refuse_durable_job_under_zdr)
verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns the org policy of record, Model Plane issues grants, Quarry (Ingestion) enforces or rejects with typed errors; there is no cross-plane DB access, so policy must travel as a signed claim or a grant field. CONFLICT: the claim channel that carries the ZDR floor only reaches user-token callers (gateway UI paths). execution-core and model-gateway call Quarry with service tokens whose zdr claim is true for every org and is deliberately ignored, so for Model-Plane-driven runs the resolved policy has to ride in the BrowserBroker grant or the start-run body set by the Model Plane. Space access must never widen the org policy, the Model can only propose and Quarry executes or rejects, and existing stricter ZDR refusals must not be loosened.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Run the ADR first: org-core claims versus capability-core grants (capability-core already has tenant-bound org-scope grants and a single coarse browser capability). Do not describe the ZDR claim as covering the agent path; deliver policy by claim to user-token callers and by grant fields to Model-Plane-driven runs. Ship a Quarry-only thin slice before any org-core storage or admin UI: one ResolvedPolicy replacing the RunPolicy::default() sites, tighten-only merge with the existing zdr floor, typed denials for Evaluate/upload/download (ties to F-t2-002). Reconcile or delete the second RunPolicy type and the unused fast/stealth presets, and wire or retire /v1/blocklists, instead of adding a third policy shape.
verevon.effortNote: Kept at L because it spans four planes plus an ADR; treat the Quarry-only slice as M and the org-core/auth-core/broker plumbing as the remaining L.
verevon.verdictReason: Direction is right and nothing substantial exists, but the delivery channel is wrong for the agent path, capability-core grants already exist as a competing policy of record, and a Quarry-only first slice is missing from the plan.

items.title: Scrape-time page actions plus screenshot and PDF formats, under one bounded, grant-gated action policy
items.summary: Add actions[] (the tagged Action enum in quarry-browser/src/actions.rs) to ScrapeOptions and run it through the existing ActionRuntime on one page before extraction, with Firecrawl-style caps (about 50 actions, 60 s total wait, script size cap), lowering waitFor and screenshot into the same ordered list. Make screenshot{fullPage, clip, quality, viewport} and pdf first-class formats that reuse the agent capture code, add tile-and-stitch for tall pages plus element and clip shots, return per-action outputs, and keep everything inline only under ZDR. Evaluate inside actions follows the F-t2-002 policy.
items.whyItMatters: Declarative actions and screenshot/PDF output are table-stakes for scrape APIs (Firecrawl SRC, Apify DOC; screenshots also in Codex and Aside). The runtime pieces already exist in Quarry but scrape cannot reach them: screenshot and pdf formats are always None (SRC).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl scrape actions (firecrawl-api-surface-057 and firecrawl-engine-and-infra-012, SRC)
others: Apify Crawlee page hooks and Playwright actions (apify-platform-060, DOC)

items.summary: Add a fill_secret action carrying an opaque vault:// reference that Quarry resolves only at execution time through the integration-corev2 token broker, fills in an isolated world after re-checking origin and field type, and then blocks page observation of the filled value; add an IC mail.otp.read action so email one-time codes are delivered by the executor after user approval. referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Agent calls request({origin, fields[{label, selector, autocomplete}], submit}). items.title: Per-org capacity: concurrency caps with backlog and fair share, per-class rate limits and plan-aware quotas
items.summary: Add a per-org concurrency cap with a bounded backlog and fair-share priority inside the existing Postgres queue (Firecrawl pattern: over-limit work waits with an expiry, 429 only when the backlog is full), per-endpoint-class rate limits on the gateway browser, scrape and search routes, and plan-keyed limits read from Control Plane entitlements via claims (no cross-plane DB reads).
items.whyItMatters: With a two-session lease pool and no per-org caps, one tenant can starve all others; the browser, search and ingestion gateway routes have no rate limiting (SRC per baseline). Plan-scaled limits are table-stakes for web platforms (Firecrawl SRC, Apify DOC).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (tenant backlog with expiry, in-flight priority penalty, 429 only on backlog overflow)
others: Firecrawl (SRC)
Firecrawl (per-endpoint base limits times a plan multiplier, with org override)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; differentiator (Apify documents plan concurrency limits but not this mechanism) || 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique as a documented design || 2 of 4 sources (both crawl platforms); common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Sync path: a per-tenant lease semaphore (holders with TTL, heartbeated) waits up to 2/3 of the request timeout with jittered backoff. Async path: if active(org) >= limit, insert into backlog(org, job, times_out_at) instead of the queue; when a job finishes, promote the oldest backlog entry respecting per-crawl max concurrency; a reaper expires backlog rows (max 48 h). Backlog capacity = clamp(limit x 2000, 50k, 2M); overflow returns 429 naming the limit. Fair share: priority stays at base until in_flight(org, 60 s window) exceeds a bucket limit, then base + ceil((count - bucketLimit) x planModifier). || Merged items add: A Redis limiter keyed by (org, endpoint class). Limit = base[class] x plan multiplier, with per-org overrides. Cheap status polling has a high limit and browser sessions a low one. The limiter fails open if the entitlement lookup is down, and returns 429 with Retry-After. || BASE_RATE_LIMITS per endpoint class (scrape 10, map 10, crawl 2, search 10, extract 2, browser 2, status 500 per minute) multiplied by a plan multiplier (1, 10, 50, 500), with per-org overrides per mode; a token-bucket limiter keyed by (org, mode); priority tier derived from the same multiplier. Quotas are counted on create (schedules, webhooks) and rejected with a typed error.

Shares the admission code with F-t2-006. || Source detail: [R-t2-05-05] Ingestion Plane enforces, Control Plane owns the numbers. Quarry reads the org's concurrency limit from the verified principal or an entitlement call, counts active rows per org in the same Postgres queue (no second store), adds an org_backlog table promoted on completion, applies an in-flight priority penalty in the claim ORDER BY (postgres_queue.rs), and returns a typed 429 with Retry-After. Count agent browser leases against the same org budget or a sibling cap so agent fleets cannot bypass it (INF). Frontend: show queue position via the existing team queue-status route. First make the durable frontier the only production crawl path (hardening of the existing queue: remove the in-workflow slice fallback, add a stall counter with max-stall fail-out). || [R-t2-04-11] Frontend Plane gateway: replace the single DEFAULT_RPM bucket lookup with a class-aware limiter (class derived from route, key = org, base limits multiplied by Control Plane plan entitlements, separate interactive and agent classes so human browsing is not throttled by agents). Ingestion Plane: per-org permit accounting in the lease pool (guaranteed minimum plus burst) and a coarse per-org backstop in quarry-edge that returns the existing RATE_LIMITED envelope with retry_after_seconds. || [R-t2-05-10] Control Plane owns the multiplier and quota numbers and exposes them in the principal or entitlement claims. Quarry edge applies a token bucket per (org, endpoint class: scrape, map, crawl, search, extract, browser, status) with Retry-After, and checks quota counts when creating schedules and webhooks. Gateway keeps coarse inbound abuse protection only. Verify what exists in the Control Plane first.
dependencies: Control Plane entitlement for concurrency per org
durable frontier always on in production
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane + Frontend gateway + Control Plane (entitlements)
items.risks: Mis-set limits block onboarding crawls; keep the count in Postgres only to avoid Firecrawl's Redis-plus-Postgres reconciler drift. Do not copy Firecrawl's broker prefetch or FoundationDB backend. || Over-tight limits frustrate interactive browsing, so keep interactive and agent classes separate and the global bucket generous. || Double enforcement in gateway and Quarry if ownership is unclear; per-process buckets are inaccurate across edge replicas unless shared storage is used.

verevon.exactGap: The gateway already has a distributed token-bucket limiter (one 600 rpm class in rate_limit.rs, layered over every merged router including browser/search/ingestions and, because it runs before require_session, effectively keyed by client IP; per-org inner limiters exist only on mcp, agents_runs, eval and memory, and mail-task has its own class), so 'no rate limiting on these routes' is wrong, while Control Plane already holds plan-keyed QuotaLimits (billing-core: api_calls/users/storage_mb) and org-core org_quotas rows but no browser/crawl concurrency keys, and quarry-edge Claims carry no plan data. In Quarry the only capacity controls are a process-global RuntimeLeasePool semaphore (2 local-Chromium / 4 Browserbase permits, keyed by host, org_id empty on the internal lease), a global AutoscaledPool and a per-host AIMD HostScheduler: there is no per-org concurrency, backlog or fair share, and agent browser runs (ChromiumoxideDriver plus the agent_runs map) have no cap at all. The Postgres queue is a per-crawl frontier (pop is scoped to org_id + queue_id and the queue name derives from the run id), so a cross-job org backlog cannot live there; the real admission seam is the quarry-control jobs table that the orchestrator dispatcher polls.

reuse: gateway RateLimiter::from_cache_with_rpm plus the route_layer-after-require_session pattern (mcp.rs, agents_runs.rs) for class-specific org-keyed limiters; mail_task_rate_limiter is the per-class precedent
Quarry ApiError::rate_limited (RATE_LIMITED + retry_after_seconds) for the typed 429
