verevonToday.gap: No agent-action settle (agents rely on explicit wait/wait_for); no per-frame deadline or warning list was found around the CDP fetch of the AX tree (verify the capture call site near the native_projection_from_cdp caller); truncation is by order, not viewport priority. The Verevon UI cannot show or use AX refs. || Explicit wait_for actions and fixed waits exist, plus a typed event SSE for the UI, but no adaptive settle was found and page events are not shown to reach the model's next observation. ScreenshotAnnotated exists only as an enum/parse entry plus tests (grep in this audit finds no producer), so set-of-marks is absent; coordinate actions and screenshots are shipped. || Quarry already emits a CDP accessibility projection with frame topology and @eN refs (the stronger primitive, used by Model Plane browser.act), but no character budget or alternative visible-DOM view was found, and the Verevon UI's BrowserObservation type has no field for AX refs or frames. For images: the Model Plane execution-core browser observation carries only a screenshot_ref (an artifact id string), the only image limits found are a 20 MiB cap on the image-generation route, and grep over apps/Model Plane (Rust and Go) finds no image budget, downscale or detail hint. Whether browser screenshots are ever sent to the model as pixels was not established.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser (settle, snapshot, set-of-marks); Model Plane (image budget and cost accounting); Frontend frame view. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-07] Ingestion Plane, quarry-browser/chromiumoxide.rs: add settle() after navigate/click/type/press with per-action budgets (navigation vs click vs type) and emit settle_ms in BrowserTelemetry; for snapshots fetch AX per frame target with timeouts inside a global deadline, return warnings[] in the observation contract (quarry-core BrowserObservation), and reorder truncation by viewport proximity. Frontend Plane: surface refs and warnings in BrowserChrome for co-browsing. Keep truncation explicit so token cost stays visible. || [R-t2-09-11] Ingestion Plane quarry-browser: settle stage after act with same-site request filtering and caps for long-polling pages; extend the observation contract with a bounded events list rendered by the Model Plane into the tool result. Add a mark renderer fed by native AX boxes (no page injection), keep marks tied to the observation revision, and make the PNG ephemeral under ZDR. || [R-t2-02-10] Ingestion Plane observation.rs: add a character budget (and truncation marker) to the AX projection, with an optional visible-DOM projection behind a flag; Frontend Plane: extend BrowserObservation in browser-client.ts with snapshot refs and frames (coordinate with the browser-automation category, which owns the UI action vocabulary). Model Plane (session-core or inference-core): first confirm how screenshots enter model context; only if pixels are sent, add a detail hint on image parts, resize before the provider call, and a per-session image budget that evicts the oldest screenshots, accounted through the cost plane.
dependencies: UI action vocabulary migration to AX refs
Model Plane cost accounting for the image part
items.risks: Long-polling pages never quiesce, so caps are essential; larger snapshots cost tokens; adding a field to the observation contract needs the Model Plane client to tolerate it. || Long-polling pages (websockets, analytics beacons) need same-site filtering and caps; marks must map to refs from the same observation revision; screenshots under ZDR stay ephemeral. || Two projections to maintain; attribute text from pages reaches the model (injection surface, keep the allowlist); low-detail images misread small text.

verevon.exactGap: Quarry already returns a bounded AX and frame projection on every observation (300 AX nodes with a truncated flag, 64 frames, 50 snapshot targets, a 500-char text snippet), console and network summaries, an observation delta, challenge classification and telemetry (usable_observation_latency_ms, estimated_snapshot_tokens), has an explicit frame-ref action contract, and has a scrape-only hydration settle (3.5 s budget, 300 ms poll) in browser_driver.rs; what is missing is any settle after agent actions (observation.rs captures page state, DevTools events, HTML and the AX projection immediately), per-frame deadlines and a warnings field (one root-frame GetFullAxTree call at depth 8), and viewport-priority truncation. On the Model Plane side observation_from_wire forwards only url, title, text snippet, screenshot id and snapshot targets (console/network summaries are dropped), the planner prompt shows at most 40 targets, no screenshot pixels reach the planner (it is text-only; only the UI suggest-action route sends a screenshot to a separate AnalyzeImage summarizer, capped at 6 MiB with 16k/8k-char prompt budgets), and ScreenshotAnnotated is already produced by the vision sidecar as a red changed-region overlay, not as set-of-marks.

apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:1988-2011,2800-2826,3050-3062 (goto, wait_for polling, fixed 100 ms sleeps on back/forward)

reuse: browser_driver.rs visible_text_len/looks_unhydrated settle loop as the model for an agent-action settle
BrowserTelemetry (usable_observation_latency_ms, estimated_snapshot_tokens) to report settle_ms
AccessibilityProjection.truncated, BrowserFrame topology and the frame_*_ref action contract
DomSummary.click_map / ElementClickTarget (ref ids already aligned with snapshot refs) as the mark source
vision sidecar annotation pipeline and put_artifact_if_allowed ZDR gating
model-gateway compact_json_for_prompt budgets already applied on the suggest-action path
verevon.constraints: Model proposes / Quarry executes: settle, snapshot and truncation are executor concerns and stay in Quarry; the wire change must be additive with serde defaults because execution-core parses WireObservation separately. CDP node handles must stay private (BrowserNativeProjection never serializes backend ids). ZDR: screenshots, annotated PNGs and the visual processor run only when ZDR is off, so any set-of-marks artifact must follow put_artifact_if_allowed and stay ephemeral. The UI still acts through CSS selectors, so AX refs and warnings reach the Model Plane first and the co-browsing UI only after a UI action-vocabulary change.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Narrow to what is missing and has a consumer: (1) agent-action settle with per-action budgets, same-site request filtering and a hard cap, reported as settle_ms, living in observation.rs/driver (not copied from the scrape-only loop in the adapter); (2) add warnings[] to AccessibilityProjection and fetch per-frame AX only if cross-origin iframe coverage is needed (getFullAXTree without frameId defaults to the root frame per CDP docs, INF) under a global deadline; (3) prioritise truncation by viewport and interactivity and align the 50-target Quarry cap with the planner's 40-target view; (4) carry console/network summaries through observation_from_wire if the model should see page events. Defer set-of-marks until the planner actually receives images and give it a new artifact kind (ScreenshotAnnotated already means changed-region overlay); drop the model image detail/budget sub-item until screenshots become model input. Side bug: observation.rs:2140 slices a byte index (&trimmed[..500]) and can panic on a multi-byte boundary.
verevon.effortNote: Settle + warnings + prioritised truncation is M; set-of-marks (M) and image budget have no consumer yet and should be split out or dropped.
verevon.verdictReason: Several claimed gaps are partly built (bounded projection, frame refs, console/network summaries, char budgets on the suggest path, an annotated artifact kind), the image budget has no consumer, and the real gaps are the missing settle, per-frame warnings and Model Plane forwarding.

items.title: Durable hosted browser sessions: idle and absolute TTLs, suspend/resume, view vs control tokens, optional recording, scrape-to-session replay
items.summary: Move agent browser run state from the in-process run map to a durable session store with a state machine (starting, running, suspended, stopped, failed), idempotent create, separate idle and absolute TTLs instead of the fixed 120 s / 12 step UI defaults, and suspend/resume implemented as a profile snapshot plus browser release and restore. Issue separate read-only and interactive live-view tokens and add optional recording gated by org policy (off under ZDR). As a later phase, persist a ReplayContext (url, actions, profile, location) on scrape results and add POST /v1/scrape/:id/session so a user or a Model run can continue from a scrape result.
items.whyItMatters: Two minutes is short for real browsing, an in-process map loses runs on restart, and enterprises want audit recordings. The plan documents say crash-safe resume is not yet proven for every provider, and 'continue interactively from this scrape' is a natural AI-first flow.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl Hangar hosted sessions (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-019, SRC)
others: Apify container URL and live view exposing DevTools (apify-platform-061, DOC)
Firecrawl scrape-to-interact replay (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-021, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Session lifecycle and live view: 2 of 4 sources (firecrawl, apify), differentiator. Replay: 1 of 4, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Session row {state, created_at, last_activity_at, idle_ttl, abs_ttl, idempotency_key}; create is idempotent via Idempotency-Key with retries, long-poll until running; a reaper transitions rows on TTL; suspend = snapshot profile and release the browser, resume = new browser plus restore; live view = signed short-lived URLs with view and control scopes; recording = screencast frames to segmented video, disabled under ZDR. Replay: store {url, waitFor, actions, profile, location} with each scrape; promote(scrape_id) verifies the caller owns it, creates a session, replays, and hands the session id to the agent or UI.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: durable session table in Postgres (same pattern as postgres_profile_store and postgres_step_receipts) with the state machine, TTL reaper, idempotency key and suspend/resume via the R-t2-03-02 profile snapshot; wire or retire persistent_session.rs. Add view-scoped and control-scoped live-view tokens at the edge; optional recording to artifacts behind an org policy flag and never under ZDR. Frontend Plane: gateway browser.rs passes TTL options and uses the two token types. Phase 2 (after R-t2-03-03): ReplayContext stored on non-ZDR scrape results and POST /v1/scrape/:id/session, with the Model Plane starting a browser run on the adopted session.
dependencies: F-t2-023 (scrape actions) for the replay phase
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane; token handling in Frontend Plane gateway
items.risks: Recordings and replay contexts are sensitive data; long sessions raise cost; replays are not deterministic on dynamic pages; the in-process run map is a restart-safety risk until replaced.

verevon.exactGap: Quarry already has the durable pieces: a Postgres-backed AgentRunCheckpoint (profile, URL, grant, control mode, status Active/Closed; in-memory fallback when no database is configured), receipts, timeline and event history, an owner projection that falls back to the checkpoint when the live run is gone, resume via resume_run_id (new lease plus persisted profile plus fresh broker grant, ZDR refused), a profile store for cookie/storage snapshots, and Model Plane durable runs with pause/resume/stop; the live Chromium handle necessarily stays in the process-local agent_runs map. Missing are idle and absolute TTLs (RunEntry has no timestamps, max_runtime_s only becomes lease.ttl_s, and persistent_session.rs has no consumers), a reaper, a fuller state machine, recording for the local driver (only Browserbase/Kernel provider flags exist), view-versus-control scope (live view and frames are owner-only, input is gated by control mode), idempotent create, any ReplayContext on scrape results, and a caller of the resume path (execution-core's StartRunRequest and the gateway never send resume_run_id). postgres_profile_store / s3_profile_store for the profile snapshot behind suspend/resume

verevon.constraints: Do not create a second run state machine: the Model Plane (session-core, model-gateway browser_run.rs) owns run pause/resume/stop while Quarry owns the browser session, lease and profile, and the F-t2-054 tab work must share the same checkpoint. ZDR: no checkpoint, timeline, recording or replay context may be stored (current code already skips these under ZDR and refuses ZDR resume), and recording needs an org policy flag from Control Plane plus consent. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so view-only sharing of someone else's run is an ACL decision, not a token type; today only the owning org and actor can read live view and frames. Resume needs a still-valid broker grant and the broker grant store is in-memory.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Extend rather than rebuild: add created_at/last_activity to RunEntry with idle and absolute TTL enforced by a reaper shared with F-t2-006; widen AgentRunCheckpoint.status beyond Active/Closed (suspended, failed) and implement suspend as release with a persisted profile (already what close_run + persist_profile does for non-ZDR runs); wire resume_run_id into execution-core's StartRunRequest and add the rehydration test the roadmap gate asks for; add idempotent create keyed by a start key like model-gateway's managed_start_key. Implement view-only as a scope on the existing owner-checked routes and WS rather than bearer URLs, and treat cross-user sharing as a separate ADR. verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. TTL + reaper + state widening is M and shared with F-t2-006; resume wiring S; scopes M; recording and ReplayContext are separate later phases.
verevon.verdictReason: Durable checkpoints, resume, profile snapshots and Model Plane durable runs already exist, so the item must describe the delta (TTL/idle enforcement, reaper, state widening, resume caller, scopes, recording, replay) instead of a new session store.

items.title: Durable, tenant-scoped authority and one audit record for every permission and approval decision
items.summary: Persist BrowserBroker grants (today an in-memory map), add a production issuance path and scope inheritance for child runs and fleets, and put evaluate and raw-CSS actions behind a sensitive one-shot grant. Add org_id to the quarry-control Webhook model, front webhook CRUD through edge with JWT org scoping, and add a dispatch-id header, a test endpoint and a longer retry ladder. Define an AuthzDecision event in audit-core (schema_version, permission, decision, decision_context, a decided_by enum separating user, saved, policy, reviewer and system, policy_id, reason_code, origin only, run_id, actor_id, duration_ms) that execution-core approvals, browser-broker validations and Quarry policy denials publish to verevon.audit.v2.*; record only denials for high-volume per-navigation checks.
items.whyItMatters: It keeps the authority model credible (Quarry executes only what a grant allows and scope cannot widen through child runs or webhooks) and completes the evidence chain for "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects", which enterprise compliance reviews ask for. Without tenant-scoped webhooks, crawl and monitor webhooks cannot be exposed to customers.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (one structured record per permission decision with decided_by, decision_context, origin only and duration_ms, denials-only for URL checks; Allow/Prompt/Forbidden policy vocabulary) and Apify (limited-permission default with scoped, expiring tokens inherited by runs and webhooks)
others: Aside (read methods whitelisted; lifecycle mutations only through ownership-tracking tools)
Apify webhooks (11 retries over about 32 hours, dispatch-id header, test button, no HMAC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Least-privilege permissions 3 of 4 (table-stakes); decision audit record 1 of 4 (Codex, unique); webhook reliability 1 of 4 (Apify, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grant = {principal, scopes[], allowed_domains[], budget, expires_at, parent_grant}; children inherit min(parent scopes) and escalation needs a recorded human approval. The component that decides emits AuthzDecision with an outcome enum {not_needed, policy_allowed, reviewer_approved, reviewer_denied, user_approved, user_approved_for_session, user_denied, user_aborted, timeout}. Webhooks are (org_id, url, secret, events), HMAC signed, retried with exponential backoff, DLQ at the end, registered only through edge.

verevonToday.gap: Grants are validated before every action (15 minute TTL, host allowlist, org and owner scope) and sensitive one-shot grants exist, but the store is a mutex-guarded in-memory map and no production path issues grants, so history is lost on restart. The sensitive-action allowlist is only respond_dialog, upload_ref and download_ref, so evaluate and raw-CSS run on an ordinary grant (unless the Model Plane risk gate separately prompts; not verified here). The Webhook struct has no OrgID and the routes are not exposed through edge; delivery is HMAC signed with 5 attempts then a DLQ. Browser approvals record (decision, decided_by, reason) and tool_action audit events carry ZDR tags, but there is no cross-plane schema, no decided_by enum, no duration, and grant validations and Quarry policy denials do not reach audit-core.

items.approach: Model Plane browser-broker: durable grant store (Postgres) with issuance from the run-start path, scope inheritance and revocation. Ingestion Plane: add evaluate and raw CSS to the sensitive-action allowlist and the edge enforcement, add org_id to Webhook with a migration for unscoped rows, and expose org-scoped CRUD through edge. Control Plane audit-core defines the AuthzDecision event type; Model Plane (execution-core approvals, browser-broker) and Ingestion Plane (policy denials) publish it with origin only, never full URLs.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (browser-broker, execution-core) with Control Plane audit-core and Ingestion Plane quarry-control
items.risks: Breaking dev flows that rely on dev-bypass tokens; migrating existing webhook rows that have no scope; audit volume from per-navigation checks and accidental URL storage.

verevon.exactGap: Confirmed: BrowserBroker's grant store is a mutex-guarded in-process map with no database; AcquireGrant has no production caller (only an unused Quarry client method and tests, while the gateway sends an interim grant_id of the form session:<id>); the sensitive allowlist is exactly respond_dialog, upload_ref and download_ref; Quarry-control's Webhook struct and table have no org_id and /v1/webhooks is mounted on quarry-control only, not quarry-edge; and approval decisions never reach audit-core in a uniform shape (the browser decided event leaves decided_by empty, session-core publishes tool_action, tool_action_reserved and run_started_zdr_waived but no permission or approval decision event, and Quarry has no audit publisher at all). Corrected: evaluate and raw CSS are not reachable on an ordinary grant through either Verevon facade, because the gateway sanitize_action rejects evaluate and execution-core's browser.act closed schema has no JavaScript, selector or URL, so a sensitive grant for them is quarry-edge defense in depth rather than a live hole. Also understated: webhook delivery already has HMAC signing, five attempts and a DLQ, and the durable approvals table already records decided_by (including system:* deciders) and decision_reason under an org filter, so the audit gap is publication and schema, not capture.

verevon.constraints: Plane ownership: grants belong to the Model Plane (browser-broker, Go with no database today, so durable storage adds a datastore dependency); Quarry only validates. No cross-plane DB access: Quarry must publish AuthzDecision over NATS and never write audit-core tables, and because Quarry has no audit publisher one must be added with its own plane/producer/event subject family and publish grant (audit-core rejects an event whose subject tokens do not match the payload). Privacy and ZDR: events carry origin only and ZDR tags, never full URLs, and per-navigation validations should be recorded denials-only. Space authority: child-run and fleet grants may only narrow (min of parent scopes) and never inherit wider authority through a Space. The webhook org_id migration must handle existing unscoped rows fail-closed.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into three independently shippable items. (a) Durable, issued BrowserBroker grants, merged with F-t2-001 rather than treating persistence and issuance separately, with parent/child inheritance on the existing parent_grant_id binding. (b) Quarry webhook tenant scoping: org_id column with migration, edge-fronted org-scoped CRUD, dispatch-id header. (c) AuthzDecision audit as a new event name on the existing verevon.audit.v2 flat shape, first published by session-core/execution-core approval decisions with decided_by filled from the durable record, and only later by Quarry policy denials. Demote the evaluate/raw-CSS sensitive-allowlist change to low-priority hardening because both facades already refuse those actions.
verevon.effortNote: As one item this bundles a new broker datastore plus issuance path, a Quarry webhook migration and edge exposure, and a cross-plane audit event with a new Quarry publisher. Split, it is roughly M (webhooks), M (audit) and L (durable grants plus issuance, overlapping F-t2-001).
verevon.verdictReason: The gap description is mostly accurate but wrongly implies evaluate/raw CSS are model-reachable on ordinary grants, bundles four independent workstreams across three planes, and overlaps F-t2-001 on issuance. Reword and split.

items.title: Document parsing depth: PDF classification and Model Plane OCR routing, Office and e-book conversion, bounded parsing and a per-org parse cache
items.summary: Branch on PDF (content-type and %PDF magic) in the scrape/crawl pipeline: classify pages as text or scanned, extract text natively with the existing lopdf code, and route only pages that need OCR or layout to the Model Plane document-intelligence provider. Add parsers:[{type:pdf, mode: fast|auto|ocr, maxPages}], per-page markdown and optional layout blocks with bounding boxes, and reuse the same OCR path for raster image URLs. || Add a quarry-transform document module that detects DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODF, RTF, CSV and EPUB from bytes and converts them to markdown under zip-bomb and part-size budgets, branch to it by content-type in the scrape/crawl pipeline, and add a crawl option to follow and store linked office/PDF files as artifacts. Put resource governance around all document parsers (including the PDF path): a tokio semaphore, size ceilings, per-page time budgets, and a content-hash parse cache keyed per org and disabled under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise knowledge is mostly PDF; crawls that skip PDFs leave the Data Plane incomplete and answers ungrounded. The pieces exist in separate planes (native text extraction in Quarry, Azure prebuilt-layout in the Model Plane) but nothing connects them for a crawl. || Company sites link office documents and enterprise users expect them ingested into the Data Plane. Untrusted binary parsing without budgets is also an availability and security risk for Quarry workers, so the guardrails must ship with the parsers.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-080/081 classification and native fast path, api-surface-052 parsers options, engine-and-infra-089 image OCR)
others: Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-085 anydoc crate with ZipReadBudget; engine-and-infra-082/083/084 for async jobs, sha256 parse cache and parser semaphore; api-surface-053)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); unique here, though PDF handling is ordinary in crawl products (INF) || 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify) for office conversion and file capture, table-stakes among scrape platforms; the cache and async-job mechanics are Firecrawl-only (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Sniff content-type and bytes; classify per page (text-layer coverage, image area) into text, scanned, image or mixed with a confidence and pagesNeedingOcr; if text-based with high confidence convert natively with heading ranking; otherwise send only the pages needing OCR to an OCR/layout service and merge per page; emit markdown, optional pages[] and blocks[{type,label,bbox,content}]; mode fast fails with a typed OCR_REQUIRED error on scans. Images: if the parsers list includes image and OCR is enabled, submit as a one-page document, else return a typed unsupported-file error. || Merged items add: Detect by magic bytes plus extension hint. DOCX: unzip with byte and per-part budgets (128 MB total), parse document.xml, _rels and header/footer with roxmltree to markdown; XLSX: sheets to GFM tables (calamine); PPTX: slide text in order; CSV to table; EPUB: XHTML chapters to markdown. A crawl option (saveFiles/contentTypes) stores matched binaries. Guardrails: key = sha256(bytes)(+variant); check cache; acquire a semaphore permit (default 3, FIFO); large files go by reference to an async job that a second request for the same hash adopts; time budget estimated per page; refresh bypasses the cache only within a small per-org budget.

verevonToday.gap: lopdf text extraction (pdf.rs extract_text) is called only by the answer fetcher (answer.rs:835). pipeline.rs has no PDF branch (no application/pdf match), so PDF URLs in scrape or crawl are not converted, although docs/GAP.md:85 says routing is implemented there. No page classification, OCR, page selection or layout blocks. The Model Plane has an Azure Document Intelligence prebuilt-layout provider (doc_intel.rs) that Quarry never calls, and image URLs are not OCRed; Quarry's vision.rs only pre-conditions screenshots for an optional sidecar. || docx.rs extract_text exists and is declared in lib.rs but has no caller (grep finds no use outside the module), though PARITY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:129 marks DOCX as shipped. No XLSX, PPTX, ODF, RTF or EPUB support, no zip-bomb budgets, no crawl capture of linked files. The pipeline has only a body-size cap: no parser concurrency limit, no parse cache, no async document jobs.

items.approach: After the S-sized routing fix (F-t2-009): native PDF fast path with classification, OCR only when needed via the Model Plane doc_intel provider over the model-gateway grant (ZDR-eligible providers only), typed layout blocks, a sha256 per-org parse cache (skipped under ZDR), and wiring docx.rs plus XLSX/PPTX/e-book parsers behind one parser semaphore. docs/PARITY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:129 marks DOCX shipped although it has no caller (stale DOC). || Source detail: [R-t2-02-04] Ingestion Plane pipeline.rs: lift is_pdf from answer.rs into a shared content-type router; add the PDF branch with page classification (text-layer coverage via lopdf), native fast path, and a typed OCR_REQUIRED error in fast mode. For scanned pages call the Model Plane (it owns the provider, cost and ZDR choice): expose doc_intel as a Model Plane route reachable by Quarry under the same grant work as R-t2-02-02. Add parsers[] to the request contract (R-t2-02-01) and optional pages/blocks in the response. Reuse the OCR path for image content types. Under ZDR require a ZDR-eligible OCR provider or return a typed refusal. The semaphore and size ceilings from R-t2-02-07 should land with this item. || [R-t2-02-07] Ingestion Plane quarry-transform: a document module (zip + roxmltree + calamine) with ZipReadBudget-style limits, returning typed errors on budget breach; pipeline.rs routes by content-type and magic bytes to PDF (R-t2-02-04) or the document module; wrap every parser in one shared tokio semaphore and size ceiling; add a crawl option (contentTypes/saveFiles) that stores matched binaries as artifacts and converts them; content-hash cache keyed by (org, sha256), skipped entirely under ZDR; use a Temporal activity for large documents instead of Firecrawl's job-adoption machinery.
dependencies: Model Plane doc_intel exposed to Quarry plus model-gateway grant (shared with F-t2-019)
ZDR eligibility flag on the OCR provider
items.risks: OCR cost and latency on large crawls (needs per-org page and cost caps); the external OCR provider must honour ZDR; the docs claim this is done, so planning may under-scope it. || Zip bombs and malformed files (the budgets are the mitigation); cross-tenant cache leaks if the key omits org; ZDR must skip the cache.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-02-04] Quarry-v2 docs/GAP.md:34,54 and docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:29 record OCR/layout PDF as an open or partial gap; no scheduled task found. || [R-t2-02-07] Quarry-v2 docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:29,104 (P2: add DOCX and extended media parsing); docs/PARITY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:129 marks DOCX shipped although it is not wired.

verevon.exactGap: quarry-transform has lopdf text and heading extraction (pdf.rs) and a DOCX extractor (docx.rs) with no caller, while pipeline.rs has no content-type router (every body is charset-decoded and run through readability), so PDF is parsed only by the answer fetcher (answer.rs:835-839) even though docs/GAP.md:85 and PARITY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:129 claim PDF routing and DOCX as shipped; there is no page classification, OCR, page selection, parser semaphore or time budget (extract_text is synchronous with only a 25 MiB size check), no per-org parse cache, and docx.rs reads document.xml with an unbounded read_to_string after only a compressed-size check. Quarry never calls the Model Plane layout route (/v1/ai/documents/layout, ZDR-gated, accepts a pages selector), and the Model Plane manifest grants quarry-edge no model call at all. The item also misses that Ingestion Plane's imports-core (Python) already ships production PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX parsers with a zip-bomb budget (member, part, total and tree-part caps, read deadline) and an ephemeral bytes-in /api/v1/import/extract endpoint (1 MB input, 60k-char output cap).

reuse: pdf.rs extract_text/extract_headings and answer.rs is_pdf (lift into a shared content-type router; F-t2-009)
imports-core parsers.py zip budget constants and routing, or its /api/v1/import/extract endpoint, instead of new roxmltree/calamine code written from scratch
Model Plane /v1/ai/documents/layout with its pages selector and ZDR gate
page_extract::model_hop_allowed and PrivacyPolicy::guard_third_party_processing for the OCR hop
SearchCache-style org-scoped Redis keys for the parse cache
verevon.constraints: Quarry to Model Plane calls are all granted:false in the cross-plane manifest and the org-bound metered model path is a separate unfinished design (DEF-QB-T17-PART2), so OCR routing needs a new feature switch, a manifest row plus registry grant and a metered path before it can run. ZDR: model_hop_allowed currently refuses every Model hop under ZDR, so a ZDR-eligible OCR route needs an explicit exception design (typed refusal otherwise), and the parse cache must be disabled under ZDR. Data Plane owns retrieval and embeddings: Quarry returns markdown or blocks only. imports-core is Ingestion Plane too but refuses ZDR for durable imports; only its ephemeral extract endpoint is ZDR-compatible.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Sequence it: (1) shared content-type router with the native lopdf path in pipeline.rs (S, F-t2-009), run in spawn_blocking with page and time budgets because extract_text is synchronous; (2) Office formats: decide by ADR between porting imports-core's budget design (member/part/total caps, deadline) into quarry-transform and calling imports-core's ephemeral extract endpoint (needs larger limits and service auth), and in either case do not wire docx.rs before it has an inflate budget; (3) OCR via the Model Plane layout route only after the manifest row, grant and ZDR exception exist; (4) per-org content-hash cache keyed (org, sha256) and skipped under ZDR. Fix the stale docs claims in the same change.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. Split into S (router + native PDF), M (OCR route with grant and ZDR design) and M (Office parsers with budgets, reuse imports-core).
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real, but the item must say PDF is already extracted in the answer fetcher, that imports-core already has budgeted Office parsers to reuse, that DOCX is unwired and unbounded, and that OCR needs a Quarry to Model Plane grant that does not exist.

items.title: Agent presence and run control UX: animated cursor and target highlight, real annotation markers, steer/queue follow-ups, needs-attention notifications
items.summary: Build one overlay layer in BrowserChrome that maps Quarry AX-ref rects (scaled to the frame) onto the frame stream. Use it for (a) an agent cursor and element highlight driven by the target rect that Quarry includes in the pre-action event, without blocking execution on a UI acknowledgement, and (b) an annotation mode where the user marks an element, text or region and the markers stay anchored to AX refs; a batch is sent to chat as one message carrying role, name, ref or selector, rect, nearby text, frame path and an optional screenshot. As an immediate small step, stop advertising the 'annotate' capability and remove the hard-coded placeholder anchor until this is real. || Include the target box/point in Quarry step 'started' events and render an animated cursor plus target highlight over the live frame in BrowserChrome (presentation-only, reduced-motion aware). Add steer and queue commands for browser runs with idempotency keys and expectedTurnId, consumed by execution-core at step boundaries, reusing Quarry's seq replay. Have Application Plane notification-core emit needs_approval, completed and failed notifications from run events.
items.whyItMatters: It makes agent actions legible and trustworthy during co-browsing, gives users a precise way to tell the agent what to change or extract, and removes a visibly fake feature: the gateway advertises annotate while the UI shows one fixed marker. || Users can follow and trust what the AI does in the shared browser, redirect it mid-run ('no, the second result') without restarting, and leave a run in the background until approval is needed. These are the daily-use expectations once the loop is live.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (annotation iab-060/061; agent cursor automation-and-safety-063)
others: Codex in-app browser (CI085: every pointer command first moves a host-drawn cursor and waits for an arrival ack) for presentation; Aside (AA036: WS envelopes with idempotent commands, steer{interrupt, expectedTurnId}, queue, afterSeq resume) for run control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources (Codex) for both; unique. || Each 1 of 3 sources (unique): cursor Codex only, steering Aside only, notifications Aside only
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Cursor: moveMouse assigns a sequence number, pushes {moveSequence, x, y} to the host overlay, and waits for a cursor-arrived ack (timeout 1500 ms) before dispatching the click. Annotation: comment payload {pageUrl, framePath, selectedText or targetDescription, targetRole, targetName, targetSelector, targetPath, targetRect, nearbyText, additionalSelections, marker point, screenshot}; overlay modes browse and comment; batch mode collects several comments before sending. Verevon: Quarry emits the target point from the AX-ref bbox before executing and may wait a short fixed delay instead of an ack. || Merged items add: Cursor: before each pointer action the executor emits {moveSequence, x, y}; the UI animates an overlay and acks. Steering: command {id (idempotency), type, expectedTurnId}; the server acks and emits events with monotonically increasing per-run seq; steer injects a user message at the next step boundary (optionally interrupting the in-flight step); queue appends to the run inbox. State changes publish notifications that the task list and approvals subscribe to.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:1822 (AI rationale bubble and step badges only)
verevonToday.gap: Annotation is a placeholder while the capability is advertised, and there is no agent cursor or element highlight; only a rationale bubble per step exists. || Quarry has typed agent-event SSE with ?from_seq replay and the gateway exposes pause/resume/stop, but the UI shows only an AI rationale bubble and step badges (no cursor or highlight), no mid-run steering or queued follow-up for browser runs was found, and a grep of notification-core finds no browser-run event handling (SRC grep; absent as far as found).

items.approach: Frontend frame overlay (cursor animated to the target before the click lands, target highlight, annotation markers anchored to AX refs from F-t2-028); Model Plane run-control protocol (idempotent steer with expectedTurnId, queued follow-ups, replayable seq); Application Plane notification-core for attention notices that skip sessions the user is already watching. || Source detail: [R-t2-08-11] Ingestion Plane: include the target AX ref and rect in pre-action events (and the hit-test of R-t2-08-05 for user marks). Frontend Plane: overlay component with frame-scale mapping, annotation mode, batch send to chat; remove 'annotate' from the advertised capabilities until shipped. || [R-t2-09-09] Ingestion Plane: add target box/point to step 'started' events (no server-side ack; presentation only). Frontend Plane: Solid overlay for cursor and highlight over the scaled live frame. Model Plane: browser_run steer/queue commands picked up by execution-core at step boundaries, never bypassing a pending approval. Application Plane: notification-core consumes run events (needs_approval, completed, failed) and links back to the approval.
dependencies: F-t2-013 co-browsing (cursor presents best on a shared tab)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane + Model Plane + Application Plane
items.risks: Coordinate mismatch with scaled frames; anchors drift on dynamic pages (re-resolve by AX ref and fail visibly). || Overlay misalignment with scaled live frames; steering mid-action must not bypass pending approvals; notification noise (batch and rate-limit); ZDR: coordinates are not sensitive but notification text must not leak page content.

verevon.exactGap: Annotation is a stub: browser-session.ts:128-135 advertises 'annotate' and returns one hard-coded anchor at 7%/18%, BrowserChrome.tsx:1844-1857 renders it, the gateway also advertises 'annotate' (browser.rs:2578, 2700) and no UI code consumes the capability. There is no agent cursor or target highlight: BrowserChrome shows only the rationale bubble (1822-1842), execution-core's BrowserActionDispatched carries action_type, url and reason, Quarry's action.started payload is only {step, action}, and no geometry (bbox or rect) exists in Quarry's snapshot or accessibility contracts. Browser runs have pause/resume/stop only (execution-core wait_out_pause_or_cancel); chat-turn mid-run queueing exists (model-gateway queued_input.rs) but not inside the browser loop, and run_completed/run_failed notifications already exist through capability-core runwatch to notification-core (toggle in AgentRunConsole, not in the browser panel) while a needs_approval notification does not.
reuse: Model Plane run-event path: execution-core OrchestrationEventSink publishes BrowserActionDispatched, BrowserObservationReceived, ApprovalRequired, ActionDecided, Paused and Resumed into session-core, which the gateway streams on /api/v1/runs/:id/events with Last-Event-ID forwarding (chat/streams.rs:180-195). This is the replayable seq, not Quarry.
BrowserChrome overlay container and the ChatLiveRunPanel that already mounts BrowserChrome in compact mode for watched chat runs (chat-run-watch.ts, ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx).
execution-core wait_out_pause_or_cancel (browser_agent.rs:972-1011) as the between-actions boundary where a steer or queued follow-up can be consumed.

model-gateway queued_input.rs design (classify-and-continue pause text, 3 messages and 2000 chars caps, tenant+user bound registry) and the /v1/invoke/:id/queue contract as the template for browser-run steering.

capability-core runwatch consumer plus notification-core types modelplane.run_completed and modelplane.run_failed (migration 013, handlers.go allowlist) and the AgentRunConsole RunWatchToggle; extend the same path with an approval-required type.
Existing approval cards in BrowserChrome (decide flow) and execution-core require_approval for the needs-attention state.
chromiumoxide AX nodes already carry backendDOMNodeId (chromiumoxide.rs:1165-1180) so rects can be fetched with a CDP box-model call when geometry is added.
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: the cursor and highlight must be presentation-only and must not gate execution on a UI ack; a steer or queued message may only change what the Model proposes next and must never bypass a pending approval (browser_events.rs:238 polls the approval). Queued input is refused for ZDR and waived tokens (http_routes.rs:823, require_non_zdr_durable_mutation), so steer/queue must keep that rule. Run events, seq and replay are Model Plane (session-core) concerns; notification-core only accepts a fixed allowlist per service principal (handlers.go:204-216), so a new notification type needs an allowlist entry and a channel-config migration. Notification text must not carry page content. Quarry's agent SSE ?from_seq is accepted but a no-op (agent_routes.rs:2700-2705) and the gateway does not proxy that stream, so the item's claim of reusing Quarry seq replay is wrong.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Ship the honesty fix first: remove 'annotate' from both capability lists (browser.rs:2578, 2700 and the browser-session.ts default) and drop the placeholder anchor (S, quick win). For the cursor, geometry does not exist yet: add an optional rect to Quarry's snapshot target or accessibility projection (CDP box model via backendDOMNodeId), have execution-core copy it into the BrowserActionDispatched event, and animate in BrowserChrome; do not describe this as AX-ref bbox already available. Build steer/queue in Model Plane (execution-core consuming at the existing pause boundary, idempotent ids, replay via session-core Last-Event-ID), not as a Quarry feature. For notifications, run_completed/failed already exist, so only surface the watch toggle in the browser or chat panel and add a needs_approval type to capability-core/notification-core (first confirm that durable browser AI runs emit RUN_COMPLETED on mp.v1.run.*.event like other runs; not verified).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall but it should be four separately shippable slices: annotate honesty fix (S), cursor/highlight incl. Quarry geometry (M-L), steer/queue in execution-core (M), needs_approval notification plus watch toggle (S-M). Completion notifications are already done.
verevon.verdictReason: Part of the item already exists (completion/failure notifications, pause/resume/stop control, chat-turn queued input) and the replay and bbox premises are wrong (Quarry agent SSE replay is a no-op, no geometry in Quarry contracts). The stub annotate marker and the missing cursor, browser-loop steering and approval notification are real. Reword to the corrected four slices.

items.title: Governed downloads and uploads: quarantined, tenant-scoped artifacts, a downloads drawer and hand-off to the Data Plane
items.summary: Turn on downloads in the Chromiumoxide driver: route downloads to a per-session quarantine directory and register the result as a tenant-scoped Quarry artifact (size and type limits, hash, malware-scan hook), withheld under ZDR. User-initiated downloads under takeover are allowed; agent downloads need the existing single-use sensitive download_ref child grant, and unsolicited downloads are cancelled. Emit started, in_progress, complete, failed and canceled events into the timeline, and add a downloads drawer in BrowserChrome with 'Save to Knowledge'. || Flip on the already-implemented artifact-only upload/download path in the Quarry driver (the capability flag is false today). Store downloads as Quarry artifacts with checksum, MIME sniffing and malware scan, and hand them to the Data Plane through its ingest API; allow uploads only from artifacts the run's owner can read, each behind a one-shot approval grant bound to the exact artifact and frame.
items.whyItMatters: Agents and users need to fetch PDFs and exports into Knowledge, and the authority model already exists in the contracts and the broker. Without it any page that serves a file is a dead end. || Agents that research or file paperwork need PDFs/CSVs and form uploads. items.title: Parallel batch scrape with shared options, idempotent creation and wait-or-resume
items.summary: Make /v1/batch fan out under a concurrency bound (min of maxConcurrency, the org limit and the per-host AIMD scheduler) with shared scrapeOptions, appendToId, an invalid-URL report and the shared status/errors/cancel routes. Accept a client Idempotency-Key on crawl/batch/schedule creation (payload hash, response replay, 409 on key reuse with a different payload) and add a bounded wait_ms that returns a resumable 408 'processing_continues' response with Retry-After instead of failing or duplicating work.
items.whyItMatters: Sequential batches are a visible slowness for ingestion and for agents that want to read N search hits at once. Retries from the gateway or the Model Plane must not double-start crawls, and slow OCR/PDF/browser work should stop failing at gateway timeouts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-007 batch with maxConcurrency/append/ignoreInvalidURLs; fc-028 processing_continues 408 contract)
others: Apify (run-sync with a wait window, DOC)
Codex in-app browser (declares bulk content but refuses it)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: batch scrape: 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Codex declared only), common; sync-with-wait and resume: 2 of 4 (Apify, Firecrawl), common; idempotency: 1 of 4 and Firecrawl's is a negative example
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: POST /batch {urls[], scrapeOptions, maxConcurrency, appendToId?, webhook?} returns a job id and separately lists invalid URLs; status/errors/cancel reuse the crawl controllers. For waiting: key every heavy request by (org, request hash), wait up to the timeout, then return 408 {code:TIMEOUT, details:{state:'processing_continues', jobId, retryAfterSeconds}} with Retry-After so an identical retry re-attaches to the same job. For idempotency, copy the shape not Firecrawl's guard: store (org, route, key) -> {payloadHash, status, responseBody}, replay on match, 409 on mismatch, expire after 24 h.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/routes.rs:134 and :670-726 (batch handoff: urls, ingest, zdr only)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/resource_routes.rs:471-474 (edge generates a fresh Idempotency-Key per forwarded control call)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/knowledge/quarry.rs:386 and :423 (curated batch crawl of up to 200 deduped URLs with SSE progress)
verevonToday.gap: Batch has no per-batch options, maxConcurrency, append, invalid-URL report or status/cancel route; public crawl/batch do not accept a client idempotency key (the generated key only protects edge-to-control retries); scrape is sync-only and crawl/batch are async-only with no wait option, no processing_continues contract and no re-attach on retry.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane. Orchestrator: turn the BatchWF loop into bounded child activities honouring maxConcurrency and the existing per-host scheduler, accept ScrapeOptions (R-t2-01-01), add appendToId and invalidUrls. Edge: read Idempotency-Key from callers and forward it instead of a random one; control already dedupes on (org_id, key, route), so add payload-hash comparison and response replay and scope strictly by org. Add wait_ms to crawl/batch/extract with in-flight dedupe on (org, request hash, zdr posture) and the 408 resumable envelope; gateway and Model Plane clients honour Retry-After. ZDR jobs cannot keep results for re-attach beyond the request.
items.risks: Parallel fan-out must still respect per-host politeness and org concurrency budgets; request-hash dedupe must include org and ZDR posture so it never crosses tenants; replayed responses must not retain ZDR content.

verevon.exactGap: /v1/batch is a durable handoff that forwards only urls, ingest, org and user (routes.rs:669-716) to BatchJobWF, which processes URLs in a plain sequential loop (workflows.go:359-381) with no per-batch options, maxConcurrency, append, invalid-URL report or cancel handlers, and the edge exposes no per-job status or cancel route (only /v1/:kind/jobs and /v1/jobs/:id/events, routes.rs:192, 232); durable batch and crawl jobs are refused under ZDR (routes.rs:563-583). The crawl and batch handoff sends no Idempotency-Key at all (handoff.rs:26-82); the random keys at resource_routes.rs:471-474 and schedule_routes.rs:164-171 belong to other forwarded mutations, while control's createJob already returns the existing job for a repeated (org, key) (resources.go:395-450) but its unique index is on idempotency_key alone (migration 007) and the generic route-level handler is a no-op placeholder (cycle23.go:436). There is no wait_ms, no 408 processing_continues contract and no re-attach; scrape is sync-only and crawl or batch are async-only.
reuse: Shared HostScheduler (per-host AIMD) and AutoscaledPool, already applied inside PageRunner for every page, so workflow-level fan-out stays politeness-bounded
Control createJob idempotency lookup and unique index (extend, do not replace)
CrawlJobWF pause, resume and cancel signal handlers as the model for batch
Edge /v1/:kind/jobs list and /v1/jobs/:id/events routes
Gateway curated batch crawl (200 URL cap, SSRF-normalised, SSE progress) as the first consumer
Model Plane model-gateway idempotency registry pattern (claim, replay, in-flight) as a reference
verevon.constraints: Idempotency keys and request-hash dedupe must be scoped by org: the unique index on idempotency_key alone makes two orgs choosing the same client key collide at insert, so namespace keys by org or change the index to (org_id, idempotency_key). ZDR: durable jobs are refused under ZDR, so wait-or-resume and replay apply only to non-ZDR orgs and must never store ZDR content. Fan-out must respect per-host and org concurrency budgets (already in PageRunner) and keep billing semantics (one BATCH_URL meter event with quantity = URL count at handoff). Ownership stays in the Ingestion Plane (edge, control, orchestrator); the gateway still SSRF-normalises URLs before calling.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder. (1) S quick win: accept Idempotency-Key on /v1/crawl, /v1/batch and schedules, namespace it by org, forward it as a header from handoff.rs (there is no random key to replace on the crawl or batch path), change migration 007's unique index to (org_id, idempotency_key), and add a payload-hash check with 409 on mismatch in createJob. (2) M: make BatchJobWF bounded-parallel (workflow.Go with a semaphore or child workflows), accept ScrapeOptions from F-t2-005, add appendToId and an invalid-URL report, and add the pause and cancel handlers CrawlJobWF has; per-host politeness is already enforced in PageRunner. (3) M to L: add per-job get and cancel routes on the edge (F-t2-017) before any wait_ms, then a 408 processing_continues envelope for non-ZDR durable jobs only.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall: roughly S for idempotency, M for parallel batch, M for status/cancel and wait-or-resume.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is confirmed, but the idempotency description is wrong for crawl and batch (the handoff sends no key and the random keys serve other mutations), the DB index is not org-scoped, ZDR removes the re-attach case, and per-host politeness is already enforced in PageRunner. Reword and split the S idempotency fix out as a quick win.

items.title: Sitemap, robots and index-assisted crawl discovery, plus URL canonicalisation and redirect de-duplication
items.summary: Extract the /v1/map sitemap code into a shared Rust discovery module that also reads robots.txt Sitemap lines, gzip sitemaps, scoped, root and registrable-domain sitemaps, and URLs already in the local index or tracked sources. Call it from crawl kickoff behind a sitemap include|only|skip option, seeding the durable frontier through the scope filter. In the same enqueue path add a canonical_url unique_key and a post-redirect check so the same page is not crawled twice.
items.whyItMatters: Docs and product sites are Verevon's main knowledge sources; sitemap seeding makes crawls complete and cheap, and reusing the local index makes re-crawls incremental. Canonicalisation prevents duplicate documents reaching the Data Plane, which improves retrieval quality and cost.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (parallel sitemap kickoff, index seeding, URL permutation dedupe with redirect race handling)
others: Apify (sitemap discovery with common-name probing)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Sitemap discovery: 2 of 4 sources, table-stakes; URL canonicalisation: 1 of 4, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Kickoff scrapes the start page then queues sitemap jobs for every candidate in parallel (3 concurrent, 25 nested max): robots Sitemap lines, <scope dir>/sitemap.xml, /sitemap.xml and the registrable-domain sitemap (plus /sitemap.txt). It parses urlset versus sitemapindex, decompresses .gz, recurses to a cap, filters each URL through the same scope filter and enqueues at a lower priority than seed links. Map is the union of index, sitemaps and optional site search, with redirects resolved, robots filtered and results ranked by query similarity. For dedupe, normalise (drop fragment but keep hash routes, optionally strip query, lowercase host); compute permutations (http/https x www x trailing slash x index.html) and lock the canonical one in a visited set before enqueue; after fetch lock the redirect target and abort if another job holds it. The limit counts the unique set.

verevonToday.gap: Live crawl has no sitemap seeding. /v1/map reads /sitemap.xml plus up to 5 nested indexes and seed links, but not robots Sitemap lines, gzip or index-assisted discovery. Crawl dedupes on the exact link string only (visited map in workflows.go); there is no canonicalisation or redirect reconciliation.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane. Move sitemap parsing into a shared quarry-runtime discovery module used by both map_routes.rs and crawl kickoff; add robots Sitemap lines, gzip, nested cap and URL cap with streaming into the frontier. Add canonical_url (unique_key) in quarry-core, a unique index on (queue/crawl id, unique_key) in the Postgres frontier, and a post-redirect check in run_page; keep aggressive normalisation (query stripping, index.html folding) opt-in per crawl. Seed from tracked sources and the local Tantivy index so repeat crawls only fetch new or changed URLs. Build after R-t2-05-01 so every sitemap URL passes the scope filter.
dependencies: unique_key column on the Postgres frontier
items.risks: Huge sitemaps; cap URLs and stream. Over-aggressive normalisation merges distinct pages on query-driven sites, so keep it opt-in.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-05-07] apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/ROADMAP.md Phase 5 (sitemap, robots) and docs/PLAN.md:240 (ignoreSitemap, sitemapOnly)

verevon.exactGap: The substrate exists: quarry-transform parses sitemap urlset and index documents and robots Sitemap lines (robots.rs:14, 80-81), and /v1/map (map_routes.rs:132-250) already reads origin /sitemap.xml plus up to 5 nested indexes and the seed page's links, but ignores robots Sitemap lines and gzip. Live crawl has no sitemap seeding or scope options (CrawlRequest is only url, max_pages, max_depth, ingest and zdr, routes.rs:533-553) and both crawl workflows dedupe on the exact link string (workflows.go:417; durable frontier request_id is sha256(run+url), workflows.go:617-620), with no canonical key or post-redirect check; the Rust CrawlFrontier that has scope, include/exclude and fragment normalisation is scaffolding that the live path does not call.
reuse: quarry-transform sitemap.rs parser and robots.rs (sitemaps field already collected) as the shared discovery inputs; map_routes.rs merge_and_scope for host scoping and dedup.

Rust CrawlFrontier (crawl_frontier.rs): seed host scope, include/exclude patterns, CrawlDenialReason, fragment normalisation, hreflang dedupe. Wire its scope filter in front of the durable frontier rather than rewriting it (this is the F-t2-016 scope filter).
Postgres frontier idempotency: ON CONFLICT (org_id, request_id) DO NOTHING (postgres_queue.rs:248-256) and the edge enqueue route (queue_routes.rs:138-155).
The existing UI flow /crawl/discover (quarry /v1/map) then CrawlPagePicker then /v1/batch, which already uses sitemap discovery for user-selected crawls.
run_page output (final_url, links, fingerprint; routes.rs:776-830) for post-redirect reconciliation.
verevon.constraints: All Ingestion Plane. Every sitemap-discovered URL is attacker-controlled, so it must pass the same security preflight and scope filter before enqueue, and robots Disallow must still apply (map_routes.rs applies the robots allow-filter and quarry_security::heur::check). /v1/crawl and /v1/batch are refused under ZDR (routes.rs:555-575), so none of this applies to ZDR callers. Do not pass thousands of discovered URLs through Temporal workflow input or history: enqueue them into the durable frontier from an activity. Aggressive normalisation (query stripping, index.html folding) must stay opt-in because it merges distinct pages on query-driven sites.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not add a canonical_url unique_key column: the Postgres frontier already enforces uniqueness on (org_id, request_id), so derive request_id from the canonical URL (durableFrontierRequestID in workflows.go:617-620, or canonicalise in the edge enqueue handler using the Rust normaliser) and keep the original URL as payload. Order the work by user value: first make /v1/map read robots Sitemap lines, gzip sitemaps and a configurable nested cap (S), because the SPA discovery flow depends on it; then add a discovery activity that seeds the durable frontier behind a sitemap include|only|skip option, after the scope filter; then post-redirect reconciliation using final_url. Seeding from the local Tantivy index is a separate later step.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. Canonical key via request_id and the /v1/map improvements are S; crawl seeding with scope filtering is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Live crawl really has no sitemap seeding or canonicalisation, but /v1/map and the sitemap and robots parsers already exist, so the item should present itself as extending them. Keep with the corrected approach (reuse request_id uniqueness, improve /v1/map first, wire CrawlFrontier scope).

items.title: Agent web toolset: content-hydrated search, next-step hints, citations, and Quarry jobs as approval-gated tools with cost estimates
items.summary: Let /v1/search accept scrapeOptions (bounded top-N, total time budget, shared fan-out) and give the Model Plane web_search tool a with_content flag so one call returns search hits plus page content. Add opt-in hints[] to success responses of scrape/search/map, computed only from local signals (truncated, empty, blocked, SERP URL), extending the existing next_actions field. Add a Model Plane tool-doc registry with a server-side 'docs read' check before high-risk browser tools, and attach stable source ids to tool output so answers cite them, with an org domain allow/deny policy honoured on service-token fetches. || Register Quarry crawl, map, batch-extract, pack runs and promoted procedures as capabilities in capability-core and as Model Plane tools, with parameter schemas taken from the pack schemas. The approval card shows an estimated cost and page cap before anything runs, and new service-principal scopes gate each route. A later phase exposes the same registry through mcp-bridge as an off-by-default, org-gated MCP facade with output-token caps.
items.whyItMatters: Agents get N pages in one call instead of search plus N fetches, waste fewer turns on blind retries, and use risky browser tools more safely. Org admins can restrict which domains agents fetch and answers stay traceable to sources. || 'AI proposes, Quarry executes' is only real if the Model can propose more than two web tools. Today the chat agent can search and fetch one URL, but crawl, extract-with-schema, packs and procedures are not agent-reachable, so the Model falls back to repeated single fetches.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-017 search with scrapeOptions; fc-029 agent_hints) and Codex in-app browser (IAB-001 documentation-read gate)
others: Apify RAG Web Browser (DOC; raw-http vs browser choice, time budget)
Aside (aside-agent-control 040: network permission hook and citation tags)
Apify (natural-language runner with confirmation before paid runs)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: search with content: 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify), common; hints and doc gating: 2 of 4 (Firecrawl, Codex), differentiator; citations with per-URL permission: 1 of 4 (Aside), unique || 2 of 4 sources; differentiator (the two sources use different mechanisms)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hydration: run search, over-fetch to survive filtering, scrape the top N concurrently with shared options inside a total time budget, attach formats per result. Hints: opt-in header, rules over locally computed signals with templates under 500 characters, max 32 rules, never raw page text, failure returns the original body. Doc gate: a registry with modes model|included|lookup and a guard that refuses a gated command until the session fetched the required doc id. Aside: tool results carry source ids and a policy hook evaluates {type:'network', url} before each fetch. || Merged items add: Apify: intent, then search the tool catalog (quality ranked), fill the input schema, show a confirmation with estimated cost, run, summarize the dataset; full-permission and rental tools are excluded. Codex: a minimal MCP server (js, js_reset, turn_ended) with surfaces selected by env (browser, computer or both; startup fails otherwise), tools.js.output_token_limit 25000, a startup timeout and enabled = false until the host turns it on.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/answer_routes.rs:44 and :145 (search-then-fetch answer pipeline, synthesis needs the Model Plane grant)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/api_error.rs:24-25 and :46-58 (next_actions exists, only on error paths)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/web_tools.rs:133 and :152 (read-only web_search/web_fetch tools, zdr in request bodies)
verevonToday.gap: /v1/search returns snippets and chunks but cannot attach full scraped content per hit; success responses carry no hints; no doc-read gate for high-risk browser tools; web_search/web_fetch have no org-level per-URL policy at tool level and the citation convention for web_fetch was not verified; /v1/answer synthesis is blocked by the manifest grant (R-t2-01-04). || SRC: the chat agent's web tools are web_search (POST /v1/search) and web_fetch (POST /v1/extract) plus two aliases, with the scopes search:read and extract:read granted to execution-core on the Quarry audience; browser.observe only observes an existing run. Crawl, map, batch, extract-with-schema, presets, packs and procedures are not tools and carry no cost estimate. Risk-classified human approvals exist for browser actions and provider writes (stronger than Apify's single confirmation). Verevon consumes MCP servers (registry, OAuth, mcp-bridge) but exposes none; Quarry's backlog defers an MCP server because Verevon is the client.

items.approach: Model Plane execution-core web_tools: search with scrapeOptions hydration, bounded next-step hints on success paths (extend next_actions), grouped citations; Quarry crawl/batch/monitor jobs exposed as approval-gated tools with a cost estimate before launch. The off-by-default MCP facade from R-t2-06-07 moves to F-t2-064. || Source detail: [R-t2-01-10] Ingestion Plane: SearchRequest.scrapeOptions reusing the batch fan-out from R-t2-01-06 and ScrapeOptions from R-t2-01-01, with ZDR and budgets applied to every hydrated fetch; hints[] emitted from local signals in scrape/search/map handlers. Model Plane execution-core web_tools.rs: with_content flag, source ids on tool output, tool-doc registry plus a server-side docs-read check ahead of upload/download/dialog tools (these already need one-shot broker approval grants, so this is additive); org domain policy read from Control Plane and enforced both in the tool and on service-token scrapes, with denials logged. || [R-t2-06-07] Model Plane: add capability ids (for example cap.web.crawl, cap.pack.run) to capability-core with Allow/Deny/Ask and risk levels; add execution-core tool definitions that map to Quarry routes using the pack and procedure schemas; the approval card shows estimated cost (R-t2-06-01 caps plus R-t2-06-09 pricing) and page limits. Control Plane: add service-principal scopes (for example crawl:write, pack:run) to the auth-core policy contract. Quarry validates and executes. Phase 2: mcp-bridge adds a Quarry MCP facade (search, fetch, extract, browser.observe/act) that always obtains a BrowserBroker grant per session, caps output tokens, and is disabled unless the org policy (R-t2-06-02) allows it.
dependencies: F-t2-022 policy and grants (required for the MCP facade)
items.risks: Cost amplification (N scrapes per search); prompt injection if hints ever echo page text (never include raw text); over-restrictive domain policies degrade answers; hint drift versus real behaviour. || Unbounded crawls proposed by the model, so require a budget and an approval for every non-trivial job. An MCP facade that talks to Quarry directly with broad tokens would bypass the gateway authority path; it must go through BrowserBroker grants and ZDR rules.

verevon.exactGap: Confirmed missing: /v1/search has no scrapeOptions and execution-core web_search sends only {query, limit, zdr}; success responses carry no hints (next_actions exists only on the error envelope); agent-path tool output has no source ids; there is no org web-domain policy on web_search or web_fetch; no crawl, map, batch, extract-with-schema, pack or procedure tool or capability id exists (cap.tool.http covers only web_search and web_fetch); and nothing produces a cost-estimate approval (the COST approval kind is mapped but never created). Understated by the item: the chat path in model-gateway already has freshness and narrowest-tool guidance in its web_search description, numbered citations with a Sources tab, untrusted-data labelling of tool results and Data Plane suggested_next_tools hints; Quarry /v1/answer already runs search then full-page fetch with ZDR handling; and the Auth Core grant of search:read and extract:read to execution-core is in the policy contract. The 'Quarry MCP' names in execution-core (web.search, web.read, browser.observe, browser.act) are in-process aliases, not an MCP server, so the off-by-default facade is still unbuilt (tracked as F-t2-064).

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: crawl, batch and pack tools must be approval-gated with budgets and page caps enforced in Quarry as well as shown in the card; a displayed cost estimate is advisory. Service-principal scopes are Control Plane (auth-core), widened deliberately with no wildcard, and the contract test fails if a grant widens. Org domain policy would be Control-owned (none exists; Space allow_domains appears only in tests) and must be enforced in Quarry for service-token fetches too, or a tool-side check is bypassable. ZDR: hydrated fetches inherit zdr; hints are computed from local signals and never echo page text (prompt injection). Hydration multiplies spend, and agent paths are deliberately free-chain only (web_tools.rs).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split. (A) Search, hints and citations (M): implement hydration by reusing the answer pipeline's fetch fan-out behind a bounded scrape option; emit success-path hints with the retrieval_metadata.suggested_next_tools pattern (including the advertised-tool guard) instead of extending next_actions; give agent-path web tools numbered source ids by reusing the chat citation machinery. Rewriting the one-line execution-core descriptions and adding a conditional prompt snippet is S and needs no docs-read registry. (B) Quarry job tools (L): crawl, map and batch as approval-gated tools with caps and, only once a cost source exists, an estimated-cost approval; org domain policy as a separate Control item. Drop the docs-read gate (browser.act is closed-schema, approval-gated and grant-checked already) and keep the MCP facade in F-t2-064.
verevon.effortNote: The item says M but bundles hydration, hints, citations, a docs gate, org domain policy, new capability ids and scopes, a cost-estimate approval and Quarry job tools. (A) alone is M; (B) is L.
verevon.verdictReason: The main gaps are real, but the chat path already has parts of the proposal (guidance, citations, untrusted labelling, a hint mechanism), the doc-read gate is low value given closed-schema typed actions, and the bundle is undersized. Reword and split into search-side and job-side items.

items.title: URL-aware planner guidance: site skills, integration-corev2 provider capability hints by domain, driver capability matrix
items.summary: Three small changes in one pass. (a) Replace the one-line web_search and web_fetch descriptions with narrowest-tool-first routing and freshness guidance (and the escalation path to crawl or browser) as tool descriptions plus a built-in 'web access' org skill. (b) Add GET /v1/drivers/{id}/capabilities to quarry-edge (driver by capability matrix with one-line descriptions) so execution-core builds the browser tool schema at grant time and offers a describe-capability tool. (c) Add url_patterns and an optional snapshot_scope to org agent skills so site playbooks inject when the current Quarry session URL matches. || Make integration-corev2 publish a versioned, machine-readable operation catalog (provider, operation, isWrite, params schema, provider domains) and have Model Plane load it instead of the hard-coded CATALOG. When a Quarry observation lands on a host that maps to a provider the org has connected, offer that provider's matching read/write actions for the next step (or a "connect this provider" suggestion card when no connection exists) instead of brittle UI clicking. Cap the hint to a few operations to avoid tool-list bloat.
items.whyItMatters: Cheap, measurable gains in tool choice: fewer proposals that the driver cannot execute (fewer Quarry rejections), smaller prompts, less spend, and more reliable runs on the sites customers use most. All of it informs the Model; Quarry still decides. || When the agent is on a GitHub, Meta, LinkedIn, Google or Shopify page it can switch to a governed API action: faster, cheaper, auditable, with approvals and idempotency already in place and no sensitive browser grant. It directly reduces browser load and risk and ties the two planes together at low cost.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (capability registry with per-backend support), Firecrawl (endpoint-selection skills) and Aside (URL-triggered site skills)
others: Firecrawl
Aside
Firecrawl (scrape/search returns provider tools matched by domain or semantic query; one execute endpoint)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources each for the three mechanisms; unique (together a differentiator) || 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex: the API description marks each member unsupportedByDefaultIn [backends], the agent calls capabilities.list() for {id, one line} and fetches documentation only on demand, disabled ids are not registered, and the runtime is transport-agnostic (REA: no Electron code in the parsed runtime scripts). Firecrawl: an umbrella skill plus per-endpoint skills tell agents which endpoint to use, narrowest first, kept separate from generated parameter docs. Aside: SKILL.md frontmatter {name, description, autoInject.keywords, autoInject.url, siteSpecific}; 16 site skills scope page snapshots with selectors; matched site skills are injected (bounded) and the rest are listed by name. || Merged items add: Catalog entries {provider, capability, description, inputSchema, price, domains[]}; discovery matches the URL host to a provider (or does semantic search over descriptions) and returns data.tools with matchedBy domain|semantic and matchedUrls; execution is a single endpoint taking [{provider, capability, options}] with a caller request id; limited to 24 tools in a 10 s budget, three detail levels, and refused under ZDR because it calls an external exchange. Verevon keeps discovery internal so ZDR is unaffected.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: web tool descriptions are one sentence each with no routing, freshness or escalation guidance. Org agent skills (session-core agent_skills with name, trigger_keywords and content) are matched by keyword overlap against the run goal at run start, at most 3 injected under a size budget; there is no URL-pattern trigger, no tab-aware injection and no snapshot scoping. Drivers declare eight deny-by-default capability booleans and gate actions fail-closed, but the matrix is only a human-readable doc (DRIVER_MATRIX.md) and not an endpoint the Model Plane reads; whether browser planner prompts adapt per driver was not verified. OpenAPI covers 46 of about 75 routes (baseline). || The agent sees a static curated operation list for connections the org already has. There is no domain-to-provider matching from browsed URLs, no input schemas in an IC-served catalog (operations are string switch arms, so no declarative registry exists), and no suggestion to connect a provider when the agent browses its site.

items.approach: Model Plane: URL-pattern site skills on top of session-core skills (Aside SKILL.md pattern), routing guidance and the driver capability matrix fed to the planner; Ingestion Plane integration-corev2 serves its action catalog with schemas and provider domains so the planner can offer a governed API action or a connect-this-provider suggestion when the browsed host matches. Bound the hints with a tool-selection budget. || Source detail: [R-t2-06-08] Model Plane (execution-core): rewrite the tool descriptions in agent.rs and ship a built-in 'web access' skill; add url_patterns and snapshot_scope fields to AgentSkill (session-core proto and ListAgentSkills) and match against the current Quarry session URL when browser.observe runs; ship 3 to 5 first-party site skills for the sites customers use most. Ingestion Plane: expose GET /v1/drivers/{id}/capabilities (from BrowserDriverCapabilities plus the allowed action set) and complete OpenAPI so parameter docs can be generated; execution-core shapes the browser tool list from it at grant time and adds describe_capability. || [R-t2-10-03] Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2) + Model Plane (execution-core). IC: add Domains []string to providers.Provider and a declarative operation registry in internal/actions (name, isWrite, params schema) that the Execute switch and a new GET /internal/catalog endpoint both read; version it. Model Plane execution-core: replace CATALOG with a cached IC catalog fetch per org, and add a host-to-provider matcher run on each browser observation (canonical registrable domain from the observation URL). Inject at most N matching operations as a "provider hint" in the next step, marking writes as approval-gated, or emit a connect-provider suggestion. Execution keeps using the existing named-operation path (execute_provider_action) with approvals, so no new write surface.
dependencies: IC declarative operation registry and catalog endpoint with schemas
Browser observations carrying the canonical URL/host to Model Plane (verify per step event)
Model Plane tool-selection budget so hints do not flood the prompt
items.risks: Skill text is operator-authored prompt content: keep it out of untrusted-web channels and inside the skill budget. Capability lists must stay in sync with driver reality, so generate them from the driver trait rather than writing them by hand. || Tool-list bloat degrading model choice (the CATALOG comment already warns); stale or wrong domain mappings pointing the agent at the wrong provider; showing connect suggestions for providers the org's policy disallows.

verevon.exactGap: Confirmed: execution-core's web_search and web_fetch descriptions are one sentence with no routing or escalation guidance and the system prompt has no web snippet (the chat path's web_search description does carry freshness and narrowest-tool guidance); org skills are keyword-matched against the run goal at run start (3 skills, 8000 characters) and AgentSkill has trigger_keywords plus a stored-but-unused trigger_file_patterns but no URL pattern and only user and background_review origins; and integration-corev2 has a coarse provider catalog (connect-time capabilities with read/write direction, no domains, no operation schemas) while execution-core uses a hard-coded CATALOG over a Go string switch. Corrected: driver capabilities are not only a human-readable doc, because POST /v1/agent/runs already accepts driver_requirements and returns driver_capabilities, execution_tier and execution_engine (documented in openapi.yaml) and quarry-edge gates actions fail-closed on them. The real gap is that neither execution-core nor the gateway reads those fields and there is no pre-run GET /v1/drivers route, so the Model's static browser.act schema never adapts to the driver.

reuse: the existing conditional SNIPPET_* mechanism in execution-core agent.rs as the measured home for routing guidance

AgentSkill.trigger_file_patterns plumbing (proto, session-core upsert, capability-core registry_apis, migrations) as the template for a URL-pattern field, plus the two existing injection paths (execution-core fetch_skill_context and model-gateway skills.rs)
