verevon.constraints: All hints inform the Model and Quarry or integration-corev2 still decide: provider actions keep the named-operation path with human approval for writes, so the hint adds no write surface. Tenant scope: hints may use only the run org's live connections, and a connect-this-provider suggestion must respect org policy on allowed providers. Skill text is operator-authored prompt content injected into model context: keep site skills out of untrusted-web channels and inside the 8000-character budget. Ownership: provider domains and operation schemas belong in integration-corev2 (Ingestion Plane) served as a versioned read-only catalog, not mirrored by hand in the Model Plane. ZDR: host-to-provider matching uses the observed URL only in memory and hints must not persist URLs. Tool-list bloat measurably degrades selection (the CATALOG comment and the measured prompt snippets), so cap hints and measure.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into four. (1) S: rewrite execution-core web_search and web_fetch descriptions and add a conditional web snippet beside the existing SNIPPET_* constants; do not ship it as a built-in org skill, because skills have no first-party origin and are matched on goal keywords. (2) S: forward the already-returned driver_capabilities and execution_tier from run start into the observation or tool result the Model sees (optionally prune browser.act variants) instead of building GET /v1/drivers/{id}/capabilities. (3) M: url_patterns on AgentSkill mirroring trigger_file_patterns end to end, matched on the observed URL when browser.observe runs, keeping both injection paths in step. (4) L: an integration-corev2 versioned operation catalog (declarative registry replacing the Execute switch) with provider domains, then replace execution-core's CATALOG and add the host-to-provider hint; start with a small hand-maintained domain map for the already-curated providers.
verevon.effortNote: Item said M. M holds only for (1) to (3); (4) is L because integration-corev2 actions are a large string switch with no declarative registry.
verevon.verdictReason: The driver-matrix endpoint is based on a wrong premise (capabilities are already returned at run start), the web guidance is half-present in the chat path, and a built-in web-access skill does not fit the skill model. Reword into S quick wins, an M site-skill item and an L provider-catalog item.

items.title: Hermetic browser and scrape evals in CI through the production tool contract, with injection and ZDR fixtures and per-release scores
items.summary: Extend the existing in-process TestSite and lab/evals fixtures with prompt-injection pages and ZDR cases, add record/replay of driver HTTP and CDP exchanges (path-confined fixtures), and add a CI job that runs lab/evals on a labelled PR and after each deploy, writing the SCOREBOARD with the commit SHA. As a later increment on canary.rs, add a mirror-and-diff mode for non-ZDR, consenting, non-agent traffic. || Drive the existing browser benchmark corpus through the same path production uses (Model Plane browser.observe and act tools, BrowserBroker grant, quarry-edge agent routes) against recorded fixture sites, score task success, steps and cost, and publish the result per release in CI.
items.whyItMatters: It keeps parity claims honest and catches regressions in driver escalation, ZDR behaviour and prompt-injection handling before users do. The harness is already substantial, but every scoreboard suite is pending and CI does not run it. || Agent quality regressions are caught before release only if evals exercise the real contract. Quarry's scoreboard is all pending and the Python eval-lab targets model-gateway, so the browser agent is currently benchmarked in neither place end to end.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (controlled test site with e2e snips gated by environment, CI matrix over engine, proxy and queue backends, mock record/replay, evals on a PR hashtag and after deploy)
others: Firecrawl shadow traffic: sampled mirror or split to staging, skipped for ZDR and agent jobs, outputs compared asynchronously
Codex in-app browser (same runtime archives used by training and production)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique || 1 of 4 sources; unique (documentation only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Serve a fixture site in CI and run e2e tests through the gateway; record mode writes driver exchanges to JSON fixtures and replay serves them by name; a CI job runs evals on a labelled PR and after deploy. Mirror mode: with probability r and only for consenting non-ZDR tenants, enqueue a job to the candidate driver, compare markdown similarity and latency, and store the result in an experiments table. || Merged items add: The eval harness installs the same CI-published runtime version as production and drives the same tool contract against a training browser service, so scores are comparable across releases.

verevonToday.gap: A Rust eval harness exists (bakeoff, browser_benchmark, provider_matrix, release_matrix, web_rerank_gate) with 12 HTML fixtures and a local TestSite (landing, login, gated dashboard, search), but every scoreboard suite is pending, quarry-v2-ci.yml runs cargo test only (no lab/evals job), and there is no record/replay and no prompt-injection or ZDR fixture. Canary splitting and experiment tagging are shipped; there is no mirror-and-diff mode. || SRC: Quarry lab/evals has a browser benchmark, a deterministic test site and a release-matrix binary, but the scoreboard suites are all pending. The Python eval-lab runs selftests in CI and live evals only against model-gateway with credentials. Nothing drives Model Plane browser.observe/act against quarry-edge with fixtures, so it is not established that evals cover the production tool contract.

items.approach: [R-t2-07-10] Ingestion Plane: add injection and ZDR pages to TestSite and lab/evals/fixtures, add a record/replay layer for driver exchanges, and wire lab/evals into a GitHub workflow triggered by a PR label and by deploy, publishing SCOREBOARD automatically. Mirror mode in canary.rs is optional and follows once evals exist; it must skip ZDR and agent runs. || [R-t2-06-10] Ingestion Plane lab/evals: add a runner that starts quarry-edge with the test site and a stub BrowserBroker, replays recorded planner traces or a fixed small model through the Model Plane tool protocol, and emits task-success, steps and cost; add it to the quarry-v2 CI workflow as a non-live job and to a scheduled live job. Publish release_matrix output with the new scores; use recorded fixtures instead of live sites to avoid flakiness.
items.risks: Flaky live-site evals (run live evals only after deploy); mirroring doubles third-party load and needs consent and ZDR exclusion. || Flaky live-site benchmarks (use recorded fixtures); model cost for live evals; CI runner limits for Chromium (the quarry-v2 workflow already documents build instability).

verevon.constraints: Prompt-injection screening is a Model Plane duty (execution-core provenance.rs, model-gateway moderation/semantic screening), so a Quarry-only fixture can prove only that hostile text is returned unmodified; an injection eval must include the Model Plane render seam. ZDR fixtures should assert no artifact, cache, checkpoint or timeline writes. The quarry-v2 CI already documents Chromium-link disk crashes, so browser evals belong in a labelled or scheduled job, hermetic via TestSite and recorded fixtures, with live-model evals only after deploy. No cross-plane DB access: the harness talks to quarry-edge over HTTP like production.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Phase 0 (S): add a quarry-v2-ci job that runs quarry-eval, quarry-bakeoff and release_matrix and uploads scoreboard with the commit SHA. Phase 1 (M): make browser_agent_e2e hermetic (quarry-edge with the browser-agent feature plus a stub grant validator against TestSite, deterministic planner or recorded planner traces) and score success, steps and cost; add injection pages to TestSite and assert on the Model Plane screening verdict; add ZDR no-write assertions. Drop the canary mirror-and-diff clause: canary.rs and experiments.rs are unwired scaffolding, so it would be a separate feature. Correct the description: the 'browser benchmark corpus' is a preview-latency microbenchmark, not tasks.
verevon.effortNote: Phase 0 is S and phase 1 M; with record/replay and the production-contract harness the whole item is L, not M.
verevon.verdictReason: The harness pieces exist but nothing runs in CI and the item mislabels canary/experiments as shipped, the browser benchmark as a task corpus, and misses the existing ignored real e2e test and the ZDR tests; scope and effort need correcting.

items.title: Memory pollution guard for runs that ingested web or browser content (verify first)
items.summary: Mark a run or thread memory_mode=polluted when any web, browser or MCP tool result enters context. The session-core memory extraction (dreaming) and graph or memory writes then skip polluted runs or route them to a review queue, with user-confirmed promotion for research tasks. Reuse the existing ZDR memory-write suppression pattern as the enforcement point.
items.whyItMatters: It stops prompt injection from becoming persistent: poisoned memories and graph facts would affect every later session, a cross-session risk specific to an AI-first product with memory. It is small and high leverage next to the browser and web tools Verevon is adding.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (no_memories_if_mcp_or_web_search setting and a polluted thread memory mode)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Codex, SRC with medium confidence); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A flag set on the thread or run when a web, browser or MCP tool result is added to context; the memory extraction job checks it and either skips extraction or sends candidates to a review queue; optionally only user-confirmed memories are stored.

verevonToday.gap: The model gateway labels web results as data, not instructions, and web-only turns skip memory recall. extract_memory_candidates takes only role and content, extracts from user and assistant text, and a grep of the Model Plane finds no polluted or taint flag, so no guard on memory writes after web or browser tool use was found. Not verified: execution-core and Data Plane graph-write paths. ZDR already suppresses memory writes (ZDR_MEMORY_WRITE_SUPPRESSED), a ready pattern.

items.approach: Model Plane: execution-core and model-gateway set a taint flag on the run when web or browser tools return content; session-core dreaming and letta_adapter writes refuse or quarantine tainted runs; Data Plane enforces the same flag when ingesting agent-derived facts. Add a user-confirmed promotion path in the UI.
items.risks: A guard that is too strict disables useful memory from research tasks; offer user-confirmed promotion. The taint must survive resume and fleet child runs.

verevon.exactGap: No run, thread or memory row carries a web, browser or MCP taint: searches of Model Plane, Control Plane, Data Plane v2, the gateway and the SPA find no polluted/taint/memory_mode flag, and both write paths (execution-core execute_save_memory and session-core Dreaming upsert_agent_memory, which always writes review_state='accepted') never ask whether web content entered the run. What exists is mitigation, not a guard: the LLM extractor frames conversation as untrusted, tags inferred rows extractor:llm, strips pasted-document blocks, and Dreaming reads only user and assistant message rows (never tool results), but an assistant turn that paraphrases a poisoned page is still extracted and save_memory is deliberately low-risk and ungated. The ZDR suppression the item proposes to reuse is bound to the verified credential (MemoryRetention::of(caller)) so it cannot express a taint that appears mid-run, and review_state 'pending' exists in the schema but nothing writes or promotes it.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dream_extractor.rs:1-60 (module doc: Dreaming rows land as accepted and are injected into every later prompt; conversation treated as untrusted; extractor:llm tag; ZDR turns never reach messages)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dream_extractor.rs:109,552,616-640 (LLM_SOURCE_LINK; strip_document_blocks; render_window keeps only user and assistant turns)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dreaming.rs:1263-1290,1318-1330 (pending-message and context queries select roles user and assistant only; zdr_waived threads skipped)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dreaming.rs:1636-1690 (upsert_current_key inserts review_state 'accepted' with no taint input)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/migrations/0013_tool_audit_intents.sql:1-15 (per-run tool name and data_category rows exist in session-core)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/grpc.rs:4096-4150 (MemoryRetention derived from the verified caller; permits_external_memory_indexing)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/memory_grpc.rs:444-505,625-635 (index_memory has no taint or provenance input; external indexing gated by retention only)
apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/memory.proto:126-140 (IndexMemoryRequest fields: no provenance or taint)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/mod.rs:650-663,2172 (save_memory dispatch and execute_save_memory take no taint)

apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:314-332,4235-4240 (data_category marks mcp__ tools unclassified; save_memory description only asks the model not to save tool output)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/capability_policy.rs:796-808 (save_memory low risk, refused under ZDR before the gate)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/wiki_agent.rs:1-15 (wiki edits are proposals; tool not offered to the model, so no agent-derived Data Plane write path)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/tool_loop.rs:4469 (tool results labelled data, never instructions)

negative searches: no polluted/taint/memory_mode in Model Plane, Control Plane, Data Plane v2, gateway or SPA (only an unrelated flag in home-draft.ts); no Model Plane doc plans a memory pollution guard
reuse: agent_memory.review_state ('pending'|'accepted'|'rejected'|'expired') and the existing reads that already filter on 'accepted' (dreaming.rs:434), so a pending row is invisible to recall with no read-side change
MemoryRetention::permits_external_memory_indexing (grpc.rs:4147) as the model for 'keep the local row, do not mirror to Letta'; the waived-run behaviour is the closest existing analogue
threads.source_scope='conversation' and PendingMessage.conversation_only (dreaming.rs:223) as the existing thread-level extraction suppression
session_tool_audit_intents (run_id, tool, data_category) and the [data_category=.. tool=..] step prefix to derive taint inside session-core without a new execution-core signal
the extractor:llm source_links marker (dream_extractor.rs:109) for provenance in the memory-management surface
verevon.constraints: Memory is Model Plane (session-core/execution-core); Data Plane v2 has no agent-derived write path today, so the item's 'Data Plane enforces the same flag' clause has nothing to enforce. ZDR already prevents durable memory writes and Dreaming never sees ZDR turns, so the guard only concerns persistent runs; a quarantine must also stop the Letta semantic mirror because Letta reads in memory_grpc search/list are not filtered by review_state. Taint must be thread-window level, not only run level: Dreaming extracts from a window that includes up to 6 earlier consolidated messages and assistant turns that paraphrase web content. Only the memory owner may promote a quarantined memory and Space membership must not widen that.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not use the ZDR credential flag as the carrier: MemoryRetention is derived from the token fixed at issuance, while taint appears mid-run. (1) In execution-core, save_memory preflight marks or refuses the write when the run's own tool history contains web_search/web_fetch/web.*/browser.*/mcp__* calls (data_category already distinguishes them). (2) In session-core Dreaming, skip or write 'pending' for extraction windows whose thread has such tool steps, derived from session_tool_audit_intents/step records, and suppress the Letta mirror for them. (3) Ship skip-only first with no promotion UI; add the pending-review path later through the memory management surface. Remove the Data Plane and graph clauses until an agent-derived graph write path exists.
verevon.effortNote: Item said S. S holds for a skip-only first slice (execution-core preflight plus a Dreaming window filter); the pending-review path needs a new accept/reject RPC (none exists in memory.proto or memory_grpc.rs), Letta mirror suppression and a UI, which is M.
verevon.verdictReason: The guard is genuinely absent and worth building, but the carrier (credential-bound ZDR pattern), the Data Plane clause and the S estimate are wrong; reword to the thread-level taint approach with a skip-only first slice. Existing prompt-level and provenance mitigations should be mentioned so the document does not say memory is entirely unprotected.

items.title: Complete web-usage metering: browser metrics, outcome and surface attributes, price table and plan keys
items.summary: Phase A: add distinct usage metrics for browser steps and minutes, agent runs and extract/map (today extract and map are billed as search queries) with attributes {outcome, driver, llm_format, paid_provider, zdr, surface}, and a closed x-verevon-surface enum set by the gateway and Model Plane. Phase B: surface per-run usage in the ingestion run view. Phase C: add plan keys (browser agent loop, persistent profiles, concurrent sessions, schedules) in org-core entitlements delivered as claims, per-class rate limits layered on the gateway's global bucket, and a per-org fair-share concurrency cap in Quarry.
items.whyItMatters: Browser agent steps and minutes are not metered at all, so the most expensive Quarry feature is invisible to billing, and one org can consume every browser lease. Cost transparency for web acquisition (separate from model cost) and abuse protection are table-stakes that two or three of the four references have.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (single pricing function, failures free, two clear limit units)
others: Apify
Aside
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 4 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Firecrawl: one pure function price(options, outcome, cost tracking, flags) per job: base unit per page, failures cost 0, surcharges for LLM or security features, PDF per page, a ZDR surcharge, with a separate tracker of real provider costs for margin. Two limit units (pages or credits, and concurrent browsers) with separate submission and status rate limits. Aside gates features per plan (for example remote control on pro and max only). Apify meters compute units (GB-RAM-hours) plus storage operations. Every Firecrawl request also carries an origin and an integration tag from a closed list for analytics and cost attribution.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: Quarry publishes idempotent usage events to billing-core over NATS (usage.> to Lago) for five metrics (scrape page, crawl seed, search query, answer synth, batch URL), with scrape skipped on error; source is fixed to quarry-edge and there is no surface tag. /v1/extract (the web_fetch tool path) and /v1/map are metered as quarry.search.query. agent_routes.rs emits no usage events, so browser steps, minutes and agent runs are unmetered. Pricing lives in Lago billable-metric configuration outside this repo (INF, from the usage.rs comment), not in a pure function the Model Plane can call for estimates. org-core default entitlements are chat, api_keys, audit_logs and sso, quotas are api_calls, users and storage_mb per plan, and ZDR is the only computed plan-gated entitlement; no browser or Quarry keys exist. The gateway has a global distributed per-org/user token bucket (600 RPM default) over every route, but no per-class limits, and Quarry's browser pool is two or four process-wide leases with no per-org fairness. The SPA usage client is unused code.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: add metrics for browser steps and minutes, agent runs, extract and map with attributes; copy x-verevon-surface (closed enum) into usage events and receipts; emit usage from the agent step path (under ZDR carry ids and counts only, never content). Control Plane: billing-core owns the price table for the new metrics (failures free) and exposes a price-estimate endpoint that Model Plane approval cards (R-t2-06-07) and the budget work (R-t2-06-01) can call; org-core adds entitlement and quota keys that reach Quarry and the gateway as signed claims, never cross-plane DB reads. Frontend gateway: add cheap/expensive rate-limit classes on top of rate_limit.rs; Frontend: per-run usage in the ingestion run view. Quarry: a per-org semaphore in front of the lease pool, sized from the claim.
dependencies: billing-core price table and Lago metric codes
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (pricing, entitlements) with Ingestion Plane (metrics, concurrency) and Frontend Plane (rate-limit classes, usage UI)
items.risks: Pricing inside Quarry would violate plane ownership, so keep prices in billing-core and only attributes in Quarry. Usage under ZDR must carry no content. A new metric needs a matching Lago billable-metric code before it ships. Claims must flow through tokens, not DB reads.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-06-09] docs/BILLING.md (metering contract shipped for five metrics); browser metrics and plan keys are not planned there

verevon.exactGap: Quarry publishes five idempotent usage metrics to billing-core over NATS (usage.rs:88-94), but /v1/extract and /v1/map are billed as quarry.search.query (extract_routes.rs:345-361 meters one unit per target even when items failed; map_routes.rs:294-310) and agent_routes.rs emits no UsageEvent, so browser steps, minutes and agent runs are unmetered (only a per-step receipt cost_usd from the flat action_cost table exists, used for max_cost_usd budgets). Events carry no surface or outcome attribute (the zdr flag already rides in scrape and search metadata), no Quarry price table or estimate endpoint was found in billing-core (pricing is Lago metric config), the plan-key lists in org-core and billing-core contain no browser or Quarry keys, and the gateway has one global token bucket. Browser leases are two fixed process-wide pools (4 Browserbase, 2 local chromiumoxide) with no per-org share.
reuse: quarry-runtime usage.rs UsageEvent, NatsUsageMeter and the usage_metrics constants: add the new metric constants there (billing-core metric names are free-form but each needs a Lago billable-metric code before shipping).
Per-step receipt cost_usd and the flat action_cost table (action_cost.rs, agent_routes.rs:2346-2362) as the quantity source for browser step metrics; keep it a budget estimator, not a price.
billing-core allowance policies keyed by metric (allowance_repository.go:189-210) for included units and rollover on the new browser metrics.
Gateway entitlement-gate pattern already used for the leads add-on (leads.rs:80-110, GET billing-core /entitlements/{key}, fail-closed 402) for browser plan keys.
Verified Quarry Claims (principal_type, service_id, zdr; auth.rs:62-91) to derive the surface tag from the caller identity.
Existing per-org budget pattern in quarry-edge config (vector_retrieval_per_org_hourly_budget, config.rs:58-62) for a per-org browser cap.
Quarry /v1/team/credit-usage|token-usage|concurrency routes (routes.rs:202-221) and the unused SPA getTeam* helpers (quarry-client.ts:140-174) as the base of a per-run or per-org usage view.
verevon.constraints: Prices stay in billing-core/Lago, never in Quarry; Quarry only emits metric names, quantities and attributes, and a new metric needs its Lago code first (BILLING.md:56-64). ZDR must propagate: new browser and agent metrics must carry ids and counts only. Note the existing SCRAPE_PAGE event already puts the final URL and fingerprint into metadata even when zdr is active (routes.rs:490-505) and billing-core persists that metadata JSON in billing_usage_events (repository.go:463-512), so fix that in the same change. Plan entitlements and quotas are defined in two places (billing-core defaults.go and the shorter org-core list in types.go:266-271) and the gateway already reads billing-core for feature gating, so browser plan keys belong in billing-core (plus allowance policies) delivered through that endpoint or token claims, never by cross-plane DB reads. The gateway limiter derives its key as org:, user: or ip: (rate_limit.rs:269-289) but its own comment says it runs before require_session, so confirm which key is used in practice before adding per-class buckets.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Derive the surface tag from the verified token principal (service_id/principal_type) plus a gateway-set closed enum accepted only from service tokens, instead of trusting a header from user tokens. Split extract and map into their own metrics and meter only successful items (today extract bills every attempted target). Emit browser step and minute events from the agent step and close path using receipt cost and duration, ids and counts only under ZDR, and do not price inside Quarry. Put browser plan keys in billing-core defaults and allowance policies and reuse the leads-style entitlement gate. Implement the per-org fair-share as a per-org semaphore in front of RuntimeLeasePool (lease_pool.rs), first with a config default, later sized from a claim.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. Phase A (metrics, extract/map split, ZDR metadata cleanup) is about M on its own; plan keys across billing-core and the gateway plus the per-org lease cap push the whole item to L.
verevon.verdictReason: The core claim holds: browser steps, minutes and agent runs are not metered at all, extract and map are mislabelled as search, and no plan keys or fair-share exist. Keep, but reword to say plan keys live in billing-core (with org-core as a second list), the surface tag should come from the verified principal, a flat action-cost estimator already exists in Quarry for budgets, and the existing scrape metadata leaks the URL under ZDR.

items.title: Fetch-path reliability: one deadline budget, wired retries and typed failure sub-codes
items.summary: Add timeout_ms to scrape and agent requests and split it across the FallbackDriver waterfall with child cancellation tokens (reserve a minimum slice for the final browser tier, map client disconnect to the root token). Wire the already-written execute_with_retry into PageRunner using ErrorCode::retryable(), with maxRetries on the policy and no retries for ChallengeDetected or SecurityBlocked. Add a sub-code and detail field on QuarryError (DNS, TLS, all drivers failed, robots-blocked, and a processing-continues detail for long jobs), versioned across Temporal, webhooks and the gateway.
items.whyItMatters: Escalation through the static, TLS and browser drivers should finish inside one user-visible deadline instead of timing out with nothing. Transient failures should be retried the same way on scrape, crawl and agent paths. The Model and UI need to know why a fetch failed so they can switch source, wait or ask the user, instead of seeing a generic DriverFailed.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (SRC) for abort tiers and the transportable error vocabulary; Apify Crawlee (DOC) for the retry contract
others: Apify Crawlee (DOC): maxRequestRetries, errorHandler before each retry, failedRequestHandler
Firecrawl robustFetch (SRC): shared internal client with retry-on-status and cooldown
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Retries: 2 of 4 sources (Apify, Firecrawl), table-stakes. Deadline budgeting and transportable error codes: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl), unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Compose cancellation tokens: request token (client disconnect) to scrape deadline token to per-engine child tokens, so an engine timeout cancels only that engine and the waterfall continues, while a scrape timeout cancels everything. Queue waits get a fraction of the budget (2/3), waitFor is at most half the timeout, and defaults are computed from the requested features. One ErrorCode union with about 55 codes extends a transportable base with serialize/deserialize so code and details cross queues and webhooks unchanged; long jobs return a processing_continues detail with estimated remaining time. Retry: count per request, an error hook may change the request, then requeue with backoff until the retry cap, then a failure hook.

verevonToday.gap: execute_with_retry is exported but called only from its own tests; Temporal activity retries (5 attempts, exponential) and the FallbackDriver chain are the only live retry paths. Per the baseline, cancellation is a flat token, /v1/scrape exposes no request timeout and the waterfall has no per-driver budget (not re-checked here). quarry-core ErrorCode has 17 coarse codes with retryable() and http_status(); it has no fetch-level detail (DNS, TLS, all drivers failed, robots-blocked, cache miss) and no processing-continues contract, although api_error carries retry_after_seconds. Strict TLS everywhere is already the safe default (no accept-invalid-certs found).

items.approach: Ingestion Plane. (a) Deadlines: add timeout_ms to scrape and agent-run requests with defaults computed in one function from the requested features; build a child CancellationToken per driver attempt with remaining-budget accounting in FallbackDriver and a reserved minimum slice for the last driver; map axum client disconnect to the root token; keep strict TLS. (b) Retries: call execute_with_retry from PageRunner, take the cap from RunPolicy.retry (exists in the quarry-core contract), skip ChallengeDetected, SecurityBlocked and robots denials, and consult the AIMD host scheduler so retries cannot storm a blocked host. Share one reqwest retry middleware for edge-to-control and Model Plane calls. (c) Errors: add a sub_code plus details to QuarryError (for example DriverFailed{dns|tls|connect|all_drivers_failed}, Forbidden{robots|policy}) rather than exploding the top-level enum, as the improvements doc section 39 also advises; add a processing_continues detail for long jobs; propagate through Temporal activities, webhooks, the gateway's recoverable/unrecoverable classification and Model Plane tool results; version the error schema.
dependencies: F-t2-027 (BlockReason maps onto the same detail field)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (quarry-runtime, quarry-core, orchestrator); Frontend Plane gateway for classification
items.risks: Budget splitting can starve the browser tier, hence the reserved slice. Retry storms against blocked hosts. Contract churn for gateway and Model Plane clients, hence a versioned schema.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-04-06] Typed failure classes are planned in QUARRY_V2_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_IMPROVEMENTS_2026_OWNERSHIP_RECONCILED.md section 39 (extend the existing ErrorCode and CrawlDenialReason enums). Deadline budgeting and wiring retry.rs are not planned in the docs reviewed

verevon.exactGap: execute_with_retry is exported (lib.rs:164) but only its own tests call it; the live retries are Temporal activity retries (5 attempts, exponential, workflows.go:94-104), which cover job paths only, not sync /v1/scrape or agent routes. PageRunner calls fetch_conditional once while holding the per-host slot (pipeline.rs:335-364), FallbackDriver.fetch_inner walks drivers with no deadline or budget split (fallback_driver.rs:57-120), ScrapeRequest has no timeout field (routes.rs:346-375) and FetchPolicy.timeout_s is declared with a default of 30 but no fetch code reads it (policy.rs:86-103). ErrorCode has 17 coarse codes (error.rs:10-30) and DriverFailed is not retryable (error.rs:38-43), so wiring the existing helper alone would not retry DNS, connect or browser-launch failures, and there is no sub-code or processing-continues detail (api_error.rs carries only retry_after_seconds).
reuse: execute_with_retry, backoff_delay and classify in quarry-runtime/retry.rs
RunPolicy.retry (quarry-core Retry) and the runtime RetryPolicy with transient_codes
HostScheduler (AIMD) and AutoscaledPool already used in PageRunner to avoid retry storms
ErrorCode::retryable() and http_status(), the api_error retry_after_seconds field
Temporal activity retry policy for job paths
model-gateway client-side per-scrape bound (QUARRY_EDGE_TIMEOUT_SECS, default 30 s)
verevon.constraints: Retry layering: Temporal already retries job-path pages 5 times, so an in-process retry on those paths would multiply attempts; wire it for sync scrape and agent paths only, or lower one layer. Retries must re-enter the per-host slot or consult the AIMD scheduler rather than sleep inside the slot (pipeline.rs:343-364 holds it across the fetch). The client-supplied timeout is a request from the caller (possibly the Model) that Quarry clamps to its own maximum. ZDR: processing-continues re-attach needs stored results and must not exist for ZDR (batch and crawl jobs are already refused under ZDR, routes.rs:563-583). Any new error sub-code or detail field changes the contract seen by the gateway and Model Plane tool results, so version it.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder: (c) sub-codes first, so DriverFailed{dns|tls|connect|all_drivers_failed} can carry its own retryable flag and robots or policy denials stay non-retryable; (a) then add timeout_ms to scrape and clamp it, with child cancellation tokens per FallbackDriver attempt and a reserved slice for the last tier (the model-gateway already bounds a scrape client-side at 30 s and escalates once to the browser itself, so avoid double budgeting); (b) last, wire execute_with_retry (or a variant taking fetch hints, since it calls driver.fetch without hints) around the sync scrape path only. Reuse RunPolicy.retry but reconcile it with the second RetryPolicy in quarry-runtime/policy.rs, there are two retry config types today. Section 39 of the improvements doc covers only the typed failure classes, not the deadline budget or retry wiring.
verevon.effortNote: Stays M if sub-codes stay inside Quarry's own envelope; L if they are propagated through Temporal, webhooks, the gateway and Model Plane tool results.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is confirmed. The item misses that DriverFailed is non-retryable (so wiring the helper alone does little), that Temporal already retries job paths (retry multiplication), that FetchPolicy.timeout_s is not enforced anywhere and that the model-gateway already bounds scrapes client-side. Reword with the corrected ordering.

items.title: Org-scoped URL cache with explicit freshness, and a cache-only no-egress mode
items.summary: Add a URL plus variant keyed cache in Ingestion Plane over the existing artifact storage (Postgres metadata, Redis hot path), keyed by org, with maxAge/minAge/store flags on scrape and agent fetches, cacheState and cachedAt in the output metadata, and negative caching. ZDR orgs bypass it entirely. In a second phase add a no_egress policy flag that pins the driver plan to cache and Data Plane artifacts and returns a typed miss without logging the URL.
items.whyItMatters: Repeated agent research becomes cheaper and faster, fewer requests hit target sites (which also reduces blocks), and the Model gets explicit freshness it can reason about. The no-egress mode gives regulated or sovereign workspaces a hard guarantee of no outbound traffic.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique, with lockdown as a further unique mode
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Key = hash(normalised URL) plus variant (mobile, country, stealth, blockAds, wait, screenshot options). Raw body goes to object storage, a metadata row to an index table, hot entries to a Redis LRU that fails fast. The read path resolves maxAge (explicit, then dynamic per domain via a 200 ms race, then a 2-day default), queries the newest entry in the window and returns cacheState hit/miss plus cachedAt; negative windows skip the DB on repeat misses and entries whose body is missing are deleted. Lockdown rewrites the engine plan to index-only, disables robots/sitemap/redirect fetching, forces ZDR and returns a typed cache-miss error that does not log the URL.

verevonToday.gap: The Quarry cache is keyed by content fingerprint and is read only when the caller sends prev_fingerprint (and never under ZDR), so there is no URL or maxAge cache, no cacheState metadata, no negative caching and no cache-only mode; SWR claimed in PRESETS.md is absent. The gateway has separate 4 h search and scrape-preview caches (see R-t2-04-02). Artifact storage and Data Plane document storage already exist as bodies to serve from.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: after R-t2-04-02 lands the shared should_cache(), build the URL index with org-scoped keys, store bodies in the existing artifact store, hot path in Redis, flags maxAge/minAge/store on scrape and agent observation fetches, cacheState and cachedAt in NormalizedOutput, negative cache for failures, self-healing when a body is missing. Never cache credentialed, action or profile requests, or anything produced under ZDR. Phase 2: no_egress policy flag (carried by the org policy floor, R-t2-04-05) that pins DriverPlan to a cache/Data-Plane-artifact driver, calling Data Plane APIs rather than its database, and returns a typed miss error without logging the URL.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane; Data Plane for the artifact-backed no-egress path
items.risks: Cross-tenant leakage if keys are not org-scoped or authenticated content is cached; stale answers surprise users, so always show cachedAt. Lockdown value is limited to a niche of regulated orgs.

verevon.exactGap: The CachePolicy contract (mode, max_age_s, vary_on, stale_while_revalidate_s) and should_read/should_write/effective_ttl in routes.rs are live and bypassed under ZDR, but the Redis PageCache is keyed quarry:page:{content fingerprint} (no org segment), is read only when the caller supplies prev_fingerprint, and has no URL key, minAge or store flag, cachedAt/cacheState in NormalizedOutput, negative caching, consumer for the SWR field or cache-only mode; a URL-plus-vary key helper, cache::fingerprint(), is dead scaffolding. The gateway keeps its own URL-keyed scrape-preview cache in Frontend-Plane Redis (key from the URL alone via a 64-bit DefaultHasher, 4 h fresh, 24 h store, ZDR-aware), also not org-scoped.

items.title: URL and domain reputation gate before fetch and navigation, then layered screening (reviewer model, Quarry-side injection labels)
items.summary: Add a ReputationProvider trait in quarry-security that SecurityEngine.preflight and the agent validate_navigation hook call before any fetch, redirect or discovered crawl link. Start with a local hash-prefix list (Web Risk Update-style) so full URLs never leave the platform, add per-org modes (off, normal, customer secure-web-gateway categories such as Zscaler) in Control Plane, and never persist verdicts for ZDR orgs. || Three optional defence-in-depth layers. Model Plane: a fixed-rubric, tool-less reviewer model that can pre-approve low-risk first-visit approvals (never hand-off or always-confirm tiers), fails closed, caches allow per (thread, origin) with a short TTL and logs decisions in receipts. Ingestion Plane: a local, hashed-prefix reputation check in egress policy (decision_source=site_status) evaluated with the domain grant. Quarry scrape/extract: an opt-in prompt-injection flag that labels suspicious spans or fails with a typed error.
items.whyItMatters: Autonomous browsing can reach phishing or malware pages, and enterprise customers want their own secure-web-gateway policy applied to Verevon's agent traffic. validate_navigation already gates every Model-proposed navigation, so the hook exists and the feature is a strong enterprise-sales point. || Cuts approval fatigue and supports unattended scheduled runs, protects agents from phishing and injection farms, and gives direct Quarry API consumers the same guard the agent path already has.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (SRC)
others: Codex in-app browser (guardian v2 reviewer with {thread, origin} cache and 5-minute expiry, credential rubric and evidence fencing; site_status reputation endpoint with per-origin cache)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique || Reviewer 1 of 3 (unique); reputation 1 of 3 (unique); injection guard 3 of 3 (table-stakes, Verevon agent path already covered)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: checkUrl(url, orgConfig): local allow/deny lists and blocked TLDs, then optional customer SWG category rules synced on an interval, then a reputation provider (Google Web Risk hash-prefix database or a batched Zscaler lookup) with a risk threshold and an explicit fail-open or fail-closed policy. It runs before the first engine and on every redirect and discovered link. Modes are off, manual, normal, zscaler. Verdicts are cached only within the request, which respects the ZDR boundary, and a per-request override is allowed only if org config permits. || Merged items add: Approval request -> reviewer sub-agent with {action, origin, sanitized URL, bounded transcript}; returns allow|deny|escalate; missing evidence is never permission. Reputation: lookup(origin, path) in a cache, call the service on miss, deny blocked categories. Injection: neutralise role-tag lookalikes, wrap in BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED markers, optionally classify chunks with a small model.

verevonToday.gap: quarry-security has SSRF heuristics, URL-signature analysis and blocklists but no reputation provider and no customer SWG integration (no WebRisk or reputation code found). The right hook, validate_navigation, is already called for Model-proposed navigation and recovery actions. || Execution-core screens ExternalWeb/BrowserScraped/ThirdPartyMcp results unconditionally (shipped). No safety reviewer exists for browser approvals (capability-core's llmreviewer is a skill-learning reviewer), no reputation lookup was found in Quarry crates (only a capability flag cap.self_owned.quarry_url_reputation_feeds), and Quarry's observation path has no injection labelling for direct API consumers.

items.approach: Phase 1: reputation gate in SecurityEngine.preflight and validate_navigation (Google Web Risk or a customer-chosen provider, verdicts not stored, ZDR-safe). Phase 2 (from R-t2-09-13, lower priority): reviewer-model screening of approvals and Quarry-side trust labels on observations as part of the prompt-injection program. || Source detail: [R-t2-04-08] Ingestion Plane: ReputationProvider trait in quarry-security, called from SecurityEngine.preflight, validate_navigation, redirect handling and crawl-link discovery. Implement a local hash-prefix provider first (periodic list sync, local match, full-URL lookup only if a prefix matches and the org mode allows it), then an optional Zscaler adapter. Per-org mode and failure policy live in Control Plane and arrive through the policy floor (R-t2-04-05). Return ErrorCode::SecurityBlocked with a reputation sub-code and show a clear block message in the browser pane. No verdict persistence for ZDR orgs. || [R-t2-09-13] Model Plane: optional reviewer step in the approval pipeline for tiers marked pre-approvable. Ingestion Plane: local reputation feed in the egress policy; opt-in injection flag on scrape/extract while execution-core screening stays authoritative for agents. Build after per-origin consent (R-t2-09-08) and typed denials (R-t2-09-07).
items.risks: Lookup APIs that receive full URLs leak user intent (ZDR), hence the local-prefix design. False positives block legitimate research, so offer an allow-list and clear messages. || The reviewer can itself be prompt-injected (fence evidence, never sole gate for irreversible actions); cost per approval; do not send full ZDR URLs to third-party reputation services; classifier false positives.

verevon.exactGap: A feed-backed local host reputation list already exists: scripts/sync-security-feeds.py (operator-run, URLhaus CSV, optional PhishTank) writes a host blocklist snapshot that quarry-edge loads once at boot into DefaultEngine, and SecurityEngine.preflight (scrape path, pipeline.rs:305) plus validate_navigation (explicit Navigate actions and tab creation) consult it, so 'absent' is wrong. Missing are scheduled sync and hot reload (no runtime mutation path outside tests), subdomain or URL-level matching (exact host only), per-org modes (the quarry-control /v1/blocklists CRUD is not wired into the engine), enforcement on redirects, click-initiated navigations and subresources (quarry-browser's guard_navigation_target and guard_page_request_target use only the SSRF heuristic, not the engine; the DNS-pinned egress proxy with decision receipts is the natural seam), and any hash-prefix or customer-gateway provider. No safety-reviewer step or Quarry-side injection labelling exists, while Model Plane screening of external-trust results is already unconditional and cross-domain navigation is already a deterministic HITL approval category.

SecurityEngine.preflight and check_discovered call sites (pipeline.rs, validate_navigation)
PinnedBrowserEgressProxy + BrowserEgressPolicy decisions/receipts as the enforcement point for redirects, clicks and subresources
execution-core deterministic RiskCategory gates and provenance screening
PrivacyPolicy::guard_third_party_processing for any external lookup
verevon.constraints: Quarry (Ingestion Plane) owns egress and security gating and the Model only proposes navigation, so the gate stays in Quarry; per-org mode and failure policy must come from Control Plane through a service read or the policy floor (F-t2-022), never a cross-plane DB read. ZDR: no verdict persistence and no full URLs sent to third-party reputation services (hence local list or hash-prefix design). A Model Plane reviewer would put a model into the approval path although approvals are deterministic HITL today, and Quarry to Model Plane calls are not granted, so layers 2 and 3 need grants and an ADR and must never be the sole gate for irreversible tiers.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword phase 1 as 'automate and extend the existing feed-backed blocklist': scheduled sync job plus hot reload (swap the RwLock sets), suffix/subdomain matching, per-org mode via the policy floor, and a reputation callback in BrowserEgressPolicy / the egress proxy so redirects, click-driven navigations and subresources are covered and receipts carry a decision source (today validate_navigation covers only explicit Navigate actions). Introduce the ReputationProvider trait and a hash-prefix Web Risk style provider only if feed coverage proves insufficient; wire or retire the unconnected /v1/blocklists CRUD. Demote the reviewer-model screening, Quarry-side injection labels and any Zscaler or other customer-gateway adapter to optional follow-ups.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for phase 1 (extend existing engine, feed automation, egress hook, per-org mode); layers 2 and 3 are separate L-sized work behind grants.
verevon.verdictReason: The item claims no reputation provider exists but a URLhaus feed-backed host blocklist is already loaded by quarry-edge; the real gaps are automation, matching depth, per-org mode and redirect/click coverage at the egress boundary, and the reviewer layers should be demoted.

items.title: Fail-closed PII redaction stage for scraped and crawled content
items.summary: Add an optional redaction transform in the Ingestion Plane pipeline (after markdown, before LLM formats, diffing and Data Plane ingest) that calls the Model Plane language PII provider with entity types and a replace style (tag, mask, remove). Policy comes per org from the Control Plane; if redaction fails or exceeds a size limit the response returns empty content plus a warning.
items.whyItMatters: GDPR posture: orgs can ingest web content into the Data Plane without storing personal data, which complements ZDR. Today only model input is filtered, not what Quarry stores.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-096 privacy service; api-surface-054 options)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: After markdown derivation and before downstream transformers and LLM formats, send markdown plus {mode, entities, replaceStyle} to a redaction service with model, Presidio and spaCy accuracy tiers; replace spans; if the call fails or the size limit is exceeded, return empty markdown with a warning (fail closed).

verevonToday.gap: The Model Plane gateway redacts emails and long number sequences from model input under a pii_filter policy, and inference-core has a language provider with a Pii operation. Quarry scrape and crawl output and Data Plane ingest are not redacted. agent_memory::redact_sensitive is re-exported in lib.rs with no caller. Cost: the model-gateway grant to Quarry is still refused (see R-t2-02-02).

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: add a redact stage in the transform pipeline gated by a per-org policy (Control Plane) and a per-request option on FormatSpec; call a Model Plane PII route (language provider) over the markdown; fail closed with a warning; run before json/summary formats and before hashing for change tracking so monitors do not store raw PII. Reuse the Model Plane deterministic pii_filter as a cheap first pass.
dependencies: model-gateway grant to quarry-edge (shared with F-t2-019)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (stage) with Model Plane (PII model) and Control Plane (policy)
items.risks: Over-redaction damages content and extraction quality; added latency on crawls; redaction accuracy claims need testing for Norwegian and other non-English text.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: nothing in the scrape/crawl path redacts content: PageRunner builds markdown, links and metadata (pipeline.rs:505-516) and persists the raw html artifact, the markdown artifact and meta.json (pipeline.rs:604-660) before the optional Data Plane ingest (pipeline.rs:855+), and quarry_runtime::redact_sensitive (agent_memory.rs:52) is used only by AgentScratchpad. SRC: the building blocks differ from the item's assumptions: Model Plane /v1/ai/language/pii accepts no entity-type or replace-style parameters (AiLanguageRequest, http_routes.rs:1947-1957; Azure parameters hard-code all categories and a '*' mask, language.rs:529), the deterministic pii_filter lives in model-gateway and is driven by capability-core safety_policies (moderation.rs:3-5,123), and quarry-edge holds no model-gateway audience (cross-plane-token-requests.json rows model-invoke, model-stream and model-audio are granted:false). DOC: SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md:97 and :218 already plan a redact_before_persist policy and a 'PII Redactor' pipeline stage, so this is planned but unbuilt rather than unplanned.
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs:505-516 (markdown, links, metadata built; no redaction step)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs:525 (fingerprint over raw body bytes) and :604-660 (html, markdown, meta.json artifacts persisted)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/agent_memory.rs:49-67 and :96-105 (whitespace-tokenizing redact_sensitive; emails, secret-like tokens, 13-19 digit runs only)
