reuse: model-gateway moderation.rs redact_pii (deterministic first pass pattern)
quarry-core PrivacyPolicy::guard_third_party_processing to gate any PII provider as a third-party processor
Data Plane retrieval-engine-rs redact.rs regex set (email, phone, card) as a reference for a shared deterministic redactor
quarry-transform crate as the home for a pure, dependency-light redactor
Model Plane /v1/ai/language/pii as an optional second tier once a grant exists
verevon.constraints: SRC: org PII policy is owned by capability-core safety_policies in the Model Plane (moderation.rs:3-5), not the Control Plane, so 'policy comes per org from the Control Plane' misassigns ownership; no cross-plane DB access means Quarry must read it through an API or accept a per-request flag. SRC: sending page text to the Model Plane PII route is third-party processing (Azure AI Language) that needs the PrivacyPolicy processor gate and ZDR-eligible terms, and the model-gateway grant is currently refused (decision D16/QB-T17). SRC: redaction must cover every persisted representation, not just markdown: raw html artifact, markdown, meta.json, the local search index, page screenshots for visual RAG, and Data Plane ingest.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start with a deterministic in-process redactor in quarry-transform (regex plus checksum validators for emails, phone numbers, IBAN, card Luhn and the Norwegian 11-digit fodselsnummer mod-11) behind a per-request redact option and an org default read from the existing policy source; do not reuse redact_sensitive as-is because it whitespace-tokenizes and would flatten markdown. Make it fail closed at the persistence boundary (no html, markdown, meta, index or ingest write when redaction errors) instead of only blanking the response. Treat the Model Plane PII model as an optional second tier after the model-gateway grant lands, and extend its route with categories and replace style if needed.
verevon.effortNote: A deterministic stage over markdown alone is M; covering all persisted representations, the policy source and an optional model tier makes the item L.
verevon.verdictReason: Not shipped, but the item misstates policy ownership, ignores raw html and other persisted artifacts, assumes a Model Plane call that is not granted and parameters the route lacks, and omits that the sovereign scraping doc already plans the stage; reword to deterministic-first, persistence-boundary redaction.

items.title: Procedure store and run-as-procedure, with postconditions so real runs can compile
items.summary: Persist compiled browser procedures (versioned, tagged, org and owner scoped), add an execute endpoint that replays a procedure through the normal step path with grant, approval and budget checks, and offer 'save as procedure' after a successful agent run. First add optional postcondition assertions to agent steps so typical click, type and select runs can reach Verified status, because the compiler today rejects anything unverified.
items.whyItMatters: Turning a one-off agent browsing session into a repeatable, schedulable procedure is the step from 'the agent browses' to 'the product automates', and a replay is cheaper than re-planning every run. Quarry already has the hard part (compile, replay-compare, quality and impact checks) which Firecrawl's open source does not expose.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (agent run exported as skill, workflow and schema)
others: Apify (immutable versioned builds with tags)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: GET /v2/agent/:id/skill returns {name, spec, skillMd, workflow, schema, blueprint} derived from a finished run (the generator itself is closed upstream, so only the route shape is known). Re-implement as: distill the verified action trajectory into a parameterized procedure (steps, element refs, input schema) plus a natural-language skill; store with a version; replay executes deterministic steps and hands drift back to the agent. Apify adds immutable builds numbered MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD, tag-to-build mapping and pinning, and records the resolved build on each run.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: compile_procedure, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact exist behind four stateless endpoints; the compiled procedure is returned to the caller and never stored, version is fixed at 1, and there is no execute-procedure endpoint. compile_procedure rejects any receipt whose outcome is not Verified (browser_procedure.rs:85), but outcome_for_action marks click, type, press, scroll, select and evaluate as Unknown ('postcondition_required'), so a typical form-driving run cannot compile; only navigate, wait, capture, dialog and download steps verify. Receipts are not appended under ZDR, so ZDR runs cannot be compiled at all. The Verevon UI does not call these endpoints and capability-core's skill sink does not take browser trajectories (not verified).

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: (1) extend the agent step request with an optional expect assertion (URL pattern, ref present, text present) that Quarry evaluates after the action and uses to upgrade the outcome to Verified. (2) Add a procedures table (quarry-control Postgres or edge Postgres): org_id, owner_id, procedure_id, version, tags, steps, source_receipt_ids, status (draft, promoted, quarantined) and the quality report; versions are immutable, tags move, and each run records the resolved version. (3) POST /v1/agent/procedures/{id}/runs starts a run and feeds the steps through the existing step handler, so grants, sensitive approvals and budgets (R-t2-06-01) apply again; on drift return RepairRequired to the planner. Model Plane: 'save as procedure' after a successful run and register promoted procedures as capabilities in capability-core (R-t2-06-07). Frontend: saved procedures list with replay-check and impact status.
dependencies: Coordinate with any automation or scheduling category
items.risks: Replaying with logged-in profiles must re-check grants and approvals every run, never replay a stored sensitive approval. ZDR runs cannot be saved. Postconditions that are too weak would let a broken replay look verified; keep the unverified-step refusal in assess_quality. Overlaps an automation category.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-06-04] docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:93-96 (persistent rollout state and fixture-backed quality gates for procedures)

verevon.exactGap: Quarry has stateless compile_procedure, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact (browser_procedure.rs:61-200) behind four routes (agent_routes.rs:3685-3695); the compiled procedure is returned to the caller, version is hard-coded to 1 (browser_procedure.rs:108), nothing stores it, no execute route exists, and nothing outside Quarry calls these routes. compile_procedure rejects any receipt whose outcome is not Verified (browser_procedure.rs:85-96) while outcome_for_action marks click, type, press, scroll, select and evaluate as Unknown (observation.rs:217-262) and StepBody has no expect or postcondition field (agent_routes.rs:818-824), so a form-driving run cannot compile; ref-based actions also embed snapshot_id, generation and ref_id (contracts.rs:650-654) and compare_replay demands exact action equality, so a stored procedure could not replay in a new session without re-binding refs.
reuse: Quarry browser_procedure.rs compile, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact and the four existing routes: keep stateless and extend.
Durable non-ZDR step receipts (receipts.append at agent_routes.rs:2346-2391, list_for_actor) as the compile source.

Model Plane run-level postcondition: PlanConfig.postcondition and judge_browser_procedure (browser_agent.rs:262-285, postcondition.rs:996-1075) as the run-level verifier to pair with a new step-level expect evaluated by Quarry.
The normal step path /v1/agent/runs/:id/step with BrowserBroker grants, execution-core approval gate (browser_events.rs:238) and max_cost_usd budgets for any replay.
Existing SemanticLocator and ElementFingerprint (contracts.rs) as the stable locators to store instead of run-specific refs.
capability-core and session-core agent_skills registration path (skillsink/sink.go) and capability-core cron for scheduling replays.
verevon.constraints: Quarry's own code and docs put procedure rollout state and business approval outside Quarry: assess_quality 'supplies evidence for the owning release/Model workflow' (agent_routes.rs:2512-2527, browser_procedure.rs:150-152), Quarry 'does not silently replay or self-heal effectful procedures' (agent_routes.rs:2523-2527) and 'Model Plane remains the planner and policy owner' (agent_routes.rs:2462-2466); persistent rollout state is listed as future work (WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:93-96). A Quarry-owned store with an execute endpoint that replays steps would make Quarry the proposer, which breaks 'Model proposes, Quarry executes'. Every replay must re-run grants, sensitive-action approvals and budgets and must never reuse a stored approval; ZDR runs write no receipts (agent_routes.rs:2360-2391) so they can never be compiled or saved.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep Quarry's role as deterministic evidence: add an optional step-level expect assertion (URL pattern, ref present, text present) that Quarry evaluates after the action to upgrade the outcome to Verified, and canonicalise stored actions to stable locators (semantic locator or element fingerprint, stripping snapshot_id, generation and ref_id) so replay can re-bind against a fresh snapshot and fail closed on ambiguity. Put the procedure store (versioned, tagged, org and owner scoped, draft/promoted/quarantined) and the runner in Model Plane (capability-core registry or session-core), where the runner proposes each stored step to Quarry's normal step endpoint, uses Quarry's replay-check for comparison, and applies grants, approvals and budgets; 'save as procedure' and the list UI are Frontend work on top.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: step-level postconditions in Quarry, locator canonicalisation and replay re-binding, a Model Plane store plus runner with approvals and budgets, and UI. It also depends on the live planner loop, grants and budgets (F-t2-001, F-t2-008, F-t2-010). Could be staged: postconditions (M), canonicalisation (M), store plus runner (L).
verevon.verdictReason: The compile, replay-check, quality and impact functions exist and are wired to routes, so the item must say the stateless half is shipped; the missing half is a store, an execute path and postconditions. The proposed placement (Quarry store plus execute endpoint) conflicts with Quarry's documented design and the Model-proposes rule, and the item misses that ref-based actions are run-specific and cannot replay verbatim.

items.title: Per-run result sets with a dataset table view and server-side export
items.summary: Give every crawl, batch and extract run an append-only result set (JSONL in the artifact store, indexed by run) behind GET /v1/runs/{id}/items?format=csv|jsonl|xlsx&fields=&omit=, with a dataset table view in the Ingestions page and a per-org retention policy. ZDR runs stream items and persist nothing. Ingestion into the Data Plane stays an explicit, selective decision.
items.whyItMatters: Users extracting structured data (prices, listings, procurement notices) need a table they can inspect, filter and export without forcing everything into the Data Plane. Today the Ingestions page shows runs, schedules, monitors, sources, evidence and profiles but no result data.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (dataset, key-value store and request queue per run)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Run creation allocates dataset_id, kv_id and queue_id and injects them into the run. The dataset is append-only (items up to 9 MB) and exports server-side with format=csv|jsonl|xlsx|xml|rss, field projection (fields, omit, clean) and hidden #-prefixed debug fields. The KV store holds content-typed records for blobs and state; named storages persist indefinitely while unnamed ones expire after about 7 days; per-object rate limits return 429.

verevonToday.gap: SRC and baseline: artifact storage (memory, filesystem, S3 with content addressing), a durable Postgres URL frontier and Data Plane ingest exist, but there is no per-run result set, no dataset or key-value API, no export formats and no dataset browser; the SPA's Quarry client (quarry-client.ts) is unused code.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: at job completion write each result item to a JSONL object in the artifact store under org/run, with an index row in Postgres, and add the items route with the export formats and projection. Retention policy per org (default expiry, longer for named sets); ZDR returns items on the stream only. Frontend: dataset table view in the Ingestions run detail with an 'ingest to Data Plane' action and a download menu. Optional output schema fields arrive with R-t2-06-06.
dependencies: Optionally F-t2-053 for typed field metadata
items.risks: Must stay a working set with retention, not a second Data Plane (no retrieval or graph). Export of large sets needs streaming. Items can contain sensitive scraped content, so ACLs follow the run owner.

verevon.exactGap: No per-run result set, dataset or key-value API, export formats or dataset browser exist: the edge route table has artifacts list/get, jobs list, run and job events, sources, snapshots and team aggregates only (routes.rs:130-293), ArtifactSummary has no run_id and the list has no run filter even though artifact keys are laid out org=/run/page_hash/kind/id (resources.rs:83-97, artifact_store.rs:186-200). The Ingestions page has runs, schedules, monitoring, sources, evidence (job events) and profiles but no result data (VerevonIngestionsPage.tsx:67-114); manual extract results are returned once inline as ephemeral evidence under a synthetic run id (ingestions/runs.rs:268-340), and the SPA quarry-client.ts is used only by its own test. Structured /v1/extract is synchronous and persists nothing.
reuse: ArtifactStore with per-run key layout (org=/run_id/page_hash/kind/id) and tenant-bound get_with_key: add a run_id field and filter to the artifact list instead of a second store.

page_extracted events (title, excerpt, summary, word_count, lang, driver; routes.rs:776-830, event.rs) already stored in control per job and served by GET /v1/runs/:id/events and /v1/jobs/:id/events: a ready-made per-page row source for crawl and batch.
Gateway /api/ingestions/runs and /api/ingestions/evidence plus the Evidence panel as the place to attach a results table.
Selective ingest to the Data Plane (crawl ingest flag, CrawlPagePicker) for the explicit promote action.
Quarry retention janitor in control (main.go:197-201, inert unless QUARRY_RETENTION_DAYS is set) for retention policy.
verevon.constraints: ZDR: /v1/crawl and /v1/batch are refused for ZDR callers (routes.rs:555-575), so a durable run result set never applies to ZDR; only synchronous scrape and extract can run under ZDR and those must stay stream-only. The result set must remain a working set with retention, not a second Data Plane (no retrieval or graph); Data Plane ingest stays an explicit decision. ACL: artifact reads are tenant (org) bound (resource_routes.rs:125-155), not per actor, so per-owner result visibility would be new work. Stored items can hold sensitive scraped content, so export must be streamed and audited.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not start with a new JSONL store plus Postgres index plus xlsx export. Smaller path: (1) add run_id to ArtifactSummary and a run filter on /v1/artifacts (S); (2) project per-page rows for crawl and batch from page_extracted events plus artifact refs, exposed as GET /v1/runs/{id}/items with csv and jsonl export streamed by the edge or gateway (M); (3) a table view in the Ingestions run detail with an ingest action. A durable structured result set only becomes meaningful once structured extraction runs as a durable job (today /v1/extract is synchronous and unpersisted), so tie the JSONL dataset design to that dependency rather than to existing runs.
verevon.effortNote: M for the projection-based approach; the item as originally designed (new JSONL store, Postgres index, retention policy, xlsx, table UI) is L.
verevon.verdictReason: The feature does not exist and the gap description is accurate, but the proposed storage design overbuilds when per-run artifact keys and page_extracted events already exist. Keep as a medium-priority item with the lighter projection approach and the durable-extract dependency stated.

items.title: Saved job definitions: expose presets, then first-party Quarry packs with typed schemas
items.summary: Phase 1 (M): expose quarry-control's preset catalog through quarry-edge with org and Space scoping, add 'save as preset' on ingestion runs, and make scrape, crawl and batch schedules actually execute. Phase 2 (L): define a declarative QuarryPack manifest (id, version, kind, input JSON Schema with UI hints and isSecret, output schema, required driver capabilities, ZDR compatibility, cost class) and wire the existing NAV vacancies, procurement and official-statistics collectors as the first first-party packs, with a generated schema form in the SPA.
items.whyItMatters: Saved, typed job definitions give users and the Model Plane a menu of known-good jobs instead of free-form crawls, and Quarry keeps execution authority by validating (pack id, input) against the schema. It also gives dormant code (presets, collectors, schedule validation) a way to ship.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (Actor manifest, input schema, tasks)
others: Codex in-app browser (availability-gated plugin bundles)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One manifest per unit (.actor/actor.json) declares name, version, build tag, env, input and output schema and default storages, and the same unit runs from the console, API, CLI, schedule or another unit. A JSON input schema with UI hints (editor, prefill, enum titles, isSecret, resource picker) renders the form and validates API input identically. Tasks are saved input plus run-option presets (up to 5,000 per user) that can be run, scheduled and shared; schedules reference presets. Codex adds an availability check (gates) before a bundled plugin is installed for a user or org.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: MountPresets is registered only on quarry-control (GET /v1/presets and /v1/presets/{name}); edge does not proxy it, so the SPA cannot reach presets, and the Rust domain preset bundles are unused. Schedules are stored and cron-validated, but control mounts the schedule lifecycle aliases with a nil Temporal client, so trigger and backfill return a typed 501, and only the change_monitor schedule kind is wired as a user-facing flow (baseline v-quarry-080, not re-verified). The NAV vacancies, procurement and official-series collectors are Go packages that nothing outside their own directories imports. The durable sources registry with monitor presets is the only user-facing preset surface. Schema-driven forms: grep of verevonv3/src for SchemaForm, schema-form, zodToForm, zod-to-json and JsonSchemaForm found nothing, so no generic renderer exists; the zod (v4) action registry shared by human UI and AI actions is the right foundation.

items.approach: Phase 1, Ingestion Plane: quarry-edge proxies control /v1/presets (read) and adds org-scoped saved presets (preset id, base preset, overrides, owner, visibility); wire a scheduler for scrape/crawl/batch kinds (the Temporal client, or a minimal control-side runner) so schedules reference presets. Frontend: 'save as preset' on ingestion runs. Phase 2, Ingestion Plane: QuarryPack manifest in quarry-core, registry in quarry-control, GET /v1/packs and POST /v1/packs/{id}/runs on edge, validated against the schema; start with the three existing collectors. Publish input and output JSON Schemas (for example schemars from the Rust types) at /v1/schemas, render them with a Solid SchemaForm, and reuse the same schema as the Model Plane tool parameters. Space-shared presets reference only sources the viewer may already see.
dependencies: F-t2-052 for output schema and views
OpenAPI completeness (baseline v-quarry-019: 46 of about 75 routes)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (with Frontend Plane for forms)
items.risks: Scope creep toward a third-party marketplace or arbitrary user code (sandbox isolation for browsers is absent), so keep packs declarative and first-party. Space-shared presets must not widen owner-plane ACLs. Divergence between zod and Rust schemas if both are hand-written: generate one from the other.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-06-06] docs/PRESETS.md and docs/SCHEDULES.md describe the preset catalog and schedule lifecycle; edge exposure and non-monitor schedule execution are not done

verevon.exactGap: SRC: GET /v1/presets exists only on quarry-control (main.go:174; presets.go:24-52) and edge does not proxy it, and its RunPolicy presets are inert end to end: control stamps the policy on the job (resources.go:460-483) but InternalRunPage has no policy field (routes.rs:743-768), the orchestrator's Policy fields in workflows.go (:17-18,:40,:71,:86) are never populated or read, and every PageRunner is built with RunPolicy::default() (routes.rs:461,1001,1116); the Rust preset bundles that PRESETS.md calls shipped (presets.rs:320-353) have no caller and no route accepts them, and the NAV, procurement and official-series collectors have no importer. SRC: schedule creation accepts cron for any kind (gateway schedules.rs:99-188) but control maps only change_monitor to a workflow (schedule_wire.go:37-52) and the orchestrator skips the rest (schedules.go:153-165), even though ScrapeJobWF, CrawlJobWF and BatchJobWF are registered and used by the ad-hoc job dispatcher (orchestrator main.go:94-118; dispatcher.go:266-290), so stored cron scrape/crawl/batch schedules never fire. SRC: a durable Sources registry (kind crawl|scrape|search, free-form config, optional hourly|daily|weekly monitor) is already shipped end to end (gateway sources.rs:47,154-175; resource_routes.rs:410-426) and overlaps 'save as preset', and no schema-form renderer exists in verevonv3/src although z.toJSONSchema already feeds agent tools (agent-tools.ts:64-69).
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/cmd/control/main.go:174, :188, :192 (MountPresets, MountSources, MountScheduleAliases with nil Temporal client; comment :176-187)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/resources/presets.go:24-52 (catalog endpoints), :69 (fast preset ignores robots), :84-96 (stealth preset)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/schedule_routes.rs:247-296 (preset = hourly|daily|weekly cadence for change monitors)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/presets.rs:320-353 (builtin_presets, resolve_preset: no callers) and docs/PRESETS.md:1-30 (documents them as shipped)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/routes.rs:563-575 (crawl and batch refused under ZDR)
reuse: quarry_sources registry (name, url, kind, config, optional monitor) as the saved-definition entity instead of a new preset entity
Registered ScrapeJobWF/CrawlJobWF/BatchJobWF plus ChangeMonitorWF per-fire run_id derivation as the template for scheduled workflows
zod action registry and z.toJSONSchema (agent-tools.ts) as the single schema source for a generated Solid form and Model Plane tool parameters
quarry-control resources.ResolvePreset and the preset catalog shape, once policy is enforced
collector packages in quarry-control (navacancies, procurement, officialseries) as logic to wrap in first-party workflows
verevon.constraints: SRC: the 'fast' preset ignores robots (presets.go:69) and 'stealth' escalates on bot signals (presets.go:84-96), so the catalog must not be exposed to users as-is; 'preset' already means three things (hourly|daily|weekly cadence, RunPolicy bundle, dead Rust bundles). SRC: saved crawl and batch jobs and schedules are durable by construction and refused under ZDR (routes.rs:563-575), so ZDR orgs cannot use them. INF: Space-shared definitions must reference only sources the viewer may already see (no widening of owner-plane ACLs); the collectors sit inside quarry-control, a metadata service, so pack execution belongs in the orchestrator or edge rather than in control.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reframe Phase 1 around what is real: (a) make non-monitor schedules fire by extending workflowFor and giving scheduled Scrape/Crawl/Batch workflows a per-fire run_id like ChangeMonitorWF; (b) define a saved job definition as a Source plus a request-level options bundle and plumb it through InternalRunPage, or drop the Go RunPolicy presets, and do not expose /v1/presets until its policy is enforced; (c) rename the overloaded 'preset' term. Demote Phase 2 (QuarryPack manifest, registry, /v1/packs, schema form) until Phase 1 ships and a second consumer exists, and wire the collectors only as first-party workflows.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall. Phase 1 is M if RunPolicy plumbing is dropped in favour of request-level options (schedule mapping S to M, edge exposure S) and L if the policy must be enforced in the Rust runtime; Phase 2 is L.
verevon.verdictReason: Presets are not a user-reachable surface today and are decorative at execution time, schedules for scrape/crawl/batch silently never run, and a Sources registry already covers much of "save as preset"; the item should be reworded around schedule execution and options plumbing, with packs demoted.

items.title: Run- and turn-scoped tabs: deterministic cleanup, persisted tab sets and cold restore under a live-page budget
items.summary: Have the Model Plane send turn_id and parent_run_id on every proposed browser action. Quarry records them, supports tab marks (deliverable, handoff), exposes a turn_ended endpoint that the Model Plane calls on turn end, interrupt and sub-agent stop (closing unmarked agent-opened tabs, downloads and blobs), and lets child runs reuse the parent's browser context under the parent's grant with narrower budgets. || Extend Quarry's existing AgentRunCheckpoint, which today stores one current_url, page hash, constraints, viewport, zdr, grant id and control mode, with the full tab list (URL, title, a bounded history window, active tab, agent or user flag). Resume then means a new lease plus lazy tab restore, and reopening a chat thread shows its tabs. Add a live-page budget in the lease scheduler that protects the active, agent-controlled, loading and downloading tabs and evicts by inactivity, restoring from the checkpoint on demand. Nothing is persisted under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Deterministic cleanup at turn end is ZDR-friendly (no leftover pages or downloads) and keeps agent context small. Sub-agent sharing lets Model Plane multi-agent runs cooperate in one browser without duplicating grants. || A paused agent run or a HITL handoff can resume on the same pages, and idle Chromium pages stop costing money. It is also what makes co-browsing durable across a closed laptop.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (tab marks plus a once-only turn-ended tracker)
others: Codex in-app browser (iab-034 thread-keyed tabs, iab-035 history snapshots, iab-031 live-page budget)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; unique || 1 of 3 sources (Codex); unique as a complete lifecycle.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A registry maps sessionId to {conversationId, windowId, owner, disposeAfterSessionActivity}; child sessions inherit the parent route with dispose=true. Every tool call carries (session_id, turn_id); tabs opened in a turn get no mark. turnEnded(session, turn) clears session downloads and blobs, restores clipboards, detaches the debugger, then closes tabs with no mark, keeps deliverable tabs as output and keeps handoff tabs for the next turn (latest mark wins). A tracker keyed (session, turn) ensures cleanup runs exactly once, and Interrupt, Stop and SubagentStop hooks all call it. || Merged items add: Key pages by (conversationId, tabId). Persist {navigation:{currentIndex, entries[{url, title, pageState}]}, favicon, title}. Budget: at most N (32) live pages; protect active, agent-controlled, audible, capturing, loading and downloading tabs; evict by inactivity rank; restore lazily by recreating the page and replaying history.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/step_receipts.rs:39-71 (AgentRunCheckpoint: single current_url, no tab list or history)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:1436-1446 (resume_checkpoint; ZDR checkpoints refused; lease ttl defaults to 120 s)
verevonToday.gap: Each agent run already gets its own CDP BrowserContext scoped to (org, actor, run) with tabs per run, behind broker grants. There is no turn concept, no tab marks, no cleanup on Model Plane interrupt or stop, and no parent/child run sharing for sub-agents (fleets are budgets only). window.open is rewritten to the same tab. || A durable single-URL run checkpoint and a resume path exist, but tabs, per-tab history, titles and an agent/user flag are not persisted, there is no binding of a tab set to a chat thread, and there is no live-page budget. The comparator's status of absent was corrected after reading the checkpoint struct.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: tab records keyed by Model Plane run and turn ids with deliverable/handoff/temporary marks and one turnEnded cleanup per (session, turn), also on interrupt and sub-agent stop (Codex); persisted tab set per run with a live-page budget and cold restore (non-ZDR only). Depends on the reaper (F-t2-006) and durable sessions (F-t2-035). || Source detail: [R-t2-05-11] Model Plane passes turn_id and parent_run_id on every proposed browser action (additive to the existing action contract). Quarry, as executor, records them, adds mark-tab actions and a turn_ended endpoint, runs cleanup at most once per (run, turn) and on the reaper path from R-t2-05-04, and lets child runs attach to the parent context while keeping their own step budgets. Never auto-close user-opened or takeover tabs. || [R-t2-08-10] Ingestion Plane: extend AgentRunCheckpoint (and its Postgres writer in postgres_step_receipts.rs) with a bounded tab list and history window; implement restore as lease plus navigate; add a scheduler budget with protection rules. Coordinate with R-t2-03-08 (durable session store, suspend/resume) and R-t2-05-11 (turn-scoped tab cleanup) so there is one session state machine. Frontend Plane: reopening a thread rehydrates its tabs.
dependencies: Model Plane run/turn ids on browser actions
items.risks: Closing a tab the user is co-browsing; protect user-opened and takeover tabs. Additive contract change must stay backwards compatible with existing callers. || Restored pages may differ (login expiry); stored URLs are sensitive, so scope them per tenant and never persist under ZDR; overlap with R-t2-03-08 can lead to two competing session models.

verevon.exactGap: Each agent run gets one per-session browser context with in-memory tabs, but tabs are REST/UI operations (agent_routes new_tab/select_tab/close_tab, gateway tab routes, BrowserChrome tab strip) because AgentAction has no tab verbs and window.open and target=_blank are rewritten into the same tab, so there are no agent-opened tabs to clean up today. Cleanup already happens at run level (execution-core always calls close_run when its loop ends, including on approval pause), and there is no turn concept, no turn_id or parent_run_id on StepRequest, no tab marks or turn_ended endpoint, no reaper or idle expiry for abandoned runs, no per-tab checkpoint (AgentRunCheckpoint stores one current_url and page hash), no live-page budget, and nothing in the Model Plane or gateway ever sends resume_run_id although Quarry supports it.
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:3240-3300,3697-3713 (new_tab/list/select/close tab REST handlers, grant revalidation per tab)

apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:969-995 (window.open and target=_blank rewritten to location.assign in the same tab), 2447-2520 (list_tabs/new_tab over in-memory pages)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/quarry_agent.rs:182-212 (StartRunRequest/StepRequest: no turn_id, parent_run_id or resume_run_id)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent.rs:755-775 (loop always calls close_run, also on WaitingApproval)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:2615-2650 (sub-agent child runs register parent_run_id in session-core, not in Quarry; none for ZDR)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/browser-broker/internal/grant/grant.go:39-69 (Grant has ParentGrantID only for sensitive approvals; in-memory store)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:78-84 (resume_run_id still needs crash/restart rehydration tests)
reuse: AgentRunCheckpoint + postgres_step_receipts writer (add a bounded tab list and history window)
resume_run_id path in start_run (new lease plus persisted profile plus fresh grant)
chromiumoxide list_tabs/new_tab and the gateway tab proxy routes plus BrowserChrome tab strip
session-core managed child runs with parent_run_id as the Model Plane source of lineage
quarry-runtime RuntimeLeasePool/HostScheduler patterns for a live-page budget
verevon.constraints: Model proposes / Quarry executes: turn_id and parent_run_id can only be additive fields on the Model Plane StepRequest, and Quarry must not read Model Plane run state; authority stays with broker grants (the grant store is in-memory, so a resumed run needs a fresh grant and a child run needs an explicit child grant rather than reusing ParentGrantID, which today binds sensitive approvals). ZDR: nothing is persisted and ZDR checkpoints are refused, so cold restore is non-ZDR only; stored tab URLs are sensitive and tenant-scoped. This overlaps the durable-session item (F-t2-035): there must be one session state machine, not two.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Demote and re-scope. First decide whether a chat thread keeps one long-lived Quarry run across turns (today one Model Plane run equals one Quarry run, closed at loop end); turn-scoped cleanup only matters then. Add agent tab verbs to AgentAction before building cleanup for agent-opened tabs. Fold persisted tab sets and cold restore into the F-t2-035 checkpoint work (extend AgentRunCheckpoint, wire resume_run_id into execution-core's StartRunRequest, add the rehydration test). Build the live-page budget only after a per-org/per-run session cap and an idle reaper exist (F-t2-025, F-t2-006). Child-run context sharing needs a broker child-grant design first.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the full item; several prerequisites (tab verbs, reaper, resume wiring, child grants) are outside it.
verevon.verdictReason: The premise (agent-opened tabs left behind, Quarry recording turn ids) does not match the code: agents cannot open tabs, the Model Plane already closes the run at loop end, and the useful remainder (tab persistence, cold restore) depends on unbuilt prerequisites, so it belongs after durable sessions and caps.

items.title: Crawl planning: validate/preview endpoint, Model Plane crawl-plan tool and a stronger /v1/map
items.summary: Add POST /v1/crawl/validate (a dry run that returns normalised effective options, violations and an estimated page count), a Model Plane crawl-planning tool that maps up to 50 site URLs, drafts crawl options from a plain-language goal and validates them, and a proposal-review step in the KnowledgeComposer before the crawl starts. Strengthen /v1/map by seeding from robots Sitemap: lines, adding an optional site: search pass through the smart router, reranking candidates through the Data Plane rerank contract, raising the limit and letting the planner call it with a service scope.
items.whyItMatters: This matches the architecture exactly: the Model proposes crawl options, Quarry validates and executes or rejects, and the user sees the proposal for approval. It gives non-technical users a one-sentence way to scope a crawl and gives the planner better discovery on docs sites with weak sitemaps.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-009 params-preview; fc-013 map)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: NL crawl planning: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl), unique; site map: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl), where Verevon is already at parity
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Map up to 50 URLs of the site to ground the LLM, prompt it with URL structure plus the user goal, produce crawl options, overlay only the fields the caller did not set, re-run the normal validator (including pattern caps), then either return the options as a preview or start the crawl; the ZDR path runs the LLM step outside traces.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/routes.rs:533-668 (no prompt field or validate endpoint on crawl)
verevonToday.gap: No crawl preview or validate endpoint and no Model Plane tool that proposes crawl options; /v1/map caps limit at 1000, does not read robots Sitemap: lines, has no search assist, ranks lexically, and is user-token-only so the Model Plane cannot call it. Map itself is shipped end to end (CrawlPagePicker), so only the planning layer is new.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: add /v1/crawl/validate reusing the CrawlRequest validator from R-t2-01-03; extend map_routes.rs with robots Sitemap: seeding, an optional site: pass gated by allow_paid_providers, and a Data Plane rerank call (the data:rerank manifest row is already granted) instead of building ranking in Quarry; add a map:read service scope. Model Plane: crawl-planning tool that calls /v1/map, drafts options through the model and calls validate. Frontend: KnowledgeComposer shows scope, limit and sample URLs for approval before the gateway starts the crawl under the user token.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (validate, map) with Model Plane (planner tool) and Frontend Plane (review UI)
items.risks: LLM-drafted regexes can be over-broad, so always show scope and limit before running; site: queries cost paid-provider budget; the planning LLM call must be suppressed from traces for ZDR.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: /v1/map is shipped end to end (map_routes.rs:132-300, gateway discover_crawl_pages at knowledge/quarry.rs:507-535, CrawlPagePicker.tsx with KnowledgeComposer.tsx:538-556 and a user-curated batch capped at 200 by normalize_batch_body), so only the planning layer is new. SRC: there is no /v1/crawl/validate and CrawlRequest carries only url, max_pages, max_depth, ingest and zdr (routes.rs:533-554), so there are no scope options for a validate call to normalise until F-t2-016 lands; map seeds only {origin}/sitemap.xml plus five nested indexes and ignores the Sitemap: lines that robots.rs:80-82 already parses, caps at 1000 and ranks lexically only (map_routes.rs:22,189-212,266). SRC: the Model Plane cannot call map because service principals are limited to scrape/search/extract/artifacts/agent (auth.rs:514-535) and execution-core web_tools declares only search:read and extract:read (web_tools.rs:39-40), and crawl and batch are refused under ZDR (routes.rs:563-575).
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/contracts/cross-plane-token-requests.json:29-39 (web-rerank granted:true; rerank only for caller-supplied candidates)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/CROSS_PLANE_INTEGRATION.md:70-75 (rerank degrades to lexical order when the token is unavailable)
reuse: CrawlPagePicker and the gateway discover route (extend to show an agent-proposed scope instead of a new review step)
quarry-transform robots parser already collecting Sitemap: lines
Data Plane web-rerank row (granted) for candidate ordering, with lexical fallback
gateway normalize_batch_body 200-URL cap and the durable /v1/batch path
execution-core web_tools.rs wrapper pattern for a new map tool with a map:read scope
verevon.constraints: SRC: /v1/crawl and /v1/batch are durable and refused under ZDR (routes.rs:563-575), so a ZDR plan can be proposed but not run and the planning tool must say so early; map itself is read-only and ZDR-safe (map_routes.rs:6-7). Model proposes / Quarry executes: LLM-drafted options remain a proposal that the user approves and the gateway starts under the user token, as the item says; a site: search pass spends paid-provider budget; the planning LLM call must be kept out of traces for ZDR orgs.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Cut the validate endpoint to a thin map-based preview (count plus samples, no normalised effective options) until F-t2-016 adds crawl scope options; do not build a new proposal-review UI, extend CrawlPagePicker to display an agent-proposed scope; add the map:read service scope and robots Sitemap: seeding first (both S), then the Model Plane planning tool, and call the Data Plane rerank row only when its token is available, degrading to the lexical ranker.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: map hardening and the service scope are S, the planner tool is M, and validate is blocked on F-t2-016.
verevon.verdictReason: Map and the user-curated page picker already exist; the item should state the genuine delta (planner tool, service scope, robots Sitemap seeding, optional rerank, thin validate) and its dependency on F-t2-016 instead of presenting map and review as new.

items.title: Provider APIs and export rewrites before rendering (Google Docs, GitHub, Notion, transcripts), after verifying current coverage
items.summary: Add a URL normaliser with a rewrite table (Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Drive links to export URLs, preserving gid) and a ProviderResolver in Quarry that, for hosts matching a connected provider, calls integration-corev2's action API with the requesting user's identity and returns a normal scrape result. Add config-driven domain-pattern to driver overrides next to the presets, and route fetched export files through the file routing from R-t2-03-04. || Add a transcript format that reads public caption tracks (no cookies by default; any cookie use requires a BrowserBroker sensitive-action grant), with a capability-advertising pattern (supported-URL patterns cached briefly, typed unsupported error). Route Google Docs, Sheets and Slides export to integration-corev2 provider actions with OAuth rather than browser cookies, and skip raw audio/video download. || Check two unknowns. First, whether the Data Plane document import and chat-attachment conversion already give the same HTML/PDF/office/e-book/image to markdown quality as the scrape pipeline; if so close it, if not extend the Data Plane import rather than adding a Quarry /v1/parse route. Second, whether integration-corev2 has Google Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides export actions and whether Quarry has a YouTube transcript extractor; prefer OAuth provider actions over browser-session export and add a YouTube transcript extractor only if missing.
items.whyItMatters: Pasting a Google Docs, GitHub or Notion link into Verevon should return a faithful document, not a rendered login wall or a ToS-risky scrape. integration-corev2 already owns OAuth tokens and provider actions, so the bridge is an API call, not new connectors. || Agents often need a video transcript or the text of a Google Doc. For documents, OAuth provider actions fit Verevon's authority and audit model better than reusing a user's browser session. || A single conversion stack keeps markdown quality consistent for chat attachments and ingested web pages, and exporting Google Docs natively beats scraping rendered Docs. Both are probably partly covered by the Data Plane and the Integration Plane already, so the first step is to avoid duplicating work across planes.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl official-API engines and rewriteUrl (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-022 and -023, SRC)
others: Codex in-app browser (automation-and-safety-112: strict URL validation, type-to-format allowlist, signed-in session export)
Firecrawl (api-surface fc-019 signed upload then parse through the same format stack) and Codex in-app browser (in-app-browser-003 site-specific export via the page session, DOC only)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: URL normaliser with a rewrite table (regex to export URL, for example docs/spreadsheets/presentation/drive ids to export endpoints keeping gid). Engine resolver: if the host matches a provider and the org has a connected account, call the provider action and return a ScrapeResult; API engines take part in the waterfall with high quality scores. Config map domain_pattern to forced driver. || Merged items add: Validate the URL against an allowlist pattern (for example docs.google.com /d/<id>, not /pub); map document type to allowed export formats; fetch the export URL with session cookies inside the browser context and store the file as an artifact. Media: GET a supported-urls list (cached), reject unsupported URLs with a typed error, POST a download request with cookies and a long timeout, return an artifact URL. || File parse: POST /parse/upload-url returns an HMAC-signed uploadRef (10-minute TTL, 50 MB cap, org-bound); the client PUTs to object storage; POST /parse {uploadRef, formats} runs the document converters and returns the same Document shape. Export: site adapters keyed by URL pattern call the site's own export endpoints with the session cookies and return an artifact (Verevon should use OAuth provider actions instead, for credential isolation).

items.approach: Step 0 (from R-t2-01-12): verify what the Data Plane import and integration-corev2 Google/Microsoft providers already cover. Then a planner override hook that sends matching URLs to connected-account provider actions over the integration-corev2 API, export-URL rewrites whose output goes through the file router (F-t2-009), and public-caption transcripts. No cookie-replay site APIs. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-10] Ingestion Plane: (1) rewrite table in the URL normaliser (S, no cross-plane dependency). (2) ProviderResolver in quarry-runtime that calls integration-corev2 over its API (no cross-plane DB access) with the caller's identity and returns content plus the provider's ACL metadata; ACLs must propagate into Data Plane ingestion and ZDR must propagate to integration-corev2. (3) domain_pattern to driver overrides in the preset config, consumed by the planner in R-t2-03-06. Use only the requesting user's own connection. || [R-t2-02-12] Integration Plane (integration-corev2): provider actions for Google Docs/Sheets/Slides and Microsoft documents with OAuth export (owned by the integration category). Ingestion Plane: a transcript format using public caption tracks, no cookies by default, with BrowserBroker grants for any session-authenticated variant; no raw media download. || [R-t2-01-12] Read the Data Plane v2 import and chat-attachment conversion code to compare formats and OCR, and the integration-corev2 provider action list for Google Workspace; then decide per item. Data Plane owns documents; Integration Plane owns provider actions; Quarry adds only a YouTube transcript extractor if absent.
dependencies: integration-corev2 action API for document fetch
F-t2-009 (export files are PDFs or Office files)
items.risks: Must not widen access: user-scoped connections only; provider ACLs and ZDR must propagate; provider rate limits and token expiry need clear errors. || Site terms and copyright for media download; cookie exfiltration risk; overlap with the Integration Plane category. || Duplicating document conversion across planes; using browser sessions for export conflicts with credential isolation.

verevon.exactGap: integration-corev2 already ships the provider reads this item wants: Google drive.file.content with exportAs=text or Office export (service.go:300, drive_read.go:30-60 and 594-615), Microsoft drive.file.content (service.go:219), GitHub contents.get and readme.get (service.go:348, 366) and list-only Notion databases and pages (service.go:463-466), and the SPA picker reaches the content ops through the gateway allowlist (browse.rs:33-41). Model Plane agents call integration-corev2 directly (integration_tools.rs:1-30) but the agent catalog omits every content op (integration_tools.rs:98-141), so those calls classify as unknown-means-write and need approval (permission/mod.rs:195-218), and any provider result shown to the model is cut at 2000 characters (integration_tools.rs:54, 817-825). Quarry itself has no URL rewrite table, no provider resolver, no transcript or caption format and no /v1/parse, and no Quarry crate references integration-corev2.
reuse: integration-corev2 Service.Execute actions (Google, Microsoft, GitHub contents/readme) and its OAuth broker
Model Plane integration_tools client, in particular read_action_json with an integration:read token (cannot perform writes)
Gateway browse allowlist and chat document extraction route /api/v1/chat/documents/extract
quarry-transform docx.rs and pdf.rs plus the existing quarry-edge file routing for export bytes that arrive as files
Model Plane fetch chokepoints (model-gateway fetch_url / deep_research, execution-core web_fetch) where the user's identity already exists
verevon.constraints: Provider reads must run on the requesting user's own connection: integration-corev2 owns the tokens and Model Plane already reaches it with an Auth Core ingestion-audience token minted per org and session (integration_tools.rs:20-23, 494-540). Quarry has no such path, so a Quarry ProviderResolver would add a new cross-plane service identity that must still carry the end user, and would put provider ACL and ZDR propagation inside the scraper. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so provider ACL metadata must travel with ingested content into the Data Plane, and ZDR must propagate to integration-corev2 and to any stored export. Reusing browser-session cookies for export is excluded by credential isolation; Notion content needs a new integration-corev2 action because pages are list-only.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Move provider-URL routing out of Quarry. (1) Add a dedicated read-only document tool at the Model Plane or gateway (URL to provider and file id, then drive.file.content with exportAs=text for Google, drive.file.content for Microsoft, contents.get or readme.get for GitHub) that decodes content to bounded text or stores it in the working set; merely adding catalog rows is not enough because content ops return base64 and the model only sees the first 2000 characters. (2) In Quarry keep only a small public-URL rewrite table (link-shared Google export URLs) whose output goes through the file router. (3) Demote the YouTube or caption transcript format, nothing exists and it needs a cookie-free design. Step 0 answers: no document converter was found under Data Plane v2 services (negative grep); chat attachments convert through the gateway (chat.rs:68, 1 MB and 60k character caps in prepare-chat-attachments.ts) and Quarry has its own docx.rs and pdf.rs, so a Quarry /v1/parse route is not justified without a quality comparison; the integration-corev2 Google and Microsoft content ops are not yet verified against live providers (drive_read.go header, task F10).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in total, but the bundle should be split: the document tool is S to M, the Quarry rewrite table is S, the transcript format is M and demoted.
verevon.verdictReason: The item says integration-corev2 coverage was not inspected; it is substantial, and the real gap is routing plus agent-visible content tools, not new connectors or a Quarry ProviderResolver. Reword to the Model Plane or gateway chokepoint and drop the Quarry to integration-corev2 design.

items.title: Engine planner v2: declared capability matrix, typed re-plan signals with budgets, learned per-domain mode and a domain-intelligence registry
items.summary: Replace plan_from_signals's five booleans with a FeatureFlags set and a static per-driver capability matrix (reusing BrowserDriverCapabilities for browser drivers), so callers never name a driver and each plan can be explained in receipts. Let drivers and content checkers return a typed Replan {NeedsBrowser, NeedsStealth, IsFile, Drop(flag)} under a ScrapeBudget {max_attempts, per_flag_flips, deadline}, and make static-to-browser hedging an opt-in preset. Add a DomainRenderProfile store (host-level verdicts only, ZDR-safe) fed by FallbackDriver escalations and a 5-10 percent dual-run sampler on crawls, with operator approval before a learned verdict is promoted. || Build the planned per-domain registry in quarry-control and give it two first consumers. (1) Passive, non-ZDR learning of which driver (static, TLS, browser) works per domain, using deterministic text similarity in Rust, feeding DriverPlan. (2) A trusted site-guidance field (rate hints, playbooks, 'do not automate' notes) that Quarry attaches to observations as labelled trusted metadata for the Model, separate from page content.
items.whyItMatters: Today every request to a JS-only site pays a static attempt plus a hydration settle, and adding a stealth tier, remote provider, file parser or provider-API engine means editing branching code. A declared matrix and typed re-plan make cost and tail latency bounded and auditable, which fits Verevon's receipts-first design, and learned verdicts cut browser cost on large crawls. || Cheaper and faster crawls with fewer wasted browser launches and fewer block events, and a clean way to steer the Model with trusted site knowledge that does not come from the untrusted page, reducing prompt-injection exposure.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl engine matrix, hedged waterfall and typed re-plan (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-001, -002, -003, -004, SRC); Apify AdaptivePlaywrightCrawler for the learned mode (apify-platform-055, DOC)
others: Firecrawl API surface feature flags (firecrawl-api-surface-061, SRC)
Firecrawl engpicker (SRC) for learned verdicts; Codex in-app browser (SRC) for the trusted guidance channel
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources for each facet (firecrawl for matrix and re-plan, apify for learned mode), unique || 1 of 4 sources for each (Firecrawl, Codex); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: buildFeatureFlags(request) -> Set<Flag>; each engine declares {flag: bool} plus a quality number; candidates are engines whose unsupported-flag weight is below a threshold, sorted by (supported weight desc, quality desc). Loop: start engine[i], select over in-flight results and a timer(maxReasonableTime_i); on timer start engine[i+1] while keeping the others; the first acceptable result wins and losers are aborted (acceptable = non-empty markdown for 2xx/304; non-2xx pass through with status). NeedsFeature{flag, prefetch?} or DropFeature{flag} errors re-run planning under a retry tracker (about 6 total attempts, per-flag caps). Learned mode: per registrable domain keep {p_browser_needed, samples}; with probability 0.1 run both HTTP and browser and compare outputs; otherwise use the predicted mode and fall back to browser if a checker rejects the HTTP result. Rust: const ENGINE_MATRIX, pure plan(flags, registered), tokio::select! over FuturesUnordered with AbortHandles. || Merged items add: Verdicts: a background job samples about 10 indexed pages per domain, scrapes each with Chrome and with a TLS client, judges success, computes text similarity and stores a verdict (TlsClientOk, ChromeCdpRequired, Uncertain) that the scrape path looks up in about 250 ms to boost the cheap engine. Guidance: a trusted operator proxy sets a header on document responses; the runtime captures it through CDP Fetch, strips it before the page sees it, keys it by (tab, URL), clears it on navigation, delivers it once to the model as trusted metadata, ignores private hosts, and suppresses it once credentials were used.

verevonToday.gap: No declared capability matrix, no typed escalation vocabulary, no budget object, no hedging, no per-domain memory of the rendering verdict and no sampled dual-mode comparison. Per-request JS-shell detection, soft-404 and challenge classification already exist and are richer than Firecrawl's empty-page gate. || FallbackDriver escalates per request (JS-shell detection, block statuses, prior_block_signals) but nothing is learned or persisted per domain, and no site-guidance field exists on observations. The registry is only planned (Phase 4 of the reliability proposal; the improvements doc marks site profiles GREENFIELD). The CDP Fetch guard and pinned browser egress proxy are in place as the hook for guidance injection.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: callers state needs and the planner picks the engine from a declared matrix (Firecrawl), typed AddFeature/RemoveFeature re-plan signals with retry budgets, HTTP-first with sampled browser comparison to learn a per-domain mode (Apify, DOC), stored in the planned domain-intelligence registry with operator approval for promotion (SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md Phase 4). || Source detail: [R-t2-03-06] Ingestion Plane, quarry-runtime: (1) FeatureFlags + ENGINE_MATRIX + pure plan() replacing the booleans, recording chosen and dropped engines in the scrape determinism stamp. (2) enum Replan and ScrapeBudget driving FallbackDriver, with the content checker returning Replan values (R-t2-03-04 becomes Replan::IsFile). (3) DomainRenderProfile (Postgres + Redis cache keyed by registrable domain, org-scoped or global for public hosts only) fed by escalations and a 5-10 percent sampler on crawls; DriverPlan reads it as a prior; operator approval before promotion, as in the Sovereign Scraping proposal. Hedge only idempotent GETs, never for profile-bound or ZDR runs where egress receipts must be one-per-request, and respect HostScheduler AIMD and robots politeness. ZDR orgs store host-level verdicts only, never content. || [R-t2-04-12] Ingestion Plane: after the registry schema exists in quarry-control (Postgres), record per-domain outcomes passively from production runs (driver used, shell detected, block reason from R-t2-04-03) for non-ZDR orgs only, compute a verdict with deterministic similarity in Rust (no model calls inside Quarry, optionally ask Model Plane), with TTL and re-calibration, and feed it into DriverPlan. Proposed profile changes need operator approval, as the reliability doc already requires. For guidance, populate it from the registry inside Quarry (no external header needed) and attach it as a labelled trusted field on observations returned to Model Plane; if a header channel is ever used it must come only from Verevon's own egress proxy, never from a response of an arbitrary site.
dependencies: F-t2-009 (file routing as first typed Replan)
Registered remote drivers (F-t2-059) to make the matrix meaningful
items.risks: Over-engineering if only three drivers ever exist (keep the matrix small); hedging doubles origin load and can trip rate limits; stale learned verdicts after a site redesign; sampled dual runs double cost; cross-org sharing of verdicts must not leak tenant behaviour. || Stale verdicts when sites change (TTL and re-calibration). A compromised registry could steer agents, so authorship is operator-only. Value is cost and robustness rather than a user-visible capability.

verevon.exactGap: plan_from_signals maps five request signals to one of three plans in a fixed static, TLS, browser order (driver_plan.rs:36-50; the TLS plan always uses TlsProfile::default() and url_type is declared but never read) and FallbackDriver escalates per request on block statuses and JS-shell detection (fallback_driver.rs:56-140) with no per-domain memory; DriverKind has only Static, Browser and Tls (output.rs:239-243), and BrowserDriverCapabilities (browser-agent flags such as persistent_profile and full_visual_fidelity) is not read by the scrape planner. There is no capability matrix, typed Replan, budget object, hedging, sampled dual-run, learned domain store or site-guidance field; the registry is only proposed (SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md Phase 4) and the only trace in code is a placeholder shared_domain_intel_id on fleets (fleet.rs:49, 014_fleets.sql).
reuse: FallbackDriver escalation logic and needs_browser_escalation (per-request JS-shell, block-status and soft-404 handling is already richer than a simple empty-page gate).
Serving driver already recorded per page (NormalizedOutput driver info, output.rs:19, and page_extracted.driver) as the passive signal for a per-domain verdict store.
quarry-control Postgres store and migrations (014_fleets.sql pattern) for a domain profile table.
The proposed schema and approval rules in SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md Phase 4 (operator approval before promotion).
CDP Fetch network guard and pinned browser egress proxy (chromiumoxide.rs:695-730) only as enforcement points, not as a guidance channel.
verevon.constraints: ZDR: record verdicts only from non-ZDR traffic (which hosts an org visits is itself retention-relevant); ZDR callers may read global verdicts but not contribute, and dual-run sampling or hedging must never run for ZDR or profile-bound runs. Trusted site guidance cannot ride inside the observation: the trust class of a browser_agent tool result is a pure function of the tool name and wholly untrusted (moderation.rs:204-240), so guidance needs a separate Model-Plane-owned channel (execution-core injecting operator-authored guidance for the run's allowed domains), operator-authored only. Promotion of learned verdicts needs an operator approval surface, and no operator or admin UI for Quarry was found. A capability matrix keyed on three DriverKind variants is premature until remote drivers are registered (the edge registers only static, TLS, Browserbase or local chromiumoxide, main.rs:290-340).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Defer the declared matrix and typed Replan/ScrapeBudget refactor until a fourth driver exists (F-t2-059), since per-request escalation already works and the refactor is mostly internal. Narrow the item to a per-domain render-mode memory: host to {js_required, last_good_driver, ttl} in quarry-control Postgres, written passively from non-ZDR page results, read as a prior in plan_from_signals, promotion by operator approval per the Phase 4 doc. Split the trusted site-guidance idea into its own Model Plane item with the separate-channel design above.
verevon.effortNote: M for the narrowed per-domain memory slice; the full item as described (matrix, typed Replan with budgets, hedging, dual-run sampler, registry, guidance) remains L.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial and mostly an internal efficiency and robustness refactor with little user-visible value: per-request escalation already exists, only three drivers are registered, the registry is already planned (Phase 4), and the guidance part is placed on a channel the Model Plane treats as untrusted. Demote and narrow to the per-domain render-mode memory.

items.title: Scrape request context and egress tiers: locale/geo/mobile emulation, country egress with policy-gated auto-escalation, profile pinning and cache partitioning
items.summary: Add profile_id, location {country, languages} and a mobile/device preset to ScrapeRequest and to lease creation. When a profile is set, the planner must use only profile-capable browser drivers, never the static/TLS tiers, never read or write the scrape cache, and stamp the profile scope into receipts. Apply Emulation.setLocaleOverride, setTimezoneOverride, setGeolocationOverride, setDeviceMetricsOverride and setUserAgentOverride at context creation, tag proxy-pool entries with a country, and include (country, languages, mobile) in the cache key. || Extend ProxyPool and EgressBroker with a vendor-neutral tier (direct/first-party, basic datacenter, enhanced residential or mobile) and an optional country, exposed as proxy: auto|basic|enhanced and country on scrape and agent runs. The broker plans basic first and escalates to enhanced only on rate-limit, transport or region-block outcomes when org policy allows it. The Model never picks the proxy. In a second phase turn the in-memory (host, proxy) health into a SessionPool that scores identities (proxy, cookie jar, fingerprint) and retires bad ones.
items.whyItMatters: The UI is Norwegian-first, so localized pricing and content matter. Scraping behind a login is only safe for knowledge ingestion if personalised pages can never leak across tenants through a shared cache and if the content inherits the owner's ACL. || Higher success on geo-restricted and rate-limited public sites for both user browsing and agent research, and localized results for market-research use cases, without a per-request choice by the Model. Verevon currently has only a flat proxy list, no geo control in the gateway or UI, and no identity health beyond a 60 s cooldown.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (profile routing firecrawl-engine-and-infra-018; location and mobile firecrawl-api-surface-060 and firecrawl-engine-and-infra-014, SRC)
others: Apify locale-constrained fingerprints and proxy country (DOC, mentioned in the comparator note rather than in this category's records)
Firecrawl (SRC) for the user contract; Apify (DOC) for the knob set and Crawlee SessionPool
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources for each (firecrawl), unique; geo is common in hosted scrapers || Tiers and geo proxies: 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Apify), table-stakes for scrapers. Session health: 1 of 4 (Apify), unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Planner: if request.profile is set, candidate engines are the browser engines that support profiles (parsers only with bytes the browser downloaded). Cache layer: personalised = headers || actions || profile means no cache lookup and no cache store. location validates an ISO alpha-2 country (special pools gated by team permission), chooses egress by country, sets Accept-Language from languages[], timezone from country default, optional coordinates, and mobile sets device metrics plus UA; cache key includes (country, languages, mobile). || Merged items add: Request field proxy: basic|enhanced|auto (default auto). Attempt 1 uses the basic pool. On a block signal (401/403/429 or a challenge hint) a typed 'needs stronger egress' error is caught by the waterfall, which retries once on the enhanced pool inside the same retry budget, with the timeout raised for stronger tiers. Pool choice is encoded as (group, country, sticky session id). Policy can pin the maximum tier per org (Safe Mode forces basic). A SessionPool holds N sessions (proxy session id, cookie jar, score): markGood decays the score, markBad raises it, a blocked status retires the session, and state persists across restarts.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/driver_plan.rs:19-41 (profile_required forces the browser; it is only ever set from the client-supplied `signals` body field, routes.rs:357 and :440, and no profile id can be passed to scrape)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:194-244 (launch flags only; no UA/locale/timezone/geolocation override)
verevonToday.gap: Scrape cannot run with a profile at all (profiles exist only on agent sessions), so the 'authenticated content never enters a shared cache' rule is only trivially true today and must ship with any profile-on-scrape feature. No locale, timezone, geolocation or device presets, and no country egress selection; search has country and language but the browser does not. || The proxy pool is a flat env list (QUARRY_PROXY_POOL) with sticky (org, host) hashing, processor-approval gating, per-run affinity and a DNS-pinned browser egress proxy, which is richer than either reference at the plumbing level. Missing: tier or class, country, residential or mobile integration, any request-level proxy field, tier escalation, and any proxy or geo control in the gateway or UI. EgressBroker keeps in-memory (host, proxy) health with a 60 s block cooldown and 3 attempts, but there is no session object binding proxy, cookie jar and fingerprint, no retirement or score decay, and no persistence across instances.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: locale, timezone, geolocation and mobile emulation per page (needs per-page emulation from F-t2-007), country-targeted egress tiers behind the processor-approval gate with auto-escalation only on 401/403/429 within the retry budget and capped by the org policy floor (F-t2-022), authenticated-profile pinning for scrape (profiles never use the shared cache), and options partitioning the cache. Session health retirement is phase 2. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-05] Ingestion Plane: add profile_id, location and mobile to ScrapeRequest and BrowserLease; set profile_required internally (ignore the client `signals` value for it), reject static/TLS fallback and cache admission when set, record the profile scope in receipts; apply CDP overrides at context creation (uses the per-page emulation from R-t2-03-01); add country tags to QUARRY_PROXY_POOL entries and a PrivacyPolicy check for third-party proxy processors. Data Plane ingestion must give scraped authenticated content the owner's ACL. Frontend Plane: device/locale picker in BrowserChrome and pass the user's locale instead of the fixed viewport. || [R-t2-04-07] Ingestion Plane. Phase 1: add ProxyTier plus country tags to ProxyPool entries; add proxy and country fields to /v1/scrape, crawl and agent-run requests; EgressBroker plans basic first and escalates to enhanced only for 429, repeated transport failure or an explicit region-block signal, and only when the org policy floor (R-t2-04-05) allows enhanced; never escalate to get past a strong bot signal (R-t2-04-03, INF adaptation of Firecrawl's 401/403/429 trigger). Record tier and country in the existing redacted egress receipts and in usage so Control Plane can meter per-GB cost and entitlement. Every vendor stays a registered third-party processor under the PrivacyPolicy gate, and ZDR orgs may only use processors with ZDR terms. Phase 2: promote broker health to a SessionPool keyed (org, host-group) with EWMA error scores and retirement; keep it in memory for ZDR orgs and use Redis with TTL otherwise; keep agent-run affinity sticky and, when blocked mid-run, propose a choice to the user instead of silently rotating mid-login. Follow the egress-tier and session-health phases already drafted in SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md.
