items.title: Register governed remote browser backends (Kernel, Browserless, Browserbase) behind an egress-containment proof
items.summary: Expose the backend list and each backend's capability set through the session API, register the already-implemented Kernel and Browserless drivers behind config, and implement the containment proof that lets a remote driver run governed agent sessions (route provider traffic through Quarry's pinned egress proxy or require a provider-side egress allowlist attestation). Today Browserbase is scrape-only and Quarry rightly refuses backends that cannot prove isolated_egress.
items.whyItMatters: The local lease pool is a hard-coded 2 and one Chromium process, so burst capacity and reliability for the in-app browser and AI runs need a scale-out path that does not change Model Plane tools. Capability flags keep the governance story intact.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex multi-backend Browsers.list with per-backend capability sets (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-009 and codexbrowser-automation-and-safety-139, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (codex), unique; remote browser providers are common across scrapers
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: trait BrowserBackend { kind(); capabilities() -> Caps; open_session(); ... } registered at startup from config; the session API lists available backends ({type, family, profile, metadata}) and the planner or Model chooses by required capabilities (for example needs_user_login selects an extension backend, needs_isolated_egress selects a hosted one).

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/main.rs:316-327 (Browserbase registered for the scrape path with pool 4; no Kernel or Browserless registration found)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:85-89 (SSRF and DNS-pinning gates required for every remote provider before enabling for agents)
verevonToday.gap: BrowserDriver trait and capability flags exist and the local driver ships; Browserbase cannot run agent sessions (no isolated_egress); Kernel and Browserless are implemented but unregistered; there is no backend list on the session API and no user-browser or DOM-only backend.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: register Kernel/Browserless behind config in main.rs, implement the egress-containment proof (provider traffic via Quarry's pinned proxy or an attested provider allowlist) and per-provider SSRF/redirect/subresource tests listed in the roadmap gates, then expose GET /v1/agent/backends with capabilities. Model Plane selects by required capabilities but never names a provider. Restrict managed providers to approved processor policies (ZDR, DPA).
dependencies: F-t2-007 (local pool) so remote and local capacity share one admission model
items.risks: Remote providers are data processors under ZDR and DPAs; the containment proof is hard to make real; provider outages need fallback to the local pool.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-03-09] apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md deliberate gate 2 (SSRF tests for every remote browser provider before enabling for agents) and SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md Phase 5 (managed providers only under approved processor policy)

verevon.exactGap: Capability flags and gates exist (BrowserDriverCapabilities, lib.rs:265-286; require_isolated_agent_egress and require_driver_capabilities, agent_routes.rs:1125-1217, with driver_requirements already accepted at 1305), but the agent path is hard-wired to one driver, state.agent_driver = ChromiumoxideDriver (main.rs:1283-1288), so there is nothing to register Kernel or Browserless into for agent runs; the scrape path has a single DriverKind::Browser slot that Browserbase takes before the local driver (main.rs:322-339). Kernel and Browserless are REST-only one-shot shims (kernel.rs:1-20, browserless.rs:1-12) constructed only in tests, and Browserbase never opens its connectUrl (browserbase.rs:5-12), so none of the three can serve ref-based actions, AX snapshots or live frames. The session API has a hard-coded capability list but no backend listing (browser.rs:2578, 2700), and per-run driver_capabilities are only echoed after a run exists (agent_routes.rs:543, 1658).
reuse: BrowserDriver trait, BrowserDriverCapabilities and the require_* gates in agent_routes
BrowserDriverAdapter::managed_provider with processor_id plus PrivacyPolicy.guard_third_party_processing (ZDR denies third-party processing even when the processor matches)
ChromiumoxideDriver code as the base for a CDP-attached remote driver (Browser::connect)
driver_requirements field already on the agent start body, per-run driver_capabilities in the response
ProfileStore for provider-agnostic persistent profiles; GAP.md 12.1 per-provider SSRF audit
verevon.constraints: Remote browsers are third-party processors: they need an approved processor policy and are refused under ZDR (privacy.rs tests), plus DPA review. Containment proof conflict: the pinned egress proxy endpoint type is loopback-only (lib.rs:331-360), which a remote browser cannot reach, so 'route provider traffic through Quarry's pinned proxy' contradicts that invariant, and GAP.md:450-462 records that Kernel and Browserbase only offer main-frame allowlists and that a real CDP connection is a prerequisite; the roadmap gate also requires redirect, iframe, XHR and subresource SSRF tests per provider before agent use (WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:85-89). Model proposes capability requirements and Quarry selects or rejects; the Model must never name a provider, and no driver_requirements usage was found in Model Plane Rust or Go sources.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-scope into three parts. (1) S to M, scrape path only: allow more than one managed browser driver by keying the registry beyond DriverKind::Browser (main.rs:322-339) and register Kernel or Browserless behind config with the existing managed_provider processor guard; this adds page-render burst capacity without touching agent governance. (2) XL for agent sessions: build a CDP-attached remote driver that reuses ChromiumoxideDriver over Browser::connect (the REST shims cannot do ref actions), replace the single state.agent_driver with a registry keyed by backend id, then implement and test the containment proof; keep Browserbase scrape-only until then. (3) S: expose GET /v1/agent/backends with capability sets and select by driver_requirements in start_run. Restrict managed providers to approved processor policies and non-ZDR runs.
verevon.effortNote: The item assumed the Kernel and Browserless drivers were ready to register. They are REST shims, so agent-capable remote backends need a new CDP-attached driver, a driver registry in AppState and a real containment proof.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial and already planned as a gate, but the central premise (register the implemented Kernel and Browserless drivers) is wrong for agent sessions and the proxy-based proof conflicts with the loopback-only invariant. Reword with the corrected split and a larger agent-session effort.

items.title: Isolate each browser session or tenant in its own container or VM instead of a shared Chromium
items.summary: Lease a container or microVM per browser session (per-org warm pools first, per-session later) with its own Chromium, a tmpfs profile directory, cgroup limits and egress only through the egress broker, destroyed at session end with persistent profiles exported encrypted. Either reuse Model Plane sandbox-manager leasing primitives or build a dedicated browser-pool service owned by the Ingestion Plane; the already present Browserbase, Browserless and Kernel drivers are an alternative route to provider-hosted isolation.
items.whyItMatters: Tenant isolation for a browser that both users and agents drive on arbitrary sites: a renderer exploit or cross-context leak in a shared Chromium crosses tenants. It is also needed before persistent profiles and downloads are offered more widely.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (isolated per-run containers; SOC 2 Type II; runtime technology not disclosed, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this category (Apify, DOC only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A sandbox manager leases a container or microVM per browser session or tenant: own Chromium, tmpfs profile, cgroup limits, egress through the egress broker only; destroy at session end and export persistent profiles encrypted to storage.

verevonToday.gap: Isolation is a per-session CDP browser context inside a shared quarry-edge Chromium (baseline v-browser-app-057). sandbox-manager leases only code and workspace sandboxes, and the Kernel driver, which would give VM-level isolation, is unwired. Mitigations in place: Chromium sandbox on by default, per-session contexts (the cookie-leak fix) and isolated-egress proof required for agent runs.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane owns the browser fleet (quarry-browser pool.rs): add a lease interface that can be backed by a per-org container pool or a provider driver, route CDP and frame streams through it, and keep the egress broker as the only network path. Start with per-org pools and a warm pool to hide cold-start latency; per-session microVMs later.
dependencies: sandbox-manager leasing primitives or a new browser-pool service
Item F-t2-008 for per-session cost metering
items.risks: Cold-start latency and cost; operational complexity of a fleet. The reference is documentation only, although the Verevon gap is verified in source.

verevon.exactGap: Isolation today is one Chromium per ChromiumoxideDriver (launched in ensure_browser, chromiumoxide.rs:194-262) with a per-session CDP browser context inside it (396-420); there is no container or microVM boundary per org or session. ensure_browser also relaunches that single shared Chromium, clearing every session's pages, whenever a lease asks for a different launch viewport (194-223, lease.rs:20-23), so concurrent tenants with different viewports can kill each other's runs. sandbox-manager is only a Postgres lease registry for thread/agent code scopes that hands out a sandbox://<id> string and starts nothing (server.go:84-97, lease.go:154), and the Kernel driver is a REST shim that is never registered (kernel.rs:1-20, main.rs:322-340).
reuse: ChromiumoxideDriver code (CDP, AX snapshot, live frames, download quarantine) as the worker-side implementation
BrowserEgressProxyProvider (per-session pinned DNS-pinning proxy with receipts)
RuntimeLeasePool / LeasePool (affinity key, TTL, semaphore admission)
ProfileStore (tenant-scoped profile snapshots, keyed org_id + profile_id) for exporting persistent profiles
Dockerfile.edge pinned Chromium build
BrowserDriverCapabilities gating and the SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md Phase 5 'owned browser fleet' plan
verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane must own the browser fleet. Model Plane sandbox-manager is a Space-capability-bound lease registry for code sandboxes (its backend id is pinned by a Control capability decision, server.go:84-107, main.go:60); making Quarry depend on it inverts 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' and drags Space authority into scraping, so that option in the item should be dropped. PinnedEgressProxyEndpoint is deliberately loopback-only (lib.rs:331-360), so a per-container Chromium needs its own proxy sidecar in the same network namespace or an explicit, reviewed relaxation of that type. ZDR: per-session workers must be ephemeral and profile export must stay blocked under ZDR (the gateway already rejects ZDR plus persistent profile, browser.rs:471-474). Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so any lease must be keyed by the verified org_id, not by caller input.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the item. Step 1 (S to M, no fleet): stop the cross-session blast radius by applying viewport per page or context through CDP emulation instead of relaunching the shared browser (chromiumoxide.rs:194-223), and change the compose default of QUARRY_BROWSER_NO_SANDBOX from 1 to 0 (docker-compose.yml:99 disables the Chromium sandbox when the variable is unset, contradicting its own comment at line 97 and .env.example:20); production manifests were not checked. Step 2 (L): add a CDP-connect mode to ChromiumoxideDriver (Browser::connect to a worker WebSocket) and a per-org pool of Chromium worker containers, each with its own pinned-proxy sidecar, all owned by the Ingestion Plane. Step 3 (XL, optional): microVM per session. Do not present the Kernel or Browserless drivers as a shortcut, they are one-shot REST shims. Also note that scrape-path sessions are keyed by host only (browser_driver.rs:139-148), so concurrent same-host browser scrapes from different orgs may share one session_key (INF, not tested).
verevon.effortNote: Original L covered only the pool. Real per-org or per-session isolation needs the CDP-connect driver plus a worker fleet and proxy placement. The cheap hardening in Step 1 is S to M and should be split off as its own quick win.
verevon.verdictReason: The isolation gap is real and absent, but the item omits two existing defects that matter more in the short term (viewport-triggered relaunch of the shared Chromium; sandbox disabled by the compose default), offers a wrong-plane option (sandbox-manager) and ignores the loopback-proxy invariant. Reword as a staged item with a quick-win first step.

items.title: Agent routines: scheduled, heartbeat and event-triggered agent runs with per-fire browser grants
items.summary: Let the agent create persistent routines through one confirmed tool: cron or one-shot runs in a new session, heartbeats that wake the same conversation later, and event routines fired by webhook, email or notification events. Build on the Model Plane's existing cron_schedules and fire-time Control authorization, and issue a fresh BrowserBroker grant scoped to the routine's allowed domains for each unattended fire.
items.whyItMatters: It turns the agent from reactive to proactive (watch a page, follow up tomorrow, react to a webhook), a visible AI-first differentiator. Event triggers can reuse integration-corev2 webhook intake and the Quarry run.completed event from R-t2-05-08.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (single routine_update tool over a routines table)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: routines(id, owner, kind cron|heartbeat, trigger schedule|event, schedule_kind once|recurring, rrule, tz, run_at, event_filter {source, from}, target_session_id, model, permission_mode, browser_binding, paused_by, pause_reason, expires_at, created_by_session). The scheduler fires schedule routines into a new session (cron) or appends a wake message to the target session (heartbeat); an inbox matcher fires event routines. One tool handles create, suggest, update, pause, resume, view and delete. Prompt rules: hide raw RRULE, update rather than duplicate, never pause silently. Plans cap active routines.

verevonToday.gap: The Model Plane has cron_schedules CRUD at /api/v1/cron, a sweeper that claims due slots with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, creates a task from a task_template, records the fire, and reauthorizes each slot with a Control decision (model.cron.create, model.cron.fire, model.schedule.run). Not verified: whether the agent can create schedules through a tool, whether heartbeat (wake the same session) or event triggers exist, how browser grants are issued for unattended fires, and whether ZDR routines avoid storing transcripts. The comparator also flagged this cluster as unknown.

items.approach: Model Plane owns routines because they start agent runs and carry model and permission settings; acquisition-only automation delegates to Quarry schedules (R-t2-05-02). Extend cron_schedules (or a sibling routines table) with kind, trigger, target_session_id, event_filter, budget and allowed domains. Each fire must pass the existing Control fire authorization and obtain a fresh BrowserBroker grant; ZDR routines persist no transcript. Expose a routine tool to the agent with explicit user confirmation on create and per-routine budgets. Event routines subscribe to integration-corev2 webhook intake and Quarry completion events.
dependencies: Model Plane cron sweeper and Control fire authorization (exist)
items.risks: Unattended agent runs widen the blast radius; require explicit user approval, per-routine budgets and domain scope, and never let a stored routine act as standing authority (the existing fire-time reauthorization pattern addresses this).

verevon.exactGap: Cron is shipped only as a user-authored, Space-bound, draft-only lane: capability-core cron_schedules (5-field cron only, no one-shot or RRULE) is swept with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, reauthorized per fire by Control (model.cron.fire, model.schedule.run), and each fire runs one inference-only scheduled step in execution-core (execute_scheduled_step_runtime, no tool loop) on a persistent lane. Missing: any agent-callable schedule or routine tool (execution-core offers none), heartbeat runs that wake an existing session, general event triggers (only the flagged-off self-forward mail-task webhook and a process_output Space-watch adapter exist), per-fire browser grants, and a non-persistent ZDR lane. Per-fire browser grants are blocked twice: the scheduled lane uses a service credential and refuses human-delegated bearers while browser tools require a delegated browser credential, and BrowserBroker has no issuance path; the ScheduleDialog doc comment also records an owner ruling that scheduled runs are draft-only through Wave 2 because a scheduled run hard-fails when a step needs approval (comment only, workflow code not opened).

verevon.constraints: Space authority: a stored schedule is never authority, every create needs a Control decision bound to the user and every fire is reauthorized, so an agent-created routine must go through the same user-bound create decision, never a service insert. The scheduled lane must not borrow a human's delegated bearer, which conflicts with the item's 'fresh BrowserBroker grant per fire' because browser tools need a delegated browser credential and the broker has no issuance path. Owner ruling: unattended runs are draft-only through Wave 2 and effectful or browser tool use in scheduled runs is Wave-3 scope, needing a pause/resume path that does not exist. ZDR: the scheduled lane is hard-wired persistent, so 'ZDR routines persist no transcript' cannot hold; refuse routine creation for ZDR users or build a non-persistent lane. Model proposes, Quarry executes: browser steps in a routine still need the Quarry grant and per-action approvals, which cannot be answered unattended.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-scope in stages. (1) An agent-proposed routine as a confirmed, user-bound schedule create (the tool returns a proposal the user approves, then the existing gateway create_cron path runs), draft-only and tool-free. (2) Event triggers by adding Watch adapters or generalizing mail-task, not by building a new matcher. (3) Tool-using or browser routines only after the Wave-3 approval pause/resume design, a scoped service-owned browser credential and BrowserBroker issuance exist. Keep acquisition-only automation (watch a page) on Quarry schedules (ingestions.create_schedule) rather than agent routines.
verevon.effortNote: L sized this as an extension of cron_schedules, but per-fire browser grants and tool-using routines need a scheduled tool loop, approval pause/resume, a scoped service browser credential and a ZDR lane. The draft-only agent-proposed routine alone is M.
verevon.verdictReason: The cron foundation exists, but the distinctive parts (heartbeat, event routines, per-fire browser grants) are blocked by the Wave-3 draft-only ruling and unbuilt prerequisites (grant issuance, scheduled tool loop, ZDR lane). Keep as a later-wave item with the narrowed first slice.

items.title: Budgeted web research job contract with run-context cost attribution
items.summary: Package the existing search, scrape and browser-agent steps as one research run in the Model Plane: input {prompt, urls?, output schema?, max cost/credits, effort}, output {status, data, partial, partialSchemaValid, stopReason such as credit_limit_reached, creditsUsed}, with one active run per thread (409 thread_busy plus the running run id). Quarry accepts a signed run-context header {requestId, parentRunId} from the Model Plane so its cost events attach to the parent run and are not billed twice.
items.whyItMatters: A predictable, budgeted research call gives other features, and any future external API user, one contract with partial results and a clear stop reason instead of stitching step-level agent routes together. Accurate per-run cost in the Model Plane cost service depends on Quarry knowing the parent run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-020 agent job and fc-022 threads; fc-021 trusted internal calls with requestId and shouldBill)
others: Apify (Actor runs with max-charge limits, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: research-agent job API: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl), unique; internal service call attribution: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: POST /agent {prompt, urls?, schema?, maxCredits, effort, strictConstrainToURLs, webhook} returns an id; GET returns {status, data, partial, partialSchemaValid, stopReason, creditsUsed, pendingApproval}; a thread rejects a new turn with 409 while a run is active. Internal agent services call the public endpoints with a shared-secret block {requestId, shouldBill} so tool calls are attributed to the parent run; Verevon should use its stronger scoped service tokens plus a signed header rather than one shared secret.

items.approach: Model Plane: add a research-run type over the existing sessions/runs with schema validation (using the json format from R-t2-01-04), a budget and partial-result semantics; it calls Quarry search/scrape/agent steps under service tokens. Ingestion Plane: accept a signed run-context header and tag cost events with run id; widen service scopes deliberately (map yes; crawl starts stay approval-gated so 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' holds). Cost service integration records per-run cost.

items.risks: Cost runaway (enforce the budget server-side); schema-valid but wrong outputs; ZDR must hold across every step.

verevon.exactGap: A research pipeline already exists but as a chat feature: model-gateway deep_research.rs (plan, concurrent search, read, synthesize, cited document artifact) runs under a session run when a request sets deepResearch, with spend caps (sub-queries, pages read, corpus chars, wall clock), a coverage report with a halt_code stop reason and a cancelled/partial outcome, yet it is in-process, dies with the stream, is not an addressable job, takes no caller budget or output schema, and has no thread-busy guard (no thread_busy or 409 concept found in Model Plane). Quarry exposes only step-level routes (/v1/search, /v1/extract, /v1/agent/runs, job listing) and meters billing UsageEvents keyed by its own request id with free-form metadata, while execution-core's web tools send only a bearer and x-quarry-org, so no parent run id reaches Quarry and Quarry usage flows to billing-core rather than the Model Plane cost-core (cost-core ingestion of Quarry cost was not traced). A USD ceiling exists only for browser runs (Quarry AgentConstraints.max_cost_usd, gateway max_cost_usd); there is no credits budget for search or scrape.

verevon.constraints: Model Plane owns the run and its cost; Quarry only executes and meters and must treat a run-context header as advisory attribution, never authority (signed, org-checked). ZDR must hold across every step: deep research is already refused for waived runs and the chat pipeline persists nothing precisely because it dies with the stream, so a durable job record must not retain content for ZDR callers. Budgets must be enforced server-side in the Model Plane, since Quarry usage reaches billing-core asynchronously. Crawl starts remain approval-gated (Model proposes, Quarry executes).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not build a new research-run type from raw steps: promote the existing deep_research pipeline to an addressable run (GET status, partial results, stopReason mapped from halt_code, one active run per thread returning 409 and the running run id), map the caller budget onto the existing caps plus a credit or USD ceiling, and add output-schema validation only after the JSON-format item lands. Add the signed run-context header as a separate small cross-plane change (web_tools.rs and the model-gateway Quarry client send requestId and parentRunId; Quarry writes them into UsageEvent.metadata). Defer the external-API-user justification until such a consumer exists.
verevon.effortNote: Reworded scope (addressable wrapper over the existing pipeline, budget mapping, thread-busy guard, run-context attribution) is M because the pipeline and its session run already exist. Output-schema validation and fully durable partial state would return it to L.
verevon.verdictReason: The item proposes packaging steps that deep_research already packages for chat. The real gaps are addressability, a caller budget, thread-busy semantics and run-context attribution to Quarry; reword to those.

items.title: Code-mode browser control: sandboxed script runtime over typed Quarry bindings, with approval-input hardening
items.summary: Offer the model one persistent REPL tool per session that runs model-written JS in a QuickJS/V8 isolate inside execution-core with only typed Quarry bindings (observe, act, locator, extract), no network, fs or raw CDP, memory/stack limits and a per-call deadline. Every binding call goes to quarry-edge with the run's grant so each action is still grant-checked, approved and receipted per Quarry step. Ship with opaque handles, no imports and freeze-and-copy of every argument that reaches an approval or Quarry call.
items.whyItMatters: Fewer model round-trips and tokens for multi-step tasks (fill a form, paginate, extract a table), and programmatic post-processing of page data before it reaches the model. It preserves 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' because each host call is a Quarry step.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (one persistent QuickJS scope per session with a small surface: page, tabs, snapshot, annotatedScreenshot, fetch, plus runtime lints; AA083 non-marshalable host handles)
others: Codex (CA077/CA054 model-visible vs programmatic observation split; approval inputs copied into a frozen object to close a TOCTOU gap)
Firecrawl (interact tool)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 3 sources; table-stakes (hardening: 2 of 3)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Embed a WASM JS engine with memory/stack limits and an interrupt deadline; keep one top-level scope per session; inject host functions that marshal to typed commands; return only values the script emits to the model. Before any approval, verify arguments are plain own data properties, deep-copy, freeze and execute exactly the frozen copy; reject module import/require.

verevonToday.gap: Verevon exposes browser.observe / browser.act as one typed action per model call; there is no batching and no programmatic post-processing. Hardening is only relevant once code-mode exists; typed JSON actions are already plain data.

items.approach: Model Plane sandboxes/execution-core: isolate runtime with typed bindings that are thin clients for quarry-edge /step using the run's grant; approvals stay per Quarry step, not per script. Build only after the single-step loop (R-t2-09-02) is live and measured, so token and latency data justifies it.
items.risks: Larger attack surface from model-written code; shipping without the hardening would create approval bypasses; one script can contain many actions, so per-script approval is unsafe.

verevon.exactGap: No script runtime exists: execution-core offers browser.observe and browser.act as single typed JSON actions (closed oneOf schema, additionalProperties false, snapshot refs only, no JavaScript, CSS selector or URL) and a bwrap-sandboxed code_interpreter that runs only python or sh with no network and no tool bridge. Code-mode is planned generically in Model Plane docs only (MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md sections 23.4-23.5 and verevon_CHAT_PARITY_BACKLOG.md #11, an in-sandbox RPC client), with no browser-specific design and no code, so the item's alreadyPlanned=false is inaccurate. The approval-input hardening half has no present gap: typed browser.act input is plain data and the approval stores the exact tool_input in a frozen, encrypted continuation descriptor.

the approval record, continuation descriptor and decision pipeline (one approval per Quarry step)

model-gateway tool-result handles / result_query to keep large page data out of model context
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: every binding call stays a separate Quarry step with the run's grant and its own approval; one approval must never cover a whole script. Approvals are durable pauses with an exact frozen descriptor and browser_agent cannot be cold-resumed, so a script waiting on approval must keep its sandbox alive and end as unknown-outcome when the wait budget is exceeded. ZDR: script inputs and outputs must not be persisted and must be scrubbed like code_interpreter output. Code-mode in general is already planned in Model Plane docs, so this must be a slice of that effort, not a parallel runtime. Preconditions are unbuilt: browser grants have no issuance path and the single-step planner loop has not been measured.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Fold into the planned generic code-mode (docs 23.4/23.5, backlog #11) as one browser binding set. Run the engine as a bwrap'd child of execution-core with network disabled, speaking a line-delimited RPC to the parent, which proxies each binding to browser.observe/browser.act with approvals, instead of embedding QuickJS or V8 in the execution-core process. Python over RPC (backlog #11) is the lower-risk first engine because code_interpreter already ships it; choose JavaScript only for a measured reason. Drop freeze-and-copy hardening from scope until a script can reach an approval, since the typed schema and descriptor already provide it.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. The sandbox substrate exists, but the item depends on grant issuance and a measured single-step loop; it becomes XL if a new JavaScript engine is embedded in-process.
verevon.verdictReason: Code-mode is already planned generically, the browser variant has unbuilt preconditions (grants, planner loop, measurements) and unproven savings, and the proposed in-process isolate conflicts with the existing sandboxed-child pattern. Keep as a later slice of the generic code-mode work.

items.title: External contract: full OpenAPI, then an audience-bound MCP server for Quarry and read-only connectors, SDK call-and-wait and a first no-code connector
items.summary: Generate the Quarry OpenAPI spec from the Rust request/response types with a CI route-coverage check (the checked-in spec lists about 46 paths against roughly 75 edge routes). Then expose a Verevon-hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth) whose tools map onto the same governed action contracts, so every call goes through the existing authority, approval, ZDR and audit path. Last, add waiters and origin pinning to the Rust client used by the gateway and Model Plane, delete or wire the dead SPA quarry-client, and ship installable agent skills or a CLI only if an external API is offered. || Build an MCP server front (Frontend Plane gateway domain or a dedicated edge service, not inside Quarry) that publishes search, scrape, map, extract, crawl-status and read-only provider actions to customers' own agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor). Authenticate with OAuth from Control Plane auth-core (resource indicators, audience-bound tokens, protected-resource metadata, introspection cached by token hash), translate calls to Quarry edge and IC with a short-lived purpose-tagged service token, and write one metadata-only audit row per call. Writes stay behind an in-product approval. As a standalone first step, classify MCP tool data categories at registration instead of 'unclassified'. || Add hand-written ergonomics on top of the OpenAPI-generated TypeScript and Python Quarry SDKs: a call-and-wait helper (submit crawl/batch/agent run, poll or subscribe, return results) and typed result iterators. Once outbound webhooks are tenant-safe, publish an n8n community node (self-hostable, open source) wrapping start-run, wait and fetch-results; Zapier and Make only if demand appears.
items.whyItMatters: Three of four reference sources expose MCP, and it is the AI-first distribution channel for external agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to use Verevon's web stack without leaking credentials. A complete OpenAPI prevents contract drift that already exists and feeds Model Plane tool schemas; none of this is needed for the in-product experience, which is why it sits after the core API work. || Gives Verevon the developer-ecosystem parity both Firecrawl and Apify have, and lets customers use Verevon's governed web layer and connectors from their own agents with ZDR and audit intact. The audit companion also improves admin visibility of agent MCP usage today. || Distribution channel for the public Quarry API and cheap parity with Apify's run-and-chain pattern. It matters less for an AI-first product whose own agents orchestrate work, so it is a go-to-market item, not a core capability.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: MCP exposure: 3 of 4 sources (Apify, Aside, Firecrawl), table-stakes; OpenAPI: 2 of 4, common; SDKs: 2 of 4, common; CLI and skills: 3 of 4 but DOC/INF-only evidence || 2 of 4 sources (both web platforms) for MCP exposure; per-call audit log in 1 of 4; common || 1 of 4 sources (Apify only; DOC records only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: OpenAPI generated from request/response types in CI and failing on route drift, driving SDKs and tool schemas. MCP: Streamable-HTTP endpoint behind OAuth, tool catalog generated from the action contracts, tool groups loaded on demand (?tools=), every call mapped to the same governed path as in-product calls. SDK: start* plus waitFor* with abort-triggered best-effort cancel, fetchAllPages with caps, and rewriting any server-provided next URL onto the configured origin before sending credentials. || Merged items add: The MCP service advertises protected-resource metadata in WWW-Authenticate, introspects the OAuth token (active, exp, aud == the MCP resource, credential_purpose) with a cache keyed by token hash that is isolated from outages. To call the core API it mints a short-lived signed credential {v, aud core, purpose, subject, iat, exp} (exp <= 120 s, iat skew <= 30 s) verified with a constant-time HMAC; the user token is never forwarded. Each call POSTs one row (tool, client, auth type, status, error class, request id) to an internal ingest; the team view omits objective/job id fields and ZDR teams get 202 with nothing stored. || Published connector apps per platform wrap the REST API (start run, poll/wait, fetch dataset items); the SDK call() helper starts a run, waits for completion and returns, enabling chained runs.

items.approach: Order matters: (1) generate full OpenAPI from the same types as F-t2-005 (46 of about 75 routes documented today, per baseline); (2) SDK call-and-wait helper on the public job lifecycle (F-t2-017); (3) an MCP front with audience-bound OAuth from Control Plane auth-core, short-lived purpose-tagged delegation to Quarry and integration-corev2, a privacy-minimised tool-call log (nothing under ZDR), and writes that still require in-product approval; (4) n8n node, CLI and skills. Step 3 reverses the documented OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG deferral and needs an owner decision. || Source detail: [R-t2-01-11] Ingestion Plane: derive OpenAPI from the Rust types (utoipa or schemars) with a CI route-coverage check, and feed JSON Schemas to the Model Plane. Model Plane tool catalog plus Frontend gateway (OAuth, endpoint): host the MCP server over the existing action contracts, with Quarry staying behind the gateway. Control Plane: customer auth and API keys as the prerequisite. Add waiters and origin pinning to the Rust client; delete or wire the SPA client. Skills wrapping MCP tools come after MCP; a CLI only if an external API is offered. || [R-t2-10-04] Frontend Plane gateway (Rust) or a new small edge service owns the MCP front; Control Plane auth-core is the authorization server (reuse the existing oidcProvider, enable DCR for MCP clients, add resource-indicator audience binding and an introspection endpoint; verify what the plugin already supports). Calls go to Quarry edge and IC with a short-lived, purpose-tagged service token from the cross-plane manifest, scoped to org and user. Tool set mirrors execution-core read tools (search, scrape, map, extract, crawl status, list_provider_actions, read actions); write actions create a pending approval in the product and return its id, never executing without in-product approval; browser control is explicitly out of scope until grants and approvals work for external callers. Audit: emit one tool.call event per invocation (tool, client id, auth type, status, error class, request id, no arguments or objective) through the existing outbox to Audit Core with a team query view; ZDR records metadata only. Phase 0 (S): classify MCP tool data categories at capability-core registration. Later: a CLI, skills and framework wrappers once request shapes stabilise. || [R-t2-10-06] Ingestion Plane, Quarry-v2 sdks/. Add a thin non-generated layer (kept outside the regenerated folders so sdks/generate.sh does not overwrite it) with startAndWait(kind, request, {timeout, onEvent}) using job status/events routes. Later, an n8n node package in a new repo folder calling the edge API with an API key; no plane changes.

items.title: Cached declarative extraction profiles generated by the Model, with bounded browser-agent escalation
items.summary: Phase A (recommended): the Model Plane generates a declarative ExtractionProfile (selectors plus transforms, never arbitrary code) once per (org, url template, schema, prompt); Quarry validates and caches it per org (not under ZDR) and executes it deterministically on later scrapes, requesting regeneration when validation fails. Phase B (nice to have): during JSON extraction the model can flag that data is behind clicks or pagination and give a goal; Quarry then starts a bounded agent run on the source host, re-extracts the visited pages and merges.
items.whyItMatters: Phase A cuts per-page model cost for monitors and recurring crawls of the same template, and matches the authority rule: the Model proposes a profile and Quarry executes or rejects it. Phase B covers data hidden behind interaction using both halves Verevon already has (extract and Quarry agent runs).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-093 deterministicJson codegen cache; engine-and-infra-092 SmartScrape escalation; api-surface-043)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Cache key = hash(cacheVersion, codegen model, url, schema, prompt). Miss: build anchor-context HTML around elements matching schema field hints, a codegen model returns an extractor, run it sandboxed, validate against the schema, store; hit: run the cached extractor and regenerate when validation or selectors fail (10 credits to generate, 3 to reuse). Escalation: wrap the schema as {extractedData, shouldUseSmartscrape, smartscrape_reasoning, smartscrape_prompt}; if flagged start a browser-agent session with the prompt, collect visited pages, re-run extraction and merge.

verevonToday.gap: No extractor codegen, validation loop or profile cache, and no escalation from extract to a browser agent. A declarative ExtractionProfile format (JSON-LD, DOM, AX sources) already exists for agent observations and is the right generation target. The cluster said agent cost budgets are not enforced: agent_loop.rs does charge a flat per-action cost against max_cost_usd, but observation.rs:3164 builds constraints with max_cost_usd None, so whether the Verevon path (Model Plane to Quarry) carries a limit is unverified.

items.approach: Model Plane: add a profile-generation prompt that outputs an ExtractionProfile validated against the quarry-core schema. Ingestion Plane: validate and execute the profile in quarry-runtime, store it per org keyed by (template URL pattern, schema hash, prompt hash) outside ZDR, and request regeneration on schema-validation failure or selector miss; complete the DOM source of ExtractionProfile if it is partial. For Phase B the Model Plane returns an escalation flag and goal; Quarry starts a bounded agent run (allowed_domains = source host, step and cost budget enforced end to end) and re-extracts.
dependencies: F-t2-019 (LLM json format and model grant)
end-to-end agent budget enforcement for Phase B
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (profile execution, cache) with Model Plane (profile generation, escalation decision)
items.risks: Silently wrong data when a template changes but output still validates; per-org cache isolation and ZDR; runaway cost on Phase B until budgets are confirmed enforced.

verevon.exactGap: No model-driven profile generation, validation loop, per-org profile cache or extract-to-agent escalation exists. The existing ExtractionProfile (contracts.rs:259-300) is executed only for agent step observations when the caller supplies it (agent_routes.rs:818-824, observation.rs:646-650), and its executor is a string scanner: DOM and Accessibility fields support only '#id', '[data-testid=...]' or the first bare tag name, values are single strings, NetworkJson and Visual sources are skipped, and there are no list, attribute or transform operations (observation.rs:2261-2355). The item's budget doubt is partly resolved: observation.rs:3164 is test code, but the HTTP step route enforces only max_steps (agent_routes.rs:446-450) and the run TTL; max_cost_usd is accepted at run start and per-step costs are written to receipts, yet no cumulative cost check runs because AgentLoop::over_budget (agent_loop.rs:154-162) is only mentioned in edge comments, never called.
reuse: ExtractionProfile, ExtractionResult and the extract_profile entry point as the schema and execution seam
scraper 0.25 and lol_html 3, already dependencies of quarry-transform, as the real selector engine
Step receipts with cost_usd and enforce_step_budget as the place to add cumulative cost enforcement
AgentConstraints.allowed_domains and check_domain for the bounded Phase B run
Per-org artifact and baseline stores for the profile cache; PrivacyPolicy/ZDR switches
extract_routes.rs json_for_org path (behind AI formats) once the Model Plane grant exists
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: a model-authored profile is declarative data that Quarry validates, caches per org and runs deterministically, which fits, but the profile must never contain code and the cache must be per org and absent under ZDR. Quarry calling inference to generate it is currently refused: every Quarry Model Plane feature is OFF by default and model-invoke is granted:false (model_plane_gate.rs:1-14, cross-plane-token-requests.json:40-46), and DEF-QB-T17-PART2 (org-bound, metered path) has no owner. Phase B needs a hard budget end to end, and the gateway starts runs with max_steps 12 and max_runtime_s 120 but no max_cost_usd (browser.rs:483-490).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder and re-source. (1) Make the executor a usable generation target first: back DOM fields with scraper selectors, add multi-valued items, attribute reads and a small closed set of transforms, and version the schema (M to L); the current format cannot express list pages. (2) Wire profile execution into scrape, schedule and monitor paths (a new format or ScrapeOptions field), because today only agent steps run it. (3) Generate the profile on the Model Plane side as a proposed argument when a monitor or source is created, send it to Quarry for validation and storage keyed by (org, URL template, schema hash), and have Quarry return a typed regenerate signal on selector miss or schema-validation failure; this avoids Quarry calling inference while the grant is refused. (4) Phase B only after cumulative max_cost_usd enforcement is added to the HTTP step route (it is absent today).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged at XL, but it now also includes the executor rewrite and missing budget enforcement; do not schedule Phase B before those land.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent is confirmed, but the item is not buildable as described: the profile executor is far too weak to be the generation target, the Quarry to Model Plane inference grant is refused, and Phase B has no cost enforcement on the production step route. Keep Phase A as a later, re-sourced item and mark Phase B blocked.

items.title: Policy-gated browsing preset limited to consent-banner handling and ad/tracker filtering (fingerprint masking deferred to an ADR)
items.summary: Re-scoped by T2. Keep the benign parts of R-t2-03-11: wire the existing consent-banner script and optional ad/tracker filtering behind an org policy flag, and make locale/timezone/TLS identity consistent with the request context of F-t2-058. Do not wire stealth.rs or fingerprint masking until an ADR on anti-bot posture decides it; F-t2-027 currently recommends deleting the dead stealth code.
items.whyItMatters: The consolidators disagree: R-t2-04-03 removes stealth code and reports blocks honestly, R-t2-03-11 wires it under policy. Verevon's contract already forbids challenge bypass (ChallengeSignal.requires_escalation defaults to true, SRC), and the honest posture (Codex, SRC) fits Verevon best. Consent handling and ad filtering still save time and cost.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify fingerprint-suite and Camoufox (apify-platform-056 and -057, DOC); Firecrawl behaviorOverrides (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-013, SRC)
others: Firecrawl tlsclient tier with an explicit demotion rule (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-007, SRC) and Apify got-scraping header generation (apify-platform-062, DOC)
Firecrawl blockAds via uBlock Origin Lite on hosted sessions (firecrawl-api-surface-059, SRC)
Codex deliberately ships no stealth because it drives real user browsers (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-011, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Stealth and TLS identity: 2 of 4 sources (apify, firecrawl), common. Ad blocking: 1 of 4, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per session sample a fingerprint {UA, sec-ch-ua, platform, screen, deviceMemory, WebGL vendor/renderer, fonts, locale, timezone} consistent with the egress country; apply it with Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (with userAgentMetadata), setLocaleOverride, setTimezoneOverride, setDeviceMetricsOverride and Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument; persist it with the profile so identity never changes mid-profile; derive HTTP headers from the same profile; planner rule: after a browser attempt fails never demote to a plain client unless explicitly allowed. Ad blocking via an MV3 blocker extension or CDP Fetch.enable with a filter-list matcher.

verevonToday.gap: Stealth and consent scripts are never injected; no fingerprint generator or persisted fingerprint; the planner only picks the Chrome TLS profile; the TLS tier does not follow redirects; the rotator policy is unwired; no ad or tracker blocking.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane. Phase A (S, hygiene): per-hop-validated redirect following in the TLS driver, planner use of Firefox/Safari profiles, wire FingerprintRotator on block, adopt the no-browser-to-plain-demotion rule. Phase B (M): FingerprintProfile persisted with the browser profile (SessionSnapshot already has UA/locale/timezone fields), applied on context creation; inject default_preamble only under the 'stealth' RunPolicy preset and log it in receipts; derive HTTP headers from the same profile and session locale (depends on R-t2-03-05 emulation). Phase C (S, optional): adblock-rust matcher in the existing CDP Fetch guard plus a default-on consent-dismiss option and a 'block ads' toggle in BrowserChrome. Never apply stealth to customer-owned authenticated SaaS sessions, and do not add CAPTCHA solving as a default (non-goal in the Sovereign Scraping proposal).
dependencies: F-t2-020 (profile persistence to hold the fingerprint)
items.risks: Terms-of-service and legal exposure on protected sites; arms-race maintenance and fingerprint drift as browsers update; an inconsistent fingerprint is worse than none; filter-list licensing (EasyList is copyleft) and breakage on sites that need ad scripts.

verevon.constraints: Quarry executes deterministically and records what it did: any Quarry-initiated click such as banner dismissal is not a Model-proposed action and must be logged in receipts and kept off authenticated customer SaaS sessions. Quarry's challenge classifier marks every detected challenge requires_escalation: true (observation.rs:213) rather than bypassing it, which fits F-t2-027's removal of the dead stealth code. ZDR is unaffected. Ad and tracker filtering must live in the existing fail-closed Fetch guard so it cannot weaken the egress policy.
verevon.approachAdjustment: The item contradicts itself: the title defers fingerprint masking to an ADR, but Phase B injects default_preamble (which bundles STEALTH_SCRIPT with the consent script) and builds a persisted FingerprintProfile. Narrow it to: inject CONSENT_DISMISS_SCRIPT alone behind an org policy flag; add an ad and tracker matcher in install_network_guard with a distinct receipt decision; per-hop validated redirect following in the TLS driver; locale and timezone from the session context (F-t2-058). Also change the consent script's behaviour: it deliberately clicks the affirmative accept button (stealth.rs:290-291) and so grants tracking consent on the user's behalf, which is the wrong default for a Norwegian and EU product; prefer reject-all or necessary-only controls, or hide the overlay, and record the choice. Move FingerprintProfile persistence and FingerprintRotator wiring under the anti-bot ADR.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in size after narrowing: consent injection and TLS redirect hygiene are S each, the ad and tracker matcher with filter-list licensing is M; the dropped fingerprint profile work would have been the larger part.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed stub with no production path, but the proposed wiring (default_preamble, FingerprintProfile) exceeds the item's own stated scope and the existing consent script accepts cookies instead of rejecting them; reword to the consent, filter and redirect-hygiene scope.

items.title: One honest product identity: unified user-agent and optional signed agent traffic (Web Bot Auth style)
items.summary: Step 1 (S): replace the four inconsistent Quarry user-agent strings with one product UA, publish a matching bot-information page, and use the same token for robots matching. Step 2 (M): add optional Web Bot Auth style request signing (Ed25519 key per deployment, Signature-Agent header) for agent-originated traffic on the static, TLS and browser-egress paths, with the key held in Control Plane. Human-driven browsing stays unsigned unless policy says otherwise.
items.whyItMatters: Sites that allow verified agents will let governed Verevon traffic through instead of blocking it, which is the compliant alternative to stealth and fits the governance story. The inconsistent UAs (one still pointing at an older domain) also undermine robots matching and site-owner trust.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (SRC, medium confidence)
others: Industry analogue: Web Bot Auth, HTTP Message Signatures with a published key directory (INF, not a studied source)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Codex); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A feature gate requires an identifying agent header on every agent-originated request from the extension backend, and clients without support get an 'update required' refusal. Web Bot Auth extends this by signing requests so sites and WAFs can verify the agent against a key directory.

verevonToday.gap: HTTP drivers do identify themselves, but inconsistently: 'Quarry/2.0 (+https://triodelab.com/quarry)' as the default (config.rs, answer.rs), 'QuarryBot/1.0 (+https://verevon.io/bot)' for HTTP/3 (main.rs:1263) and bare 'QuarryBot' for /v1/map (map_routes.rs:23). TLS-impersonating and browser drivers present a Chrome identity; the browser UA path was not verified. There is no signed identity, no published key directory and no agent marker on browser traffic.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: define one product UA constant and bot-info URL in quarry-core and use it everywhere, including robots matching (R-t2-04-01) and map. Add an optional signer (Ed25519, Signature-Agent, covered components per the draft standard) applied in the static and TLS drivers and in the browser egress proxy for agent-run traffic only; mark the policy flag in the run policy. Control Plane holds and rotates the key and serves the key directory. Decide explicitly how the browser driver's UA should look when it presents a Chrome identity, so the product's stance on honest identification is consistent.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane; Control Plane for key custody
items.risks: Self-identifying makes some sites block more, and the standard is still emerging. Signing must not apply to user-driven browsing by default.

verevon.exactGap: Quarry uses five unaligned UA strings and no signing: 'Quarry/2.0 (+https://triodelab.com/quarry)' as the edge default (config.rs:302), in the answer fetcher (answer.rs:716) and in the Ingestion compose env (docker-compose.yml:21), 'Quarry/2.0' in FetchPolicy (policy.rs:101, hashed at :349 but never applied to a request), 'QuarryBot/1.0 (+https://verevon.io/bot)' for HTTP/3 (main.rs:1263) and bare 'QuarryBot' for /v1/map robots matching (map_routes.rs:23). The chromiumoxide driver never sets a UA (it only reads navigator.userAgent), the TLS driver presents Chrome, Firefox or Safari identities, and driver_plan escalates static to tls to browser, so the presented identity changes along the fallback chain. A grep of apps finds no Signature-Agent, Signature-Input or Web Bot Auth code, no key directory and no bot-information page.

C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/map_routes.rs:23 (MAP_UA = "QuarryBot"), :250-258 (the only production robots allow-filter, keyed on MAP_UA)

C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/policy.rs:65-69 and :140 (RobotsMode defined, never read in the runtime); quarry-runtime/src/lib.rs:165 (RobotsCache only exported)

C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/driver_plan.rs:60-92 (static falls back to tls then browser; stealth_level 0, 1, 2)

C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:1797 (reads navigator.userAgent only) and :706-780 (install_network_guard: CDP Fetch listener whose ContinueRequestParams::new(request_id) sets no headers)
C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/browser_egress_proxy.rs:1-9 and :417-434 (proxy permits only HTTP absolute requests or opaque HTTPS CONNECT tunnels)

C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/CONTRACTS.md:310-318 (UA overrides only as explicit fields; must not downgrade the TLS profile) and :192-201 (QUARRY_PROFILE_KEY env or kms key-source convention)
reuse: quarry-core as the home for one product UA and bot-info URL constant
FetchPolicy.user_agent and headers (policy.rs:87-104) as the policy carrier, once a driver actually applies them
CDP Fetch interception in install_network_guard (chromiumoxide.rs:706-780) as the per-request seam for browser traffic
Static/TLS driver request builders (fetch.rs build_client, quarry-tls lib.rs header assembly) for signing non-browser traffic
QUARRY_PROFILE_KEY env or kms key-source convention as the precedent for holding a signing key
verevon.constraints: Honest identification cannot be uniform while the driver ladder static to tls to browser deliberately presents browser identities on the upper tiers (CONTRACTS.md:318, driver_plan.rs:66-90); the product needs an explicit stance per tier before signing is meaningful. UA unification has little enforcement effect until robots matching is wired into the live crawl path (F-t2-016): RobotsMode is never read and only /v1/map filters by robots. Key custody: a grep of Control Plane finds only HMAC service-auth files and no key-directory service (INF), Control Plane must stay out of the per-request hot path, and no plane may read another's database, so signing keys should live where the signer runs. Human takeover and agent actions share one Chromium instance and one CDP seam, so agent-only signing needs a per-run actor flag that Quarry does not carry at the Fetch seam today (initiator exists on control events only).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Three corrections. (1) The count is five sources plus a dead policy field: route one constant from quarry-core into StaticDriver, Http3Driver, SimpleHttpMarkdownFetcher, ReqwestRobotsFetcher, MAP_UA and the compose env, and either apply or delete FetchPolicy.user_agent. (2) Do not sign in browser_egress_proxy: it cannot add headers to HTTPS CONNECT tunnels; sign browser requests at the CDP Fetch seam (ContinueRequestParams with headers) and sign static and TLS requests in their drivers. (3) Hold the Ed25519 private key in Quarry's own secret or KMS source and publish the public key directory from a public edge or gateway route; Control Plane only audits rotation. Gate step 2 on an ADR that states the identity policy for the TLS and browser tiers.
verevon.effortNote: Step 1 stays S; step 2 stays M only if signing goes through the CDP Fetch seam and drivers (three transports plus a public key directory and rotation make it the upper end of M).
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is right and the direction is sound, but the item miscounts the UA sources, points signing at a component that cannot sign HTTPS requests, and places key custody in Control Plane without a seam for it. Reword with the corrected placement and the tier-identity ADR as a prerequisite.

items.title: Browsing data lifecycle: server-side history with agent/user source, bookmarks, clear-site-data, permission-deny events, support export
items.summary: Derive a per-user visit log from Quarry session timelines, tagged source agent|user, retention-limited and disabled under ZDR, and show it in a history page with an agent filter and a short list of user-scoped bookmarks (or reuse Knowledge saved sources). Add clear-site-data on a profile by type and origin (cookies, storage, cache) with counts first. Make permission handling deny-by-default in the driver with a 'permission requested' event shown as an info chip. Add an opt-in, redacted export of a session's timeline and receipts to support tickets, never under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: History and clear-data are table-stakes in both reference browsers and let users see and undo what the agent did in their profile; Verevon today only keeps a browser-local list of 10 entries. Category 1 deferred a consent-gated history query for agents to this item, so it also prepares a bounded read tool.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (history with Agent badge and source filter; clear-browsing-data dialog with counts; prompts keyed per page)
others: Aside (bookmarks, history panel, downloads bubble, privacy page)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: History and bookmarks: 2 of 3 sources, table-stakes. Clear data: 2 of 3, table-stakes. Permission prompts and diagnostics: 1 of 3 each, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: History store deduplicated by day with favicons; each visit tagged agent|user; a settings page with search, delete-selected and a source filter; agent-facing history reads are gated by their own approval mode. Clear dialog maps selected data types and range to storage clears and shows counts first. Permissions: default deny for request and check handlers with a prompt store keyed per page. Diagnostics: opt-in tab diagnostics attachment and a bounded ring buffer of recent session events.

verevon.constraints: ZDR: the owner timeline already returns 409 and receipts/timeline events are skipped for ZDR runs; a history view must keep that and never store URLs for ZDR runs (plan hard constraint, BROWSER_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md:25). Plane ownership: a visit log derived from receipts is Ingestion-owned (tenant and actor predicates), but bookmarks are user content, not browser evidence, and Quarry may persist durable knowledge only through Data Plane contracts, so they belong in a user-owned store outside Quarry (Data Plane saved sources, Application Plane or a gateway-side user store) with the Frontend only displaying them. Space authority: profile scope includes org_shared (any org member), so clear-data on an org-shared profile must be limited to its owner or an org admin and must not widen access. A stored-snapshot clear can race a live lease that re-saves the snapshot on release (the Kernel driver does, kernel.rs:194-200; not verified for the Chromium driver, INF), so it needs lease coordination.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into two deliverables. (A) clear-data plus permissions, S-M: implement clear-site-data as load, filter (cookie domain, storage and IndexedDB origin keys) and save on the stored SessionSnapshot through ProfileStore, with counts reused from restore_probe, and use CDP Storage.clearDataForOrigin only for a live session; add an explicit deny-all permission policy and a 'permission requested' timeline event in chromiumoxide. (B) visit history, M-L: add a tenant and actor scoped cross-run query on the receipt store (new Quarry route), project only host/path, time and initiator with a TTL, add initiator to receipts (or derive it from Control events) and keep it off under ZDR; put bookmarks in a user-owned store outside Quarry. Treat the redacted support export as a separate small gateway item that composes the existing timeline and receipts routes.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M: five sub-features across three planes; history needs a cross-run receipt query, an initiator field and retention, and bookmarks need a store that does not exist. Clear-data plus permission deny alone is S-M.
verevon.verdictReason: Status partial and the gap is real, but the item understates the existing seam (a durable actor-bound owner timeline with initiator and ZDR handling already exists) and misplaces two parts: clear-data should mutate the stored profile snapshot rather than rely only on CDP calls, and bookmarks should not live in Quarry. Reword and split before scheduling.

items.title: Quarry-backed page utilities: find, zoom, print-to-PDF, full-page and area screenshot, viewport emulation, colour scheme
items.summary: Expose what the Chromiumoxide driver already does (full-page screenshot and PDF) through the gateway and the shell, and add the missing pieces in Quarry: a find action that returns match rects to highlight in the frame, viewport_set and reset through device-metrics emulation, a colorScheme session option that follows the user's theme, and a zoom scale. Frontend adds a find bar, zoom control, device presets, area-select capture and copy-to-clipboard. Print and screenshot outputs are artifacts, withheld under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Find, zoom, print and capture are table-stakes for a browser panel, and viewport control is one of the plan's own never-closed capabilities. Most of the capture work is already in the driver, so the gap is exposure rather than engine work.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (find, per-tab zoom, device metrics override, emulated colour scheme); Aside for the screenshot overlay with area handles
others: Aside (viewport and full-page capture, copy to clipboard)
Codex screenshots attached to comments and cropped thumbnails
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Utilities: 2 of 3 sources, table-stakes. Screenshots: 2 of 3, table-stakes. Viewport emulation: 1 of 3 and colour scheme: 1 of 3, both unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: findInPage open, query, next, previous and close; zoom percent persisted per tab with a banner; Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride {width, height, deviceScaleFactor, mobile} with an explicit reset; Emulation.setEmulatedMedia for prefers-color-scheme re-synced on theme change; full-page capture through captureBeyondViewport or scroll-and-stitch with a drag-area overlay. For Verevon: Quarry CDP calls plus a thin UI.

verevon.constraints: The shared chromiumoxide driver keeps one Chromium process with a process-wide active viewport: acquiring a lease whose viewport differs closes and relaunches the browser and clears every page, egress policy and dialog (chromiumoxide.rs:194-215). The gateway sends 1280x800 while Model Plane's quarry_agent.rs sends none, so a UI device preset applied through the lease would tear down concurrent runs; runtime viewport, zoom and colour-scheme control must be page or context scoped CDP emulation, never lease-viewport based. ZDR for screenshot and PDF artifacts is already enforced in Quarry and the gateway, so only the new UI must keep honouring the withheld state. Model proposes, Quarry executes: any new action (find, viewport_set, colour scheme) added to AgentAction is also a model-proposable action and needs a risk class (read-only for find, low for emulation); UI-only affordances such as zoom and find need not enter the model allowlist.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword into two steps. Step 1 (S, gateway and frontend only): add pdf to sanitize_action, add application/pdf with attachment disposition and nosniff to safe_browser_artifact_content_type, add full_page and a PDF button to the shell, and do area capture and copy-to-clipboard client-side from the returned PNG. Step 2 (M, Quarry): add page-scoped Emulation (setDeviceMetricsOverride with reset, setEmulatedMedia for prefers-color-scheme, page scale for zoom so the JPEG live frame stays sharp) and a find action returning match rects; do not route device presets through the lease viewport.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall, but now two parts: Step 1 is S (exposure and one content-type fix); Step 2 is M because viewport emulation must avoid the process-wide relaunch behaviour.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is correct and the item rightly says capture is already in the driver, but it omits two real gateway blockers for PDF (allowlist and media-type coercion) and it misses that viewport changes through the lease relaunch the shared Chromium, which changes the approach for presets. ZDR withholding for these artifacts already exists, so that part should not be listed as new work.

items.title: Browser chrome polish in the SPA: tab menu, new-tab page, typed error cards, split view, keyboard commands, activity strip, reader view
items.summary: A bundle of Frontend-led refinements that need little or no new Quarry surface. Tab context menu with duplicate (new tab, same URL and profile), reopen-closed (a closed-tab stack in Quarry session state), reorder, copy URL and open in the system browser. A new tab renders a compact search-or-ask page built from DashboardSearchPanel and the composer. Quarry returns typed navigation errors (network error, egress-policy denial, domain-lock denial, anti-bot) and BrowserChrome shows a Norwegian-first error card with retry and the reason. Register browser commands in the app's shortcut registry (without stealing keys forwarded to the remote page during takeover). Optional later: split view of two Quarry tab streams, a low-rate multi-run activity strip, and a reader view from the Quarry scrape markdown (translation through Model Plane inference outside ZDR).
items.whyItMatters: Removes small daily frictions once the browser is usable (items 01 to 04) and makes denials and failures understandable instead of silent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (tab menu commands, error pages, top sites, central keymap, browser activity preview)
others: Aside (search-or-ask new tab page, split view, tab-capture live previews, reader mode)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Tab operations: 1 of 3 recorded (table-stakes by inference). New tab page and live previews: 2 of 3, common. Error pages, split view, keyboard commands, reader/translation: 1 of 3, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tab context-menu command ids (copyUrl, duplicate, newTabToTheRight, rename, reload, openInExternalBrowser) dispatch to a tab store and duplicate clones history; on load failure net error codes map to localized categories and a local error document is rendered with the original URL stored so reload retries it; accelerators are named commands in a central keymap. Aside paints the new-tab omnibox immediately and mounts the composer in ask mode. Preview: thumbnail of each active run's latest frame, click to open the full panel.

items.title: Render MCP App (ui://) resources in an opaque-origin sandbox, and retire the permissive web-view iframe
items.summary: Support interactive UI returned by MCP servers: Frontend Plane renders MCP App resources in an opaque-origin iframe served from a separate sandbox origin with a strict CSP and scheme allow-list, with a postMessage bridge that proxies tool calls through the gateway to Model Plane approvals. In the same change, delete or constrain the unused WebPageViewer iframe that combines allow-scripts with allow-same-origin.
items.whyItMatters: Lets integration results (forms, pickers, dashboards from MCP servers) appear inline and be operated safely, and removes a latent client-side security hazard. It is emerging and not a parity blocker.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (MCP App guest view on a dedicated sandbox origin, only about/blob/data/https/wss allowed, permission requests denied, agent limited to locator actions)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Codex only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Render MCP App resources in a guest view on a separate sandbox origin; a session request filter allows only safe schemes; permission requests are denied; attach requests are queued with expiry; the agent drives the view through accessibility locators, never raw script.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:495-518 (model-generated HTML in srcdoc iframe with sandbox="allow-scripts" and deliberately no allow-same-origin, referrerpolicy no-referrer)

verevonToday.gap: Chat artifacts are correctly sandboxed, but there is no MCP Apps rendering, no postMessage tool bridge and no agent operation of rendered widgets. WebPageViewer would load third-party pages directly in the user's browser with same-origin retained and no URL scheme check if it were ever wired in, which also bypasses Quarry's egress, ZDR and SSRF controls.

items.approach: Frontend Plane. Add an McpAppFrame component next to ChatArtifactPanel using the same sandbox="allow-scripts" opaque-origin pattern, served from a separate sandbox domain with CSP (no network except an allow-list), and a postMessage bridge that sends tool-call requests to the gateway, which routes them to Model Plane (approvals apply). Needs Model Plane MCP gateway support to pass ui:// resources through. Remove WebPageViewer or replace it with the Quarry-backed remote browser view.
dependencies: Model Plane MCP gateway/runtime support for UI resources in tool results
A separate sandbox origin/domain and CSP
items.risks: T2 note: the DashboardSearchResults.tsx:184 iframe combining allow-scripts and allow-same-origin is a possible security issue if its content can be same-origin; it was not verified. If verification confirms it, split that fix out and treat it as a priority quick win. || Sandbox escape if allow-scripts and allow-same-origin are ever combined on same-origin content; phishing UI inside widgets; widgets triggering tool calls that skip approvals.

verevon.exactGap: MCP App rendering is absent: no ui://, resources/read, resourceUri or postMessage tool bridge exists in model-gateway, execution-core, mcp-bridge, the gateway or the SPA, the MCP client implements tools/list and tools/call only, and tool_result_handles unwraps a single text block. Reusable and shipped: ArtifactHtmlPreview (srcdoc iframe with sandbox allow-scripts and no allow-same-origin, no-referrer, wrapped in a strict CSP with connect-src none, pinned by a test). WebPageViewer (DashboardSearchResults.tsx:147-192) is exported but has no importer and carries sandbox allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on a third-party src.

items.title: Share an agent run and its evidence with Space members through the existing resource-grant authority
items.summary: Let an owner share a finished browser or ingestion run (timeline, receipts, screenshots) read-only with named users or a Space, by adding a run resource kind to the user-core resource_grants facade that the ShareDialog already uses. The Ingestion owner plane checks the grant before serving artifacts and issues short-lived signed artifact URLs per viewer. No anonymous public links by default, and ZDR runs have nothing durable to share.
items.whyItMatters: Sharing a browsing run with its evidence is a natural collaborative feature for a workspace product, and it is what Aside's published sessions deliver. It must respect 'Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL'.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (published shared sessions with tool outputs and capped images)
others: Apify
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Aside publishes a snapshot of the transcript plus tool outputs and up to 20 images per tool result, with explicit size caps, into an immutable share record that resolves to a read-only view. Apify adds time-limited pre-signed URLs for single objects and scoped READ/WRITE grants on chosen storages via a resource picker.

verevonToday.gap: SRC and baseline: artifacts are served only after an owner-gated gateway check and the timeline and evidence replay viewer is read-only for the owner. The gateway's ShareDialog backend proxies user-core resource_grants for documents (view-only MVP), but there is no share-run, link or signed-URL mechanism. Whether resource_grants accepts non-document resource kinds was not verified.

items.approach: User-core (or Application Plane projection): add a run resource kind to resource_grants and a Space projection of the share. Ingestion Plane: before serving receipts and artifacts, check the grant through the owner-plane ACL API and return per-viewer, short-lived signed URLs. Frontend: reuse ShareDialog on the Browser and Ingestions run views. Redact or let the owner deselect screenshots before sharing.
dependencies: resource_grants support for run resources (to verify)
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (projection) with Ingestion Plane (ACL and artifact serving)
items.risks: Apify's link sharing is ACL-widening by design and must not be copied. Screenshots can contain secrets. Grants must be revoked when the owner leaves the org.

items.title: Control Plane governance extras: SIEM export, saved approval preferences and privacy-safe usage events
items.summary: After the unified decision audit exists, add a per-org audit-core exporter (batches with gzip, bounded queue that drops the oldest with a lag metric, retry ladder then a DLQ, encrypted credentials, destination host allowlist, test delivery). Store browser approval preferences in Control Plane user settings (approval_mode, per-origin rules, revision, revision-checked PATCH) so the Model Plane risk gate can record decided_by=saved_user_permission. Add typed, enum-only product usage events (takeover, approval requested and resolved, tool called with terminal status) forwarded server-side to the Control Plane usage stream.
items.whyItMatters: SIEM export is an enterprise procurement checkbox once audit is unified; saved approvals cut approval fatigue on repeat sites; usage events show which browser features users and agents actually use, to prioritise parity work. All are invisible to day-one users.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl for SIEM (per-org batches of 200 events or 1 s, bounded 100k queue dropping the oldest, retry ladder 5 s to 30 min then a DLQ kept 7 days, destination host allowlist) and Codex for preferences and usage events (revisioned server document mirrored locally; typed events without URLs)
others: Aside (usage telemetry with opt-out)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: SIEM 1 of 4 (unique); approval preferences 1 of 4 (unique); product usage analytics 2 of 4 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An audit-core consumer per org with {kind, endpoint allowlist, encrypted credentials}; user browser_prefs with If-Match revision read by the risk gate; an analytics event catalogue whose properties are enums and counts only, disabled for ZDR orgs and on user opt-out, with no third-party script in the page.

verevonToday.gap: SIEM export is absent (audit-core persists verevon.audit.v2.> and usage events with no export integration, and Quarry does not publish to audit-core subjects). Saved approval preferences and product usage events are unknown: a limited grep found no analytics client (posthog, statsig, mixpanel, amplitude, sentry) in the SPA source or gateway manifest, and no browser approval-preference setting was located. Not checked: Model Plane approve-for-session persistence.

items.approach: Control Plane: audit-core exporter, user settings schema for browser_prefs, usage event ingestion. Model Plane: risk gate reads preferences but never auto-approves ZDR-forbidden or sensitive one-shot actions; saved rules are origin-scoped and expiring. Frontend Plane: a small typed event module posting to a gateway endpoint, suppressed under ZDR.
items.risks: Exporting URLs for ZDR orgs and destination SSRF (allowlist hosts); saved permissions silently widening authority; third-party analytics conflicting with ZDR and sovereignty positioning.

verevon.exactGap: None of the three deliverables exists. audit-core is a durable consumer of verevon.audit.v2.> and verevon.usage.v2.> with append-only audit_events and usage_events tables and a pull API (GET /v1/audit, /v1/usage) but no push exporter, destination config or delivery queue, and Quarry publishes no audit events (only Model Plane session-core publishes tool_action). User settings are generic per-category rows with no revision field and no browser category, and the browser decided event leaves decided_by empty (browser_events.rs:148,574,612), so no saved-approval path exists. No analytics client appears in the SPA package.json or gateway Cargo.toml, and usage_events holds billable usage, not product events.

verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns audit, usage and user settings, so the exporter and preferences store live there; Model Plane may read preferences only through a Control authority call and must never auto-approve sensitive one-shot actions or anything ZDR forbids. Exported audit must carry no page content for ZDR orgs and the destination needs a host allowlist (SSRF) and encrypted credentials. (1) SIEM export stands alone as an audit-core consumer with per-org destination, allowlist, retry then DLQ and test delivery; an S interim is to let customers pull GET /v1/audit with a service token.
