(3) Product usage events should not add a SPA analytics client: emit enum-only counters server-side from the gateway or execution-core into the existing usage v2 subject, suppressed for ZDR orgs. Quarry must first publish decision audit (F-t2-036) before an export is meaningful for browser actions.

verevon.verdictReason: All three parts are absent and the item correctly sits late, but it bundles unrelated work, double-counts the approval-preference store that F-t2-032 needs, and proposes a SPA analytics path that conflicts with ZDR; rewrite as a SIEM-export item plus a merge note into F-t2-032 and a server-side-only usage-counter note.

items.title: Quarry failure-mode and provider hardening: fail-open policy review, opaque provider errors, Postgres maintenance (verify first)
items.summary: Write down and implement a per-dependency failure policy in Quarry RUNBOOKS: fail open with a short TTL for rate and plan limits during a Control Plane outage, always fail closed for ZDR posture, grants and billing. Add a typed ProviderError that never echoes upstream bodies for the Browserbase, Browserless and Kernel drivers, and proxy live-view capability URLs through the gateway with short-lived tokens. Add autovacuum settings for the hot queue and event-history tables and move to scheduled index maintenance only once volume justifies it.
items.whyItMatters: Keeps Quarry available during Control Plane incidents without weakening ZDR or authority, prevents leaking provider capability URLs (which allow session takeover) to users or logs, and keeps the Postgres SKIP LOCKED queue healthy as volume grows. Each is small; none is urgent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (cached entitlements with FAIL_OPEN_LIMITS and a 60 second TTL; hosted-browser errors mapped to fixed messages with the body cancelled; pg_cron REINDEX CONCURRENTLY in staggered slots with a watchdog)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl) for each; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per-org entitlement cache (10 minutes) with fail-open defaults for limits only; provider client maps non-2xx responses to typed errors without bodies and never forwards raw live-view URLs; scheduled maintenance jobs plus tuned autovacuum on queue and event tables.

verevonToday.gap: Quarry edge sets no CORS layer (good) and /version exposes the git SHA. Not verified: behaviour when the Control Plane or billing-core is unreachable, whether provider error bodies or live-view capability URLs reach clients unredacted, and whether the Postgres deploy config tunes autovacuum for the queue and event-history tables. Providers are mostly unwired today, so the provider hardening is low urgency.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane only: document the failure matrix in docs/RUNBOOKS.md and add tests for each dependency; add ProviderError in quarry-browser and route live-view through the existing live_view route with short-lived tokens; add autovacuum and maintenance settings to the quarry-control migrations or deploy config.
items.risks: Failing open on the wrong check widens access; less detailed provider errors (keep detail in sensitive logs only); reindex load in production.

verevon.exactGap: Confirmed missing: the Browserbase, Kernel and Browserless drivers put the raw upstream response body into QuarryError details or message (browserbase.rs:119-124, kernel.rs:325-334, browserless.rs:172-184), the agent driver_err and the gateway's forward_quarry_failure pass error bodies through, the ingestion-postgres compose command tunes memory only with no autovacuum or reindex settings, and RUNBOOKS.md has no dependency-failure matrix. Not true as framed: quarry-edge has no synchronous plan, rate-limit or entitlement lookup against Control Plane or billing-core (usage leaves asynchronously over NATS via NatsUsageMeter, noop without NATS), so there is no limit check to fail open; the real Control Plane outage dependency is auth-core JWKS, where get_jwks returns 500 once the 300 s cache expires with no stale-if-error. Provider exposure is small today: Browserless is constructed only in tests, Browserbase is registered only when keys are set and only in the scrape driver registry (agent runs use chromiumoxide), and neither the gateway nor the SPA consumes Quarry's live-view route.

Keep ProviderError redaction (S) for the Browserbase, Kernel and Browserless drivers, and also redact the chromiumoxide details.error strings if they reach users. Defer the live-view proxy until a provider live view is actually surfaced (no gateway or SPA consumer exists). Check the production compose and the real Postgres deployment before adding autovacuum settings (only docker-compose.yml was read for flags; the grep covered the production file but found nothing).

items.title: Contract and signal hygiene: deprecation registry, signed browser and sandbox images, web-result usefulness signal
items.summary: Three independent small tasks. (a) A typed deprecation registry and tower middleware in quarry-edge that sets Deprecation, Sunset, Link and Warning headers on retiring routes, plus a CI contract test that fails when the gateway or Model Plane call a deprecated route. (b) Sign the Quarry browser, mcp-bridge and sandbox images in CI (cosign) and verify them at deploy or admission. (c) A usefulness event per web tool result (used, ignored, failed) from the Model Plane, aggregated per domain or provider in Ingestion and fed into capability-core scoring, with no content stored under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Quarry's contracts evolve quickly while the gateway and Model Plane clients lag, browser and sandbox images handle live user sessions, and source ranking improves cheaply from a machine-readable usefulness signal. None of these is user-visible, but each is cheap insurance.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (deprecation protocol and result feedback), Codex (signed bundle receipts)
others: Codex in-app browser
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources each; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Firecrawl: a typed registry {id, route matcher, deprecated_at, sunset_at, successor, message} drives Deprecation (RFC 9745), Sunset, Link rel=successor-version and Warning 299 headers plus JSON warnings, attached before auth so rejected calls still see them, with per-version request adapters; POST /v2/feedback is keyed by job id inside a short window and requires specifics on negative ratings. Codex: CI signs a receipt (RSA PKCS1 SHA256, key id, per-plugin sha256, source sha, workflow ref) and the runtime verifies it before enabling a bundle.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: Quarry exposes /v1 only, the Firecrawl-compat adapter was deleted and no Deprecation or Sunset handling was found in Quarry crates (comparator grep). A grep of .github/workflows finds no cosign, sigstore, attest, slsa, trivy or provenance step, and the Model Plane decision ledger records no cosign, SLSA or SBOM in the plane. No feedback route exists in quarry-edge/src (comparator grep); capability-core has an operator_rating input to scoring but no per-result signal from agents. Image signing could live in a deploy pipeline outside this repo, which was not checked.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: deprecation registry plus middleware in quarry-edge and a contract test in quarry-v2-ci.yml. Support Plane or CI: cosign signing and verification for the images and the mcp-bridge bundle. Model Plane: emit the usefulness event keyed by the Quarry request id; Ingestion aggregates ids and domains only; capability-core scoring consumes it.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane, with Support Plane (signing) and Model Plane (usefulness events)
items.risks: Low. The usefulness signal must not log content under ZDR (ids and domains only). The signing task needs a registry and key-management decision before it is worth doing.

verevon.exactGap: None of the three tasks exists: quarry-edge serves /v1 routes only with no Deprecation, Sunset, Link or Warning handling (routes.rs:131-275; the only 'deprecated' in routes.rs is a Rust lint allow at :80), no workflow under .github/workflows references cosign, sigstore, SLSA, SBOM or provenance, and no web-result usefulness event or Quarry feedback route exists. Two premises also fail: only auth-service, org-service and user-service workflows build and push images (none for Quarry or Model Plane; the Model Plane compose header says to build only through a host build script, and both composes carry SOURCE_REVISION and BUILD_DATE build args), and capability-core scoring ranks capabilities from health columns rather than domains or search results, although its rollout_state 'deprecated' is an unrelated capability lifecycle flag.

verevon.constraints: Quarry's only callers today are the gateway and Model Plane, so protocol deprecation headers have almost no audience until the external API of F-t2-064 exists; deprecation belongs with that OpenAPI work. Image signing has no CI artifact to sign: Model Plane images are built through a host build script and compose (its compose header), and no workflow pushes Quarry or Model Plane images, so a publish pipeline, registry and key-management decision (Support Plane or infra) must come first; mcp-bridge is not a Quarry component, it is referenced from Model Plane docs and the model-gateway registry. Usefulness signal: ZDR must drop it (as implicit_feedback does under ZDR) and it may carry only ids and domains; Model Plane must not write Ingestion storage, so it needs a NATS event or a Quarry endpoint with a service principal (a new entry in the cross-plane token manifest and Control Plane registry checked by quarry-docs-contract.yml). Behavioural signals are asymmetric: ignored is weak evidence and silence is not approval (implicit_feedback.rs header), and failed is already known to Quarry.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the bundle. (a) Fold deprecation metadata into F-t2-064 as OpenAPI deprecated flags plus a CI route-coverage check, and add tower middleware only when an external audience exists. (b) Defer image signing until a registry publish pipeline exists, then sign in that pipeline; frame it as a deploy-pipeline item for infra, not a Quarry change. (c) Keep a much smaller usefulness signal: Model Plane emits used (cited) with Quarry request id and domain, Quarry aggregates per domain for its own search and answer ranking, and capability-core is not the consumer because it scores tools, not sources.
verevon.effortNote: As a bundle L: (a) S-M and absorbed by F-t2-064, (b) L because there is no image publish pipeline to attach signing to, (c) M including a cross-plane contract and a ranking consumer that does not exist yet.
verevon.verdictReason: Status absent is accurate, but the bundle rests on premises the code contradicts: no external API consumers for deprecation headers, no image publish pipeline to sign, and capability-core cannot consume a per-domain usefulness signal. Demote and split; (a) belongs to F-t2-064 and (c) is a smaller, differently placed item.

items.title: Agent scaling bets: child browser subagents and WebMCP page tools (site playbooks and MCP exposure are covered by F-t2-043 and F-t2-064)
items.summary: Four independent, later-stage bets: URL-pattern-bound site playbooks (guidance only, never permissions) injected into browser observations and learned from successful run receipts; child browser runs with narrower child grants (read-only class, capped concurrency) spawned by a parent run; browser.observe/act exposed as an MCP tool behind the same broker grants and approvals; and WebMCP page-tool discovery executed as sensitive-class actions with one-shot approval.
items.whyItMatters: Playbooks raise success on common SaaS UIs, subagents give parallel research, MCP exposure lets external agents use Verevon's governed browser, and WebMCP positions Quarry for sites that publish typed tools.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (sixteen SKILL.md playbooks with autoInject {keywords, url}; subagent profiles with isolated browser state) and Codex (CDP WebMCP.enable per frame with toolsAdded/Removed events)
others: Aside outbound-only relay with allowlisted remote operations
Codex CI109 signed browser-access attestation for cloud agents
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Playbooks 2 of 3 (common); remote drivers 2 of 3 (common); subagents 1 of 3 (unique); WebMCP 1 of 3 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Playbooks: registry keyed by URL pattern or keywords, injected into the next observation header and marked as guidance. Subagents: spawn(profile, task) gives a new session with its own browser binding and a tool set filtered by profile, results returned as text. WebMCP: enable the domain per frame, keep a per-tab tool registry, expose tools as webmcp:<host>:<tool> with per-site permission and review.

verevonToday.gap: Quarry supports parallel runs and any authorised device can drive sessions (cloud-native, no relay needed). No URL-bound skills (grep of Model Plane found none), no WebMCP handling in Quarry crates, and neither child-grant fan-out from execution-core nor MCP exposure of browser tools is evidenced; these were not verified in code.

items.approach: Model Plane: URL-bound skills injected into observations (seed a few top sites, learn more via procedure compile in browser_procedure.rs); child browser runs with child grants and a per-org concurrency cap; MCP tool wrapper over the same grants. Ingestion Plane: discover WebMCP tools in observations and execute them as sensitive-class actions with fenced descriptions. Schedule each separately.
items.risks: Stale playbook selectors; cost explosion from subagents (cap concurrency per org); external clients must never obtain grants outside the user's ACL; page-defined tools are untrusted input.

verevon.exactGap: Delegated subagents are shipped in Model Plane (nested agent loop, depth 1, per-run ceiling default 8 and hard cap 100, research fan-out) and the in-loop browser.observe and browser.act aliases exist behind a broker-validated grant, but delegated children are leaf-role and refused browser_agent and browser.act as risky, so there are no child browser runs. Missing: a read-only browser action class in broker grants (grant.go carries allowed actions only for sensitive scopes), any per-org live browser run cap (Quarry has only global lease pools), and any WebMCP handling (no code anywhere; the only mention is an outbound 'expose Verevon actions to in-browser agents' bridge in the root plan Verevon-ai-first-plan.md, the opposite direction to Quarry discovering page tools). External MCP exposure of browser tools is not in the gateway, whose mcp.rs only proxies the MCP-server registry.

reuse: run_delegated_child and the research fan-out dispatch (shipped) for spawning children and merging results
BrowserBroker Grant.ParentGrantID pattern for child grants that are strict subsets of the parent grant
execute_quarry_browser_mcp and the browser.observe alias for read-only observation by a child on a leased run
resolve_child_ceiling and the org ceiling hook for a per-org child cap

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: WebMCP descriptors discovered in a page are untrusted input and must be fenced, and their execution must go through a Quarry action with a fresh one-shot broker approval grant, never directly from the Model Plane. Child grants must be strict subsets of the parent (ParentGrantID shape) and may never widen the owner's ACL or a Space's authority; the leaf-role rule (agent.rs:1628-1665) must be relaxed only for a defined read-only browser class, not generally. The shared Chromium process means parallel child runs share one browser, and today a UI session (1280x800) and a Model Plane run (no viewport) already force relaunches that drop each other's pages, so that must be fixed before fan-out. ZDR inheritance by child runs was not verified (INF) and must be confirmed before browser children ship.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Follow the title: remove site playbooks (F-t2-043) and the MCP exposure wrapper (F-t2-064; the in-loop browser.observe and browser.act aliases already exist) from the summary and approach. For child browser runs: reuse run_delegated_child, add a read-only browser action class to BrowserBroker grants (F-t2-032) with a leaf-role exception limited to that class, add a per-org live-run cap in Quarry, and first make viewport page-scoped so concurrent runs stop relaunching Chromium. Keep WebMCP as a research spike only (the CDP WebMCP domain is experimental, INF) and do not schedule it until real sites publish tools.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for child browser runs, which are L because they depend on action classes (F-t2-032), a per-org cap and the viewport fix; WebMCP is a separate M spike.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is accurate: subagents and in-loop browser MCP aliases already exist, so the item should not read as greenfield, and child browser runs are specifically blocked by the leaf-role risky-tool rule and missing action classes. The summary and approach still describe playbooks and MCP exposure that the title assigns elsewhere, and WebMCP should be demoted to a spike.

items.title: Design spike only: drive the user's own signed-in Chrome through an attested extension backend, behind per-tab consent
items.summary: Only after the multi-backend work in R-t2-03-09: ship an MV3 extension with debugger permission and a relay to Quarry (native messaging or a hosted bridge) that registers a 'user_browser' BrowserBackend with isolated_egress=false and security_evidence=false. Allow it only for interactive (non-background) runs with explicit per-tab user consent, a visible indicator, and Quarry relaying and recording every action the Model proposes. || Write an ADR and prototype scope for an extension plus native-host bridge that lets the user's own Chrome/Edge profile act as a Quarry executor kind. To keep the Model-proposes/Quarry-executes rule, the extension would only run actions that Quarry has already validated against a BrowserBroker grant and would return receipts to Quarry; it must not take instructions from the Model Plane or the SPA directly. Do not start implementation until the connector-to-browser bridge and Quarry profile login hand-off have shipped.
items.whyItMatters: It is the only route to SSO-protected enterprise apps and the user's signed-in state without importing credentials, and it delivers the 'it uses my browser' experience that Codex offers. It is high value but conflicts with Verevon's governed-egress model, so it is a later, deliberate product decision. || Users want agents to use sites where they are already signed in, without re-authentication. It is an alternative to R-t2-10-01 for authenticated access, but it weakens the server-side containment that makes ZDR, egress proof and grants enforceable.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex native messaging host plus extension using chrome.debugger (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-010, SRC)
others: Codex browser plugin (Chrome extension plus Rust native messaging host bridged to the app server)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (codex), unique || 1 of 4 sources for the extension and native-host pattern (Codex only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: MV3 extension with the debugger permission attaches chrome.debugger to tabs the user shares; a native messaging host (or hosted WebSocket bridge) relays CDP commands from the agent service; the extension enforces per-tab consent and shows an indicator. || Merged items add: Extension to native host over stdin/stdout; native host to app server over a local WebSocket or named pipe; the manifest pins extension ids and required protocol versions with explicit update-required errors; tab-context assets are written in bounded chunks.

items.approach: Spike, not build: measure how much of the need is already met by the secret bridge (F-t2-024) and takeover login into scoped profiles, then decide in an ADR. If pursued, it is one more backend in the multi-backend abstraction (F-t2-059) with its own reduced capability set, because it gives up egress containment, SSRF guarantees and ZDR evidence. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-12] Frontend Plane: extension and consent UI. Ingestion Plane: 'user_browser' BrowserBackend with capability flags set false for containment and ZDR evidence so policy can refuse it for ZDR and background runs; the Model proposes and Quarry relays and records; the Model Plane approval grants (sensitive actions) still apply. Treat as a separate product decision with security review before any build. || [R-t2-10-08] Frontend Plane (extension, distribution) plus Ingestion Plane (a new executor kind registered with Quarry) plus Model Plane (BrowserBroker grant). Start with an ADR; a prototype would register the extension as a lease provider attested by a device key, with egress proof and ZDR weaker than remote Chromium and clearly labelled.
dependencies: Extension store review and enterprise policy deployment
F-t2-024 (secret bridge) and Quarry profile login hand-off, to measure how much of the need they already meet
items.risks: Loses egress containment and SSRF guarantees; ZDR evidence cannot be guaranteed; extension store review and enterprise rollout; prompt-injected pages act with the user's real sessions. || Exposes the user's full signed-in profile to agent actions; hard to audit; conflicts with Quarry executes and with ZDR/egress guarantees; extension permissions and store review burden.

verevon.exactGap: No extension, native host or user-browser executor exists (a repo search for chrome.debugger, nativeMessaging and manifest_version matches only a plan JSON); all browsing is a Quarry-leased chromiumoxide with one agent driver in AppState, and persisted profiles plus human takeover cover signed-in access. The product owner ruled on 2026-09-28 that the user's own Chrome and its logins are not driven and the 2026-10-01 parity audit records it as parked or ruled out. Quarry's fail-closed gate (require_isolated_agent_egress) refuses any agent driver without isolated_egress and security_evidence, so a user_browser backend flagged false on both would be refused unless that gate is redesigned.

verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not carry this as a build recommendation. Record it as parked by owner ruling (2026-09-28, restated 2026-10-01) and list what would have to change to reopen it: an owner decision, the multi-backend abstraction (F-t2-059; AppState holds a single agent_driver today), a redesigned fail-closed gate that distinguishes interactive consented runs from background runs, and an attested relay in which Quarry validates every action against a BrowserBroker grant before the extension executes it. verevon.verdictReason: Absent, so it cannot be dropped as shipped, but it contradicts the owner's recorded ruling and the fail-closed egress gate; it should be moved out of the recommendation set into a parked or decision-record note that only an explicit owner reversal reopens.
